canonical_transcript.content: Production can end up with all DB2 pool members held for many hours. The starvation report counts held members but cannot identify the long-lived worker that lazily acquired and retained one outside an explicit lease scope. Make the next starvation verdict identify the actual lazy-acquire call site without overwriting attribution for explicit begin/end scopes. Preserve the existing pool lifecycle, add regression tests when appropriate, and run relevant verification before finishing.

1:/* db2_pool.h: bounded DB2 (Postgres) connection pool.
2: *
3: * Decouples connection count (M) from thread count (N): instead of one libpq
4: * connection per live thread (the legacy db2_conn() model, which scales 1:1
5: * with threads and marches into Postgres max_connections), a fixed pool of M
6: * reusable connections is leased/returned at unit-of-work boundaries. See
7: * docs/proposals/pending/db2-connection-pool.md.
8: *
9: * This module is the raw bounded pool (lease/return/reset/reaper). The
10: * thread-local, re-entrant lease scoping that preserves db2_conn() semantics
11: * lives in db2_init.c (db2_lease_begin/_end, plus a lazy per-thread lease so the
12: * 668 db2_conn() call sites are unchanged). The pool is ALWAYS ON — db2_init()
13: * initializes it unconditionally; there is no opt-in flag and no per-thread
14: * fallback. WP-0's re-entrancy audit (zero cross-connection nesting) is what
15: * makes replacing the per-thread model outright safe.
16: */
17:#ifndef DEC_DB2_POOL_H
18:#define DEC_DB2_POOL_H 1
19:
20:/* The longest a lease may reasonably be held. The pool's reaper flags anything
21: * past this as stuck, and db_postgres.c bounds a statement by the same figure so
22: * the two cannot drift: a statement that outlived this would be reported stuck by
23: * a pool that had no way to stop it. Defined here because the pool owns the
24: * policy; db_postgres.c consumes it (header only — no link edge). */
25:#define DB2_POOL_HOLD_CEILING_MS 300000
26:
27:/* Exit status used when the pool proves unrecoverably starved and the process
28: * gives up so a restart policy can recover it. Distinct from a crash so an
29: * operator (and the entrypoint's exit reporter) can tell the two apart. */
30:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE 92
31:
32:/* Consecutive sweeps of total starvation before the process gives up on itself.
33: * At the 30s sweep interval this is ~2 minutes of EVERY member stuck with
34: * callers waiting — far beyond any real unit of work, and past the point where
35: * the ceiling (which is itself 5 minutes) has already been exceeded by all of
36: * them. Deliberately several sweeps rather than one: a single sweep that
37: * happens to catch every member mid-hand-off must not restart a healthy kb. */
38:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_SWEEPS 4
39:
40:#include <stddef.h>
41:
42:#ifdef __cplusplus
43:extern "C"
44:{
45:#endif
46:
47:   /* Hard upper bound on pool size (guards config). */
48:#define DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE 256
49:   /* Default lease wait when a caller passes <= 0. */
50:#define DB2_POOL_DEFAULT_LEASE_TIMEOUT_MS 30000
51:
52:   /* Open `size` connections to libpq_url and start the reaper. Returns 0 on
53:    * success, -1 on error (errbuf set). size is clamped to [1, DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE].
54:    * Idempotent: a second call with the same url is a no-op success. */
55:   int db2_pool_init(const char *libpq_url, int size, char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_len);
56:
57:   /* True once db2_pool_init has succeeded. */
58:   int db2_pool_active(void);
59:
60:   /* Lease one connection, blocking up to timeout_ms (<=0 -> default). Returns a
61:    * PGconn* (void*) owned by the caller until db2_pool_return, or NULL on
62:    * timeout/exhaustion (the caller must fail its unit of work cleanly, NOT
63:    * fall back to an unbounded wait). */
64:   void *db2_pool_lease(int timeout_ms);
65:
66:   /* Reset session state (ROLLBACK; RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION; DISCARD ALL)
67:    * and return the connection to the pool. On reset failure the member is
68:    * poisoned: closed and replaced with a fresh connection (rate-capped). NULL
69:    * is ignored. */
70:   void db2_pool_return(void *conn);
71:
72:   /* Unconditionally discard a leased member after transaction cleanup or
73:    * connection integrity failure. The stale handle is never made available to
74:    * another caller; the slot is reopened under the normal poison rate cap. */
75:   void db2_pool_discard(void *conn);
76:
77:   /* Drain + close all members; stop the reaper. After this db2_pool_active()
78:    * is false. */
79:   void db2_pool_shutdown(void);
80:
81:   /* Snapshot for metrics / `aimee workers`. Any out-param may be NULL.
82:    * `stuck` = leases observed held past the hold ceiling (a live thread that
83:    * missed lease_end; logged, not reclaimed — see db2_pool_reaper_sweep). */
84:   void db2_pool_stats(int *size, int *in_use, int *waiters, long *lease_grants,
85:                       long *lease_timeouts, long *stuck, long *poisoned);
86:
87:   /* Run one reaper sweep synchronously: logs + counts leases held past the
88:    * ceiling and returns that count. It does NOT reclaim — reclaiming a
89:    * still-leased connection a live thread may use would corrupt libpq;
90:    * reclaim-on-thread-death is the lease thread-local destructor's job
91:    * (db2_init.c). Production also runs an internal reaper thread. */
92:   int db2_pool_reaper_sweep(void);
93:
94:   /* Test seam: override connection open/close/reset (any NULL restores the real
95:    * libpq op) so unit tests exercise lease/return/poison without a Postgres
96:    * server. Not for production use. */
97:   void db2_pool_set_test_ops(void *(*open_fn)(const char *, char *, size_t),
98:                              void (*close_fn)(void *), int (*reset_fn)(void *));
99:
100:   /* Test seam: lower the stuck-lease ceiling so a sweep can flag in ms. */
101:   /* Record which db2_lease_begin call site holds `conn`, so a stuck lease is
102:    * reported as a code location rather than a member index. */
103:   void db2_pool_note_lease_site(void *conn, const char *site);
104:
105:   void db2_pool_set_test_ceiling_ms(int ceiling_ms);
106:
107:   /* Test seam for the unrecoverable-starvation policy. Production leaves this
108:    * NULL and the process exits with DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE; a test installs
109:    * a recorder so the decision is observable without killing the runner.
110:    * Passing NULL restores the production behaviour. */
111:   void db2_pool_set_test_starved_action(void (*action)(const char *reason));
112:
113:#ifdef __cplusplus
114:}
115:#endif
116:
117:#endif /* DEC_DB2_POOL_H */

1:/* db2_pool.h: bounded DB2 (Postgres) connection pool.
2: *
3: * Decouples connection count (M) from thread count (N): instead of one libpq
4: * connection per live thread (the legacy db2_conn() model, which scales 1:1
5: * with threads and marches into Postgres max_connections), a fixed pool of M
6: * reusable connections is leased/returned at unit-of-work boundaries. See
7: * docs/proposals/pending/db2-connection-pool.md.
8: *
9: * This module is the raw bounded pool (lease/return/reset/reaper). The
10: * thread-local, re-entrant lease scoping that preserves db2_conn() semantics
11: * lives in db2_init.c (db2_lease_begin/_end, plus a lazy per-thread lease so the
12: * 668 db2_conn() call sites are unchanged). The pool is ALWAYS ON — db2_init()
13: * initializes it unconditionally; there is no opt-in flag and no per-thread
14: * fallback. WP-0's re-entrancy audit (zero cross-connection nesting) is what
15: * makes replacing the per-thread model outright safe.
16: */
17:#ifndef DEC_DB2_POOL_H
18:#define DEC_DB2_POOL_H 1
19:
20:/* The longest a lease may reasonably be held. The pool's reaper flags anything
21: * past this as stuck, and db_postgres.c bounds a statement by the same figure so
22: * the two cannot drift: a statement that outlived this would be reported stuck by
23: * a pool that had no way to stop it. Defined here because the pool owns the
24: * policy; db_postgres.c consumes it (header only — no link edge). */
25:#define DB2_POOL_HOLD_CEILING_MS 300000
26:
27:/* Exit status used when the pool proves unrecoverably starved and the process
28: * gives up so a restart policy can recover it. Distinct from a crash so an
29: * operator (and the entrypoint's exit reporter) can tell the two apart. */
30:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE 92
31:
32:/* Consecutive sweeps of total starvation before the process gives up on itself.
33: * At the 30s sweep interval this is ~2 minutes of EVERY member stuck with
34: * callers waiting — far beyond any real unit of work, and past the point where
35: * the ceiling (which is itself 5 minutes) has already been exceeded by all of
36: * them. Deliberately several sweeps rather than one: a single sweep that
37: * happens to catch every member mid-hand-off must not restart a healthy kb. */
38:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_SWEEPS 4
39:
40:#include <stddef.h>
41:
42:#ifdef __cplusplus
43:extern "C"
44:{
45:#endif
46:
47:   /* Hard upper bound on pool size (guards config). */
48:#define DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE 256
49:   /* Default lease wait when a caller passes <= 0. */
50:#define DB2_POOL_DEFAULT_LEASE_TIMEOUT_MS 30000
51:
52:   /* Open `size` connections to libpq_url and start the reaper. Returns 0 on
53:    * success, -1 on error (errbuf set). size is clamped to [1, DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE].
54:    * Idempotent: a second call with the same url is a no-op success. */
55:   int db2_pool_init(const char *libpq_url, int size, char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_len);
56:
57:   /* True once db2_pool_init has succeeded. */
58:   int db2_pool_active(void);
59:
60:   /* Lease one connection, blocking up to timeout_ms (<=0 -> default). Returns a
61:    * PGconn* (void*) owned by the caller until db2_pool_return, or NULL on
62:    * timeout/exhaustion (the caller must fail its unit of work cleanly, NOT
63:    * fall back to an unbounded wait). */
64:   void *db2_pool_lease(int timeout_ms);
65:
66:   /* Reset session state (ROLLBACK; RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION; DISCARD ALL)
67:    * and return the connection to the pool. On reset failure the member is
68:    * poisoned: closed and replaced with a fresh connection (rate-capped). NULL
69:    * is ignored. */
70:   void db2_pool_return(void *conn);
71:
72:   /* Unconditionally discard a leased member after transaction cleanup or
73:    * connection integrity failure. The stale handle is never made available to
74:    * another caller; the slot is reopened under the normal poison rate cap. */
75:   void db2_pool_discard(void *conn);
76:
77:   /* Drain + close all members; stop the reaper. After this db2_pool_active()
78:    * is false. */
79:   void db2_pool_shutdown(void);
80:
81:   /* Snapshot for metrics / `aimee workers`. Any out-param may be NULL.
82:    * `stuck` = leases observed held past the hold ceiling (a live thread that
83:    * missed lease_end; logged, not reclaimed — see db2_pool_reaper_sweep). */
84:   void db2_pool_stats(int *size, int *in_use, int *waiters, long *lease_grants,
85:                       long *lease_timeouts, long *stuck, long *poisoned);
86:
87:   /* Run one reaper sweep synchronously: logs + counts leases held past the
88:    * ceiling and returns that count. It does NOT reclaim — reclaiming a
89:    * still-leased connection a live thread may use would corrupt libpq;
90:    * reclaim-on-thread-death is the lease thread-local destructor's job
91:    * (db2_init.c). Production also runs an internal reaper thread. */
92:   int db2_pool_reaper_sweep(void);
93:
94:   /* Test seam: override connection open/close/reset (any NULL restores the real
95:    * libpq op) so unit tests exercise lease/return/poison without a Postgres
96:    * server. Not for production use. */
97:   void db2_pool_set_test_ops(void *(*open_fn)(const char *, char *, size_t),
98:                              void (*close_fn)(void *), int (*reset_fn)(void *));
99:
100:   /* Test seam: lower the stuck-lease ceiling so a sweep can flag in ms. */
101:   /* Record which db2_lease_begin call site holds `conn`, so a stuck lease is
102:    * reported as a code location rather than a member index. */
103:   void db2_pool_note_lease_site(void *conn, const char *site);
104:
105:   void db2_pool_set_test_ceiling_ms(int ceiling_ms);
106:
107:   /* Test seam for the unrecoverable-starvation policy. Production leaves this
108:    * NULL and the process exits with DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE; a test installs
109:    * a recorder so the decision is observable without killing the runner.
110:    * Passing NULL restores the production behaviour. */
111:   void db2_pool_set_test_starved_action(void (*action)(const char *reason));
112:
113:#ifdef __cplusplus
114:}
115:#endif
116:
117:#endif /* DEC_DB2_POOL_H */

1:#!/bin/sh
2:# git-askpass-forge.sh — the GIT_ASKPASS shim the forge-credential broker
3:# installs (workspace-resource-plane §4). git invokes GIT_ASKPASS with the
4:# username/password prompt text and uses the program's stdout as the answer.
5:#
6:# The brokered short-lived forge token is passed to the child process in the
7:# GH_TOKEN environment variable (see forge_cred_build_env), NEVER on the command
8:# line or on disk. This shim echoes it as the password (and, for the username
9:# prompt, the conventional "x-access-token", which token-auth forges accept; the
10:# repo URL may also carry the username). Nothing is logged.
11:case "$1" in
12:*[Uu]sername*) echo "x-access-token" ;;
13:*) printf '%s\n' "$GH_TOKEN" ;;
14:esac

6:/* git_cred_inject — assemble the execve() environment for a webchat user's git
7: * operation, injecting their HTTPS forge token from the sealed vault (webchat-git
8: * WP-C). The token is read autonomously (server wrap) from the `webuser:`
9: * principal's vault and crosses ONLY in the git child's environment (GH_TOKEN) +
10: * a GIT_ASKPASS shim — never on disk, never on the command line, never logged,
11: * vault-only at rest.
12: *
13: * Cross-tenant safety: the git child runs as the owning user's own OS UID
14: * (WP-I), and the kernel restricts /proc/<pid>/environ to that UID, so another
15: * webuser cannot read the token from the environment. Per-principal isolation +
16: * vault-at-rest is the security boundary.
17: *
18: * SSH-key injection (in-memory ssh-agent) is WP-C2. */
19:
20:/* Build a NULL-terminated envp for an execve() of a git command, with the HTTPS
21: * forge token resolved vault-first and injected via GH_TOKEN + the GIT_ASKPASS
22: * shim (GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0), plus SSH_AUTH_SOCK when a vaulted key is loaded.
23: * This is the ONE credential-resolution policy every git network op routes
24: * through, so the precedence can never drift between call sites.
25: *
26: * Token precedence (first hit wins):
27: *   1. preferred_token — a live caller-supplied token that must win: an inline
28: *      clone token, or the in-memory workspace broker token (§4). NULL = none.
29: *   2. per-host vault  — git_host_cred for the repo's remote HOST, resolved from
30: *      `remote_url` (if given) else from the `origin` remote of `repo_dir`. This
31: *      is the built-in server vault (server principal, server-wrap), keyed by
32: *      host so one server can talk to many forges (github/gitlab/gitea/...).
33: *   3. webuser vault   — the `principal`'s own vaulted personal forge token.
34: *   4. server identity — a GitHub App installation token, else a server-Vault token.
35: * The `principal`'s vaulted SSH key is also loaded into the in-memory ssh-agent
36: * (SSH_AUTH_SOCK) when present, independent of the token above.
37: *
38: * Any of principal/remote_url/repo_dir/preferred_token may be NULL. `repo_dir` is
39: * consulted only when a host token is needed and `remote_url` is NULL — a single
40: * local `git config --get remote.origin.url` (no network, no creds). Returns a
41: * malloc'd array (free with git_cred_inject_free_env), or NULL when no credential
42: * of any kind is available (caller falls back to ambient creds) or on error.
43: *
44: * `out_token_fd` selects how an HTTPS token reaches git:
45: *   - non-NULL  → FD MODE. The token is written to a CLOEXEC memfd (anonymous,
46: *     never a named path) whose fd is returned in *out_token_fd, and the env
47: *     carries AIMEE_GIT_TOKEN_FD=GIT_CRED_TOKEN_TARGET_FD (a number, not the
48: *     secret) instead of GH_TOKEN. The caller must run git with
49: *     safe_exec_capture_cwd_env_fd_timeout(inherit_fd=*out_token_fd,
50: *     target_fd=GIT_CRED_TOKEN_TARGET_FD) and close *out_token_fd afterwards. The
51: *     token then never appears in the child's /proc/<pid>/environ. *out_token_fd
52: *     is set to -1 when there is no HTTPS token (ssh-only / no creds).
53: *   - NULL      → LEGACY ENV MODE. The token is injected as GH_TOKEN in the env
54: *     (used by the long-lived editor path until it migrates). */
55:#define GIT_CRED_TOKEN_TARGET_FD 21 /* fd number the askpass reads in the git child */
56:char **git_cred_inject_build_env_for_repo(const char *principal, const char *remote_url,
57:                                          const char *repo_dir, const char *preferred_token,
58:                                          char *const *parent_environ, int *out_token_fd);
59:
60:/* Back-compat shim: build the env for `principal` with no repo context — webuser
61: * vault → server identity → ssh-agent (no per-host token). Equivalent to
62: * git_cred_inject_build_env_for_repo(principal, NULL, NULL, NULL, parent). */
63:char **git_cred_inject_build_env(const char *principal, char *const *parent_environ);
64:
65:/* Resolve just the HTTPS token (no env assembly) under the SAME precedence as
66: * the env builders above: preferred → per-host vault → principal vault → server
67: * identity. For the one caller that needs the raw token rather than an exec env
68: * — the in-process GitHub REST open-PR, which puts it in an Authorization header
69: * (git_pr_api.c). Writes the token to `out` and returns 1, or 0 (no token, out
70: * empty). Centralizing here keeps the precedence from drifting and keeps the
71: * credential ladder out of downstream callers. */
72:int git_cred_inject_resolve_token(const char *principal, const char *remote_url,
73:                                  const char *repo_dir, const char *preferred_token, char *out,
74:                                  size_t cap);
75:
76:/* 1 if aimee-server has git configured AT ALL: a per-host vault entry (any host),
77: * or its own forge identity. Resolves nothing and returns no token — the per-host
78: * store is asked only for host NAMES.
79: *
80: * This is the predicate the require_aimee_git restriction hangs off (operator
81: * ruling 2026-07-15): "the restriction applies only if aimee-server has a
82: * configured git". That is a property of the SERVER, not of a checkout, and asking
83: * it per-repo made the rule fire or stand down depending on the ambient cwd of the
84: * calling thread — the same command allowed from one directory and refused from
85: * another (observed live on .254: DENY in a wfe worktree, allow from the daemon's
86: * cwd twelve seconds later).
87: *
88: * The rule it gates: "do not shell out to git/gh — use aimee's git_* tools, which
89: * run on aimee-server". With no credential anywhere, aimee's tools cannot do git
90: * either, so blocking the shell would remove the only route rather than redirect
91: * it. No aimee route -> no restriction. */
92:int git_cred_forge_configured(void);
93:
94:/* Free an envp from git_cred_inject_build_env (zeroes the GH_TOKEN entry first). */
95:void git_cred_inject_free_env(char **envp);
96:
97:#endif /* GIT_CRED_INJECT_H */

1:#!/bin/sh
2:# git-askpass-forge.sh — the GIT_ASKPASS shim the forge-credential broker
3:# installs (workspace-resource-plane §4). git invokes GIT_ASKPASS with the
4:# username/password prompt text and uses the program's stdout as the answer.
5:#
6:# The brokered short-lived forge token is passed to the child process in the
7:# GH_TOKEN environment variable (see forge_cred_build_env), NEVER on the command
8:# line or on disk. This shim echoes it as the password (and, for the username
9:# prompt, the conventional "x-access-token", which token-auth forges accept; the
10:# repo URL may also carry the username). Nothing is logged.
11:case "$1" in
12:*[Uu]sername*) echo "x-access-token" ;;
13:*) printf '%s\n' "$GH_TOKEN" ;;

1:/* db2_pool.h: bounded DB2 (Postgres) connection pool.
2: *
3: * Decouples connection count (M) from thread count (N): instead of one libpq
4: * connection per live thread (the legacy db2_conn() model, which scales 1:1
5: * with threads and marches into Postgres max_connections), a fixed pool of M
6: * reusable connections is leased/returned at unit-of-work boundaries. See
7: * docs/proposals/pending/db2-connection-pool.md.
8: *
9: * This module is the raw bounded pool (lease/return/reset/reaper). The
10: * thread-local, re-entrant lease scoping that preserves db2_conn() semantics
11: * lives in db2_init.c (db2_lease_begin/_end, plus a lazy per-thread lease so the
12: * 668 db2_conn() call sites are unchanged). The pool is ALWAYS ON — db2_init()
13: * initializes it unconditionally; there is no opt-in flag and no per-thread
14: * fallback. WP-0's re-entrancy audit (zero cross-connection nesting) is what
15: * makes replacing the per-thread model outright safe.
16: */
17:#ifndef DEC_DB2_POOL_H
18:#define DEC_DB2_POOL_H 1
19:
20:/* The longest a lease may reasonably be held. The pool's reaper flags anything
21: * past this as stuck, and db_postgres.c bounds a statement by the same figure so
22: * the two cannot drift: a statement that outlived this would be reported stuck by
23: * a pool that had no way to stop it. Defined here because the pool owns the
24: * policy; db_postgres.c consumes it (header only — no link edge). */
25:#define DB2_POOL_HOLD_CEILING_MS 300000
26:
27:/* Exit status used when the pool proves unrecoverably starved and the process
28: * gives up so a restart policy can recover it. Distinct from a crash so an
29: * operator (and the entrypoint's exit reporter) can tell the two apart. */
30:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE 92
31:
32:/* Consecutive sweeps of total starvation before the process gives up on itself.
33: * At the 30s sweep interval this is ~2 minutes of EVERY member stuck with
34: * callers waiting — far beyond any real unit of work, and past the point where
35: * the ceiling (which is itself 5 minutes) has already been exceeded by all of
36: * them. Deliberately several sweeps rather than one: a single sweep that
37: * happens to catch every member mid-hand-off must not restart a healthy kb. */
38:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_SWEEPS 4
39:
40:#include <stddef.h>
41:
42:#ifdef __cplusplus
43:extern "C"
44:{
45:#endif
46:
47:   /* Hard upper bound on pool size (guards config). */
48:#define DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE 256
49:   /* Default lease wait when a caller passes <= 0. */
50:#define DB2_POOL_DEFAULT_LEASE_TIMEOUT_MS 30000
51:
52:   /* Open `size` connections to libpq_url and start the reaper. Returns 0 on
53:    * success, -1 on error (errbuf set). size is clamped to [1, DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE].
54:    * Idempotent: a second call with the same url is a no-op success. */
55:   int db2_pool_init(const char *libpq_url, int size, char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_len);
56:
57:   /* True once db2_pool_init has succeeded. */
58:   int db2_pool_active(void);
59:
60:   /* Lease one connection, blocking up to timeout_ms (<=0 -> default). Returns a
61:    * PGconn* (void*) owned by the caller until db2_pool_return, or NULL on
62:    * timeout/exhaustion (the caller must fail its unit of work cleanly, NOT
63:    * fall back to an unbounded wait). */
64:   void *db2_pool_lease(int timeout_ms);
65:

1:/* db2_pool.h: bounded DB2 (Postgres) connection pool.
2: *
3: * Decouples connection count (M) from thread count (N): instead of one libpq
4: * connection per live thread (the legacy db2_conn() model, which scales 1:1
5: * with threads and marches into Postgres max_connections), a fixed pool of M
6: * reusable connections is leased/returned at unit-of-work boundaries. See
7: * docs/proposals/pending/db2-connection-pool.md.
8: *
9: * This module is the raw bounded pool (lease/return/reset/reaper). The
10: * thread-local, re-entrant lease scoping that preserves db2_conn() semantics
11: * lives in db2_init.c (db2_lease_begin/_end, plus a lazy per-thread lease so the
12: * 668 db2_conn() call sites are unchanged). The pool is ALWAYS ON — db2_init()
13: * initializes it unconditionally; there is no opt-in flag and no per-thread
14: * fallback. WP-0's re-entrancy audit (zero cross-connection nesting) is what
15: * makes replacing the per-thread model outright safe.
16: */
17:#ifndef DEC_DB2_POOL_H
18:#define DEC_DB2_POOL_H 1

20:/* The longest a lease may reasonably be held. The pool's reaper flags anything
21: * past this as stuck, and db_postgres.c bounds a statement by the same figure so
22: * the two cannot drift: a statement that outlived this would be reported stuck by
23: * a pool that had no way to stop it. Defined here because the pool owns the
24: * policy; db_postgres.c consumes it (header only — no link edge). */
25:#define DB2_POOL_HOLD_CEILING_MS 300000
26:

29: * operator (and the entrypoint's exit reporter) can tell the two apart. */
30:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE 92
31:
32:/* Consecutive sweeps of total starvation before the process gives up on itself.
33: * At the 30s sweep interval this is ~2 minutes of EVERY member stuck with
34: * callers waiting — far beyond any real unit of work, and past the point where
35: * the ceiling (which is itself 5 minutes) has already been exceeded by all of
36: * them. Deliberately several sweeps rather than one: a single sweep that
37: * happens to catch every member mid-hand-off must not restart a healthy kb. */

44:{

1:/* db2_pool.h: bounded DB2 (Postgres) connection pool.
2: *
3: * Decouples connection count (M) from thread count (N): instead of one libpq
4: * connection per live thread (the legacy db2_conn() model, which scales 1:1
5: * with threads and marches into Postgres max_connections), a fixed pool of M
6: * reusable connections is leased/returned at unit-of-work boundaries. See
7: * docs/proposals/pending/db2-connection-pool.md.
8: *
9: * This module is the raw bounded pool (lease/return/reset/reaper). The
10: * thread-local, re-entrant lease scoping that preserves db2_conn() semantics
11: * lives in db2_init.c (db2_lease_begin/_end, plus a lazy per-thread lease so the
12: * 668 db2_conn() call sites are unchanged). The pool is ALWAYS ON — db2_init()
13: * initializes it unconditionally; there is no opt-in flag and no per-thread
14: * fallback. WP-0's re-entrancy audit (zero cross-connection nesting) is what
15: * makes replacing the per-thread model outright safe.
16: */
17:#ifndef DEC_DB2_POOL_H
18:#define DEC_DB2_POOL_H 1
19:
20:/* The longest a lease may reasonably be held. The pool's reaper flags anything
21: * past this as stuck, and db_postgres.c bounds a statement by the same figure so
22: * the two cannot drift: a statement that outlived this would be reported stuck by
23: * a pool that had no way to stop it. Defined here because the pool owns the
24: * policy; db_postgres.c consumes it (header only — no link edge). */
25:#define DB2_POOL_HOLD_CEILING_MS 300000
26:
27:/* Exit status used when the pool proves unrecoverably starved and the process
28: * gives up so a restart policy can recover it. Distinct from a crash so an
29: * operator (and the entrypoint's exit reporter) can tell the two apart. */
30:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE 92
31:
32:/* Consecutive sweeps of total starvation before the process gives up on itself.
33: * At the 30s sweep interval this is ~2 minutes of EVERY member stuck with
34: * callers waiting — far beyond any real unit of work, and past the point where
35: * the ceiling (which is itself 5 minutes) has already been exceeded by all of
36: * them. Deliberately several sweeps rather than one: a single sweep that
37: * happens to catch every member mid-hand-off must not restart a healthy kb. */
38:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_SWEEPS 4

40:#include <stddef.h>
41:
42:#ifdef __cplusplus
43:extern "C"
44:{
45:#endif

47:   /* Hard upper bound on pool size (guards config). */
48:#define DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE 256
49:   /* Default lease wait when a caller passes <= 0. */
50:#define DB2_POOL_DEFAULT_LEASE_TIMEOUT_MS 30000
51:
52:   /* Open `size` connections to libpq_url and start the reaper. Returns 0 on
53:    * success, -1 on error (errbuf set). size is clamped to [1, DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE].
54:    * Idempotent: a second call with the same url is a no-op success. */
55:   int db2_pool_init(const char *libpq_url, int size, char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_len);
56:
57:   /* True once db2_pool_init has succeeded. */
58:   int db2_pool_active(void);

60:   /* Lease one connection, blocking up to timeout_ms (<=0 -> default). Returns a
61:    * PGconn* (void*) owned by the caller until db2_pool_return, or NULL on
62:    * timeout/exhaustion (the caller must fail its unit of work cleanly, NOT
63:    * fall back to an unbounded wait). */
64:   void *db2_pool_lease(int timeout_ms);

66:   /* Reset session state (ROLLBACK; RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION; DISCARD ALL)

69:    * is ignored. */

75:   void db2_pool_discard(void *conn);

77:   /* Drain + close all members; stop the reaper. After this db2_pool_active()

84:   void db2_pool_stats(int *size, int *in_use, int *waiters, long *lease_grants,

1:/* db2_pool.h: bounded DB2 (Postgres) connection pool.
2: *
3: * Decouples connection count (M) from thread count (N): instead of one libpq
4: * connection per live thread (the legacy db2_conn() model, which scales 1:1
5: * with threads and marches into Postgres max_connections), a fixed pool of M
6: * reusable connections is leased/returned at unit-of-work boundaries. See
7: * docs/proposals/pending/db2-connection-pool.md.
8: *
9: * This module is the raw bounded pool (lease/return/reset/reaper). The
10: * thread-local, re-entrant lease scoping that preserves db2_conn() semantics
11: * lives in db2_init.c (db2_lease_begin/_end, plus a lazy per-thread lease so the
12: * 668 db2_conn() call sites are unchanged). The pool is ALWAYS ON — db2_init()
13: * initializes it unconditionally; there is no opt-in flag and no per-thread
14: * fallback. WP-0's re-entrancy audit (zero cross-connection nesting) is what
15: * makes replacing the per-thread model outright safe.
16: */
17:#ifndef DEC_DB2_POOL_H
18:#define DEC_DB2_POOL_H 1
19:
20:/* The longest a lease may reasonably be held. The pool's reaper flags anything
21: * past this as stuck, and db_postgres.c bounds a statement by the same figure so
22: * the two cannot drift: a statement that outlived this would be reported stuck by
23: * a pool that had no way to stop it. Defined here because the pool owns the
24: * policy; db_postgres.c consumes it (header only — no link edge). */
25:#define DB2_POOL_HOLD_CEILING_MS 300000
26:
27:/* Exit status used when the pool proves unrecoverably starved and the process
28: * gives up so a restart policy can recover it. Distinct from a crash so an
29: * operator (and the entrypoint's exit reporter) can tell the two apart. */
30:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE 92
31:
32:/* Consecutive sweeps of total starvation before the process gives up on itself.
33: * At the 30s sweep interval this is ~2 minutes of EVERY member stuck with
34: * callers waiting — far beyond any real unit of work, and past the point where
35: * the ceiling (which is itself 5 minutes) has already been exceeded by all of
36: * them. Deliberately several sweeps rather than one: a single sweep that
37: * happens to catch every member mid-hand-off must not restart a healthy kb. */
38:#define DB2_POOL_STARVED_SWEEPS 4
39:
40:#include <stddef.h>
41:
42:#ifdef __cplusplus
43:extern "C"
44:{
45:#endif
46:
47:   /* Hard upper bound on pool size (guards config). */
48:#define DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE 256
49:   /* Default lease wait when a caller passes <= 0. */
50:#define DB2_POOL_DEFAULT_LEASE_TIMEOUT_MS 30000
51:
52:   /* Open `size` connections to libpq_url and start the reaper. Returns 0 on
53:    * success, -1 on error (errbuf set). size is clamped to [1, DB2_POOL_MAX_SIZE].
54:    * Idempotent: a second call with the same url is a no-op success. */
55:   int db2_pool_init(const char *libpq_url, int size, char *errbuf, size_t errbuf_len);
56:
57:   /* True once db2_pool_init has succeeded. */
58:   int db2_pool_active(void);
59:
60:   /* Lease one connection, blocking up to timeout_ms (<=0 -> default). Returns a
61:    * PGconn* (void*) owned by the caller until db2_pool_return, or NULL on
62:    * timeout/exhaustion (the caller must fail its unit of work cleanly, NOT
63:    * fall back to an unbounded wait). */
64:   void *db2_pool_lease(int timeout_ms);
65:
66:   /* Reset session state (ROLLBACK; RESET SESSION AUTHORIZATION; DISCARD ALL)
67:    * and return the connection to the pool. On reset failure the member is
68:    * poisoned: closed and replaced with a fresh connection (rate-capped). NULL
69:    * is ignored. */
70:   void db2_pool_return(void *conn);
71:
72:   /* Unconditionally discard a leased member after transaction cleanup or
73:    * connection integrity failure. The stale handle is never made available to
74:    * another caller; the slot is reopened under the normal poison rate cap. */
75:   void db2_pool_discard(void *conn);
76:
77:   /* Drain + close all members; stop the reaper. After this db2_pool_active()
78:    * is false. */
79:   void db2_pool_shutdown(void);
80:
81:   /* Snapshot for metrics / `aimee workers`. Any out-param may be NULL.
82:    * `stuck` = leases observed held past the hold ceiling (a live thread that
83:    * missed lease_end; logged, not reclaimed — see db2_pool_reaper_sweep). */
84:   void db2_pool_stats(int *size, int *in_use, int *waiters, long *lease_grants,
85:                       long *lease_timeouts, long *stuck, long *poisoned);
86:
87:   /* Run one reaper sweep synchronously: logs + counts leases held past the
88:    * ceiling and returns that count. It does NOT reclaim — reclaiming a
89:    * still-leased connection a live thread may use would corrupt libpq;
90:    * reclaim-on-thread-death is the lease thread-local destructor's job
91:    * (db2_init.c). Production also runs an internal reaper thread. */
92:   int db2_pool_reaper_sweep(void);
93:
94:   /* Test seam: override connection open/close/reset (any NULL restores the real
95:    * libpq op) so unit tests exercise lease/return/poison without a Postgres
96:    * server. Not for production use. */
97:   void db2_pool_set_test_ops(void *(*open_fn)(const char *, char *, size_t),
98:                              void (*close_fn)(void *), int (*reset_fn)(void *));
99:
100:   /* Test seam: lower the stuck-lease ceiling so a sweep can flag in ms. */
101:   /* Record which db2_lease_begin call site holds `conn`, so a stuck lease is
102:    * reported as a code location rather than a member index. */
103:   void db2_pool_note_lease_site(void *conn, const char *site);
104:
105:   void db2_pool_set_test_ceiling_ms(int ceiling_ms);
106:
107:   /* Test seam for the unrecoverable-starvation policy. Production leaves this
108:    * NULL and the process exits with DB2_POOL_STARVED_EXIT_CODE; a test installs
109:    * a recorder so the decision is observable without killing the runner.
110:    * Passing NULL restores the production behaviour. */
111:   void db2_pool_set_test_starved_action(void (*action)(const char *reason));
112:
113:#ifdef __cplusplus
114:}
115:#endif
116:
117:#endif /* DEC_DB2_POOL_H */

5: * domain functions declared by DB2 subsystem headers as they land.

9: * all subsystem state are private to src/db2/.

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:296:{"content":"## What aimee-server is\n\n`aimee-server` is a single C11 process that owns **DB1** (local SQLite), runs the\nbounded compute pool, routes delegates, serves the lifecycle hooks, and exposes\nthe public HTTP `/v1` surface (its only client transport). The thin clients\n(`aimee`, `aimee-webchat`) hold no database; they reach this process over `/v1`\n(local `aimee-http.sock` or remote TCP) and forward typed requests. The expensive\nstate (open DB handles, a\nwarm KB connection, the worker pool) lives here, in a warm long-running process,\nwhich is what keeps CLI startup under 10 ms and a pre-tool hook check around 1 ms.\n\nIt links `-lsqlite3` (plus `-lssl`/`-lcrypto`/`-lpam`) and is built with\n`-DAIMEE_DB2_DISABLED`: it **never** links libpq and holds no DB2 SQL. All\nknowledge operations go through the typed **KB client** (`kb_client*.c`) to\n`aimee-kb`. The storage boundary is compile-enforced (`make check-linking`,\n`readelf` symbol checks).","doc_id":"02b6b1ef52293ff0b785736e","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:340:{"content":"## 2. Process topology\n\naimee ships as **four primary artifacts** plus one optional gateway. Each is a\nseparate OS process with a distinct responsibility and a distinct linkage\nprofile (see §5).\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph User[\"User surface\"]\n        Tool[\"AI coding tool<br/>Claude Code / Gemini / Codex / Vibe / Copilot\"]\n        Browser[\"Browser\"]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Local[\"Local machine (same-user trust zone)\"]\n        CLI[\"aimee<br/>thin CLI + MCP serve<br/>(DB-free)\"]\n        WC[\"aimee-webchat<br/>Go browser service<br/>(DB-free)\"]\n        SRV[\"aimee-server<br/>DB1 owner · compute pool<br/>· RPC + HTTP /v1\"]\n        KB[\"aimee-kb<br/>DB2 owner · local/shared KB<br/>· pgvector · ingest/curator\"]\n        GW[\"aimee-gateway<br/>(optional) ambient presence\"]\n        DB1[(\"DB1<br/>SQLite\")]\n        DB2[(\"DB2<br/>Postgres + pgvector<br/>local or shared\")]\n    end\n\n    subgraph External[\"Untrusted zone\"]\n        Providers[\"Model providers<br/>OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Ollama\"]\n    end\n\n    Tool -->|hooks: stdin/stdout| CLI\n    Tool -->|MCP: stdio JSON-RPC| CLI\n    Browser -->|HTTPS + PAM| WC\n    CLI -->|/v1 HTTP<br/>UDS or TCP| SRV\n    WC -->|/v1 HTTP<br/>UDS or TCP| SRV\n    GW -.->|/v1 HTTP| SRV\n    SRV -->|typed KB /v1<br/>HTTP :8741| KB\n    SRV --> DB1\n    KB --> DB2\n    SRV -->|delegate HTTPS| Providers\n    KB -.->|embeddings / synthesis<br/>sidecars| Providers\n```\n\n| Artifact | Language | Owns | Links | Startup |\n|----------|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| `aimee` | C11 | nothing (thin client) | `-lpthread` only, **no** SQLite, **no** libpq | < 10 ms |\n| `aimee-webchat` | Go | nothing (thin client) | pure Go (PAM via cgo) | fast |\n| `aimee-server` | C11 | Local DB1 (SQLite), sessions, compute pool, delegate routing, hooks, MCP dispatch, HTTP /v1 | `-lsqlite3`, **never** libpq | persistent |\n| `aimee-kb` | C11 | DB2 (Postgres + pgvector), memory inference, embeddings, code index, ingest/curator; local or shared by deployment | `-lpq`, **never** SQLite | persistent |","doc_id":"031b9366a4728a5d373df352","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:353:{"content":"## Background curator finding\n\nThe current curator does not meet the retention rule:\n\n- it is default-off yet checks interval rather than enabled state internally;\n- agent-runtime and trigger-scheduler hooks can run it concurrently despite non-idempotent state;\n- an async server wrapper has no live caller;\n- it scans only global skills and misses project scope;\n- filename-prefix grouping and whitespace overlap are not reliable semantic evidence;\n- `use_count` observes injection, not actual activation or outcome;\n- protected, pinned, bundled, and user skills can appear in emitted clusters;\n- the promised snapshot is a TODO and `snapshot_path` is unused;\n- its DB1 maintenance plan has no production consumer, can silently truncate invalid JSON, ignores\n  persistence errors, and reports unreliable metrics;\n- tests exercise the island itself, not a supported user journey.","doc_id":"0345aea6c828eb8f58b5a35d","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:363:{"content":"## Cross-cutting items not yet tracked\n\nThe following are real gaps that are not tracked anywhere yet. Each deserves an\nowner when someone is ready to pick it up.\n\n- **Developer onboarding:** as external services accumulate (DB2 with\n  pgvector, Python embedder sidecar, LLM endpoint for curator), the\n  \"fresh-Debian to green-test-suite\" story stops fitting in anyone's\n  head. A `setup.sh` that handles all of it is worth a week of effort\n  and has no technical blocker.\n- **Standing LoCoMo / LongMemEval cadence:** too many acceptance\n  criteria cite \"within ±0.005 of baseline,\" but the benchmarks don't\n  run on a cadence. Either put them on nightly/weekly CI (with a\n  retention policy for the artefacts) or stop citing parity\n  criteria that nobody measures.\n- **Proposal-supersession hygiene rule:** the PR that supersedes a\n  proposal should move the old one (to `rejected/`, `deferred/`, or\n  wherever it belongs) **in the same commit**. Drift like the\n  pluggable-db proposal sitting in `pending/` after being deleted by\n  its successor is how `pending/` becomes stale signal. The stacks run the\n`aimee-llm` inference gateway (embeddings, reranking, and synthesis) as a service,\nwhich downloads its cpu-tier models on first boot, so embedding and reranking work\nwith nothing external. The tier is chosen by `AIMEE_LLM_TIER`: `cpu` serves\nQwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 1024 dims; the GPU tiers (`small` 16 GB, `mid` 24 GB,\n`large` 32 GB) serve Qwen3-Embedding-4B at 2560 dims.\nTo run a standalone embedder or curator LLM instead, use\nthe `curator-llm` compose profile. Backends and tiers:\n[KB_LLM_BACKENDS.md](docs/KB_LLM_BACKENDS.md) and\n[AIMEE_KB_SYNTH_TIERS.md](docs/AIMEE_KB_SYNTH_TIERS.md).\n\n| Compose file | Brings up | Use when |\n|--------------|-----------|----------|\n| `compose.server-managed.yaml` | `aimee-server` only; the wizard's Deploy step then launches `aimee-kb` + `aimee-llm` + Postgres via the mounted Docker socket | **Recommended default.** One container to deploy; the browser wizard brings up the rest. |\n| `compose.server.yaml` | `aimee-server` + `aimee-kb` + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway | Advanced: the full split stack brought up together, no socket mount. Scale/update/place server and kb independently. |\n| `compose.yaml` | `aimee-kb` + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway | The knowledge service alone: building block for a shared/scaled kb. |\n| `compose.server-standalone.yaml` | `aimee-server` only (SQLite DB1, no kb) | DB1-backed `/v1` with no shared knowledge. |\n\n**Bring up the self-deploying server:**\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server-managed.yaml up -d","doc_id":"05a73f772e91ca0f03742356","doc_kind":""}

The\n  autopilot `pipelines` table is left untouched, so old autopilot actions keep\n  working and the two namespaces never collide.\n- **CLI/API namespace (#3/#45):** a new `aimee pipeline …` CLI/MCP surface\n  (`status`, `gate`, `list`, `cancel`, `resume`, plus the loop driver), distinct\n  from `autopilot`. Any HTTP exposure uses `/v1/roundtable/pipelines/…`, never the\n  KB/corpus `GET /v1/pipeline/status`.\n- **Gate authority (#53/#54):** **no new capability bit** (the 16-bit `CAPS_ALL`\n  mask is full). But the deeper fact is that\n  **every** UDS HTTP client is indistinguishable: `server_http_authorize` returns\n  0 for `!is_tcp` (\"UDS: filesystem-permission auth, no token\") and\n  `server_http_conn_caps` grants `CAPS_ALL`, so the thin CLI, MCP, and webchat all\n  arrive as anonymous trusted-local with no caller identity. Notably the **HTTP-\n  over-UDS path captures no peer identity, whereas the legacy NDJSON socket already\n  derives `uid:<peer_uid>`** (`server_auth.c:263-265`). Two complementary fixes:\n  (a) capture the UDS peer UID on accept as a baseline principal (parity with\n  NDJSON), and (b) require forwarding proxies — webchat first — to stamp trusted\n  internal headers for source, principal/session, original request id, and\n  idempotency. Attribution cannot rely on the forwarded HTTP request alone. **Both\n  are net-new code:** `handle_conn` never calls `platform_ipc_peer_cred()` today\n  (it exists but is uncalled on the HTTP path), and there is no trusted-peer\n  allowlist — so distinguishing a trusted proxy (webchat) from an arbitrary UDS\n  peer, and gating forwarded-header acceptance on it, must be built before any\n  forwarded source/principal is trusted (it is a security prerequisite, not a\n  config knob). A UID allowlist by itself is insufficient in a same-user local\n  deploy (proxy and arbitrary clients share a UID) — though in the container\n  deploy webchat is root and the server is uid 1000, so UID *can* separate them\n  there. The robust cross-deploy answer is a proxy credential, and aimee already\n  ships the pattern: webchat reads `$AIMEE_HOME/server.token`, so reuse that\n  shared-secret/HMAC rather than invent a new factor.\n- **DB1 is a single shared SQLite handle, and audit writes are best-effort.** DB1\n  is one process-wide `sqlite3*` (`db1_init.c:19`) opened `SQLITE_OPEN_FULLMUTEX`\n  with `journal_mode=WAL` and a busy handler that retries 15× (20–150 ms) then","doc_id":"06178983346d4ba541339f2b","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:728:{"content":"## Durable server cache and refresh policy\n\nUse DB1 as the server-local authority so cache bytes and the monotonic generation/HWM commit atomically with the existing FULLMUTEX/WAL transaction gate and backup lifecycle. Add an immutable generation row plus singleton current pointer bound to generation, validity, exact JWKS/payload/envelope bytes and digests, previous/manifest digests, manifest id/public-root digest, trust-bundle digest, and fetch time. A `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction validates current state, inserts only an absent byte-identical generation, and advances the singleton pointer atomically. Commit ambiguity is unavailable; it never authorizes from presumed state. DB1 unavailable, busy, corrupt, inconsistent, or constraint failure denies and clears output.\n\nAt startup, after DB1 initialization and before listener acceptance, validate the configured trust bundle and any cached row. One authenticated refresh is allowed when configured. Consumer authorization uses the exact half-open interval `valid_from <= now && now < valid_until`; it grants no clock-skew extension beyond signed times. A refresh should be scheduled before expiry, but failure may continue using the artifact only until `valid_until`. Startup outage is nonfatal only if the cache is already cryptographically valid and currently in that interval; an empty or stale cache leaves management authorization unavailable and emits a bounded operator warning/availability metric without artifact or token bytes. This slice does not make the server data plane unavailable, and the existing unconditional `/v1/management/action` 503 remains unchanged regardless of cache state.\n\nExpose a cache lookup/refresh orchestrator with a single-flight mutex/condition. A known `kid` uses a currently valid cache without network. An empty cache or a strictly well-formed cache missing an otherwise valid token header `kid` makes exactly one authenticated mTLS fetch; concurrent waiters share that attempt; the verifier retries once and then rejects. A malformed JWKS, token header, signature, or claims is INVALID and never triggers network access. Transient fetch failure never deletes or replaces the last valid cache, but an expired/not-yet-valid cache cannot authorize.","doc_id":"06d90d251e1cb0eaa83b43d9","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:1827:{"content":"## Durable local replay consume\n\nAdd a DB1-owned `db1/server_management_jti.{c,h}` module and schema table dedicated to management\ntoken consumption, not a server TU reaching through `db1_internal.h` and not a generic idempotency\nstore:\n\n`server_management_jti(jti TEXT PRIMARY KEY, issuer, kid, audience, subject, team_id,\ncapability, peer_issuer, peer_serial, peer_fingerprint, request_sha256, correlation_id,\nissued_at, expires_at, consumed_at)`.\n\nSchema `CHECK`s mirror every application bound: jti 16..128, issuer 1..255, kid 1..64,\naudience 1..127, subject 1..576, positive team id, capability 1..64, peer issuer 1..511,\npeer serial 1..79 lowercase hex, both SHA-256 fields exactly 64 lowercase hex, correlation id\n1..128, and integer times with `0 <= issued_at < expires_at`. The application uses a compiled live\nrow ceiling of 4096; because the table can never exceed that ceiling, deletion of all expired rows\ninside the transaction is itself bounded. Index `(expires_at,jti)`. A single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`\ntransaction:\n\n1. deletes rows whose `expires_at` is strictly before the current time;\n2. checks a compiled live-row ceiling before insert;\n3. inserts the fully verified claim tuple with the current consume time; and\n4. commits before reporting success.\n\nThe unique insert is the authorization point. Constraint conflict means replay; saturation,\nbusy/locked DB, schema error, clock error, or commit ambiguity is unavailable/deny, never success.\nThe row is not deleted on downstream failure: C1a has no dispatch, and later packets must treat an\naccepted token as consumed before any action attempt. Persistence across process restart is\nmandatory. Expiry GC is bounded and indexed; tests use injected time and capacity rather than\nsleep. The existing DB1 transaction gate serializes in-process writers; external `SQLITE_BUSY`\ndoes not spin or sleep and fails unavailable. The promised crash boundary is process crash/restart,\nnot arbitrary power-loss durability: later dispatch occurs only after COMMIT returns success. If","doc_id":"11f20c28224228cd8dc020a3","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:1959:{"content":"## 6. The aimee-server\n\n`aimee-server` is the hub. It owns DB1, runs the compute pool, routes delegates,\nserves hooks, and exposes both the internal RPC protocol and the public HTTP /v1\nAPI.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    L[\"Listen sockets<br/>aimee-http.sock (HTTP /v1) + optional localhost TCP\"]\n    EV[\"HTTP listener<br/>(accept loop hands each connection to its own worker thread)\"]\n    AUTH[\"Auth gate<br/>local UDS = filesystem-trusted (full surface)<br/>TCP = bearer-scoped + 16 capability flags\"]\n    POOL[\"Bounded compute pool<br/>(delegate exec, chat, tool calls)\"]\n    DB1[(\"DB1 SQLite\")]\n    KBC[\"KB client<br/>typed RPC to aimee-kb\"]\n    PROV[\"Delegate HTTP client<br/>libcurl\"]\n\n    L --> EV --> AUTH\n    AUTH -->|fast handlers| DB1\n    AUTH -->|blocking handlers| POOL\n    POOL --> DB1\n    POOL --> KBC\n    POOL --> PROV\n```\n\nKey properties:\n\n- **Per-connection workers, bounded compute pool.** The HTTP accept loop hands\n  each connection to its own detached worker thread, so a slow or streaming\n  request never blocks the listener and independent `/v1` requests run\n  concurrently. Heavyweight handlers (DB query, network, subprocess, delegate\n  inference) additionally run on a bounded compute pool; a compute budget gate\n  serializes heavyweight inference to bound resource use.\n- **Transport.** Clients reach the server over its `/v1` HTTP surface: the\n  always-on `~/.config/aimee/aimee-http.sock` Unix socket, plus an optional\n  localhost TCP listener. Dispatch methods use dedicated `/v1` routes; the\n  generic `POST /v1/rpc` endpoint is retired. Streaming chat uses\n  `POST /v1/chat/stream`, whose body is a sequence of newline-delimited aimee\n  events terminated by a final status object. (The legacy newline-delimited\n  JSON-RPC socket was removed.)\n- **Authentication.** The local UDS is filesystem-permission gated and fully\n  trusted: it reaches the entire dispatch surface, with no token. The optional\n  TCP listener requires a configured bearer token and is capability-scoped.","doc_id":"133d45efee549b03c1b82df7","doc_kind":""}

Engine + authoritative state\n\n- **State = `(work_item_id, workflow_name, workflow_version, current_stage,\n  mode)`**, driven entirely by the pinned workflow graph — the engine has no\n  hard-coded lifecycle. Default store DB1 (per-user sqlite); `lifecycle.store: db2`\n  for team-shared.\n- **Single source of truth = the work-item row.** Proposal front-matter carries a\n  *derived/regenerated* status block (a cache); on divergence the row wins, `--force`\n  to overwrite from front-matter.\n- **Work-item id** is **server-minted and non-forgeable**: `wi_<random-128-bit>`\n  generated server-side at creation (never derived from client-supplied or\n  forgeable inputs like a client timestamp), with `(normalized_repo_url,\n  proposal_path)` stored as columns and a UNIQUE constraint that rejects a second\n  open work item for the same proposal (repo URL normalized — scheme, trailing\n  `.git`, host case — so fork/re-push variants don't silently diverge). Surfaced,\n  embedded in front-matter, the positional arg every verb takes.\n- **Terminal states:** `accepted`, `rejected` (human-initiated where the workflow\n  permits), `abandoned` (any non-terminal → terminal; requires `reason` + `actor`).\n  `aimee lifecycle status` distinguishes in-progress / rejected / abandoned.\n- **Loop-back accounting:** each loop-back increments an attempt counter on the\n  target stage; a per-stage `max_attempts` (default from cost caps) prevents an\n  infinite PR-fail→implement→fail cycle and forces a human decision when hit.\n- **Audit:** every transition appends to an immutable `lifecycle_event` log\n  (actor, stage, verdict/approval id, artifact content_hash, cost). Retained for the\n  work item's lifetime + a configurable `lifecycle.audit_retention_days` after a\n  terminal state, then GC'd; transcripts are referenced by id (stored with the\n  delegate job records), not duplicated inline.\n- **Concurrency:** ≤1 in-flight `advance` per work item (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / advisory\n  lock) so two terminals can't double-spend.","doc_id":"16ace9b68b83d23fc400f430","doc_kind":""}

A `setup.sh` that handles all of it is worth a week of effort\n  and has no technical blocker.\n- **Standing LoCoMo / LongMemEval cadence:** too many acceptance\n  criteria cite \"within ±0.005 of baseline,\" but the benchmarks don't\n  run on a cadence. Either put them on nightly/weekly CI (with a\n  retention policy for the artefacts) or stop citing parity\n  criteria that nobody measures.\n- **Proposal-supersession hygiene rule:** the PR that supersedes a\n  proposal should move the old one (to `rejected/`, `deferred/`, or\n  wherever it belongs) **in the same commit**. Drift like the\n  pluggable-db proposal sitting in `pending/` after being deleted by\n  its successor is how `pending/` becomes stale signal. Worth a short\n  `CONTRIBUTING.md` addition alongside the PR template.\n- **Dedicated operator audit surface:** the data is all there\n  (`operator_id` on every shareable row, `content_hash`, timestamps),\n  but a CLI verb rendering per-operator / per-scope activity in a\n  legible way does not exist. Flagged as a known gap in the\n  DB1/DB2 storage-boundary work.\n- **Distributed-mode auth design:** the deep-curator token lifecycle\n  is deliberately minimum-viable (opaque bearer, config-file seeded,\n  per-token audit). OIDC, short-lived tokens with refresh, per-user\n  login flows, and token-management endpoints are all deferred until\n  a real multi-tenant deployment motivates them. When that lands, it\n  deserves its own tracking item.","doc_id":"16d38030c7690919d4616177","doc_kind":""}

The product must\nsay **journaled compensating restore**, not atomic restore.\n\nBefore the first target write:\n\n1. acquire the DB1-backed per-worktree lease, retain its fencing token through every\n   journal update, and prove no turn is active for the session/worktree;\n2. authorize and no-follow-resolve every manifest path;\n3. verify root/provider identity, blob integrity, free space, same-device constraints,\n   and compare-and-swap tuples;\n4. capture the current state of every manifest target as a terminal compensation set;\n5. durably write `rewind_restore_runs` and every ordered step as `STAGED`;\n6. prepare same-filesystem, fd-relative temp objects and `fsync` them.\n\nCommit processes paths in deterministic order, using fd-relative rename/unlink, with file\nand parent-directory `fsync` after each rename group. Each completed step is journaled.\nThe fencing token is revalidated immediately before every target mutation; an expired or\nsuperseded owner cannot continue applying after daemon replacement.\nOnly after all filesystem steps land does one DB1 transaction mark the operational result\n`RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING` and enqueue a stable audit event id. The common audit bridge then\nappends that event to its separate sink and a final DB1 compare-and-swap marks `RESTORED`.\nThis does not pretend SQLite and the WORM/file audit sink share a transaction. Because the\ncurrent append-only sinks have no idempotency key, crash recovery is explicitly\nat-least-once: doctor retries the same event id and readers collapse duplicate terminal\nevents by that id. A future authoritative sink may add native deduplication or require\ncompensation on audit failure; this proposal does not claim cross-store exactly-once.\n\nOn a normal apply failure, the same journal drives compensation in reverse order. A crash\nleaves `RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS`; doctor can deterministically resume compensation from the","doc_id":"18c9a4cc0f4c1e3e8d4608e5","doc_kind":""}

Hundreds of `.c` files plus generated headers and `*.inc` split units. |\n| `src/db1/` | DB1 (SQLite) data layer, owned by `aimee-server`. |\n| `src/db2/` | DB2 (Postgres + pgvector) data layer, owned by `aimee-kb`. |\n| `src/server/` | `aimee-server` internals: event loop, auth, sessions, compute pool, HTTP /v1, KB client. |\n| `src/kb/` | `aimee-kb` internals: service dispatch, ingest/curator workers, KB HTTP. |\n| `src/gateway/` | Optional `aimee-gateway` (ambient presence: Telegram/ntfy/webhook, STT/TTS). |\n| `src/linux/`, `src/mac/`, `src/windows/`, `src/posix/` | Platform abstractions (events, IPC, paths, process). |\n| `src/headers/`, `src/shared/`, `src/vendor/` | Internal headers, shared helpers, vendored libs (cJSON). |\n| `src/tests/` | C unit tests (`test_*.c`), `fuzz_corpus/`, `support/`, and `test_build_integrity.sh`. |\n| `webchat/` | Standalone Go browser service (thin client to `aimee-server`). |\n| `frontend/` | React 19 + Vite UI, bundled to a single HTML file for webchat. |\n| `api/` | OpenAPI specs (`openapi-server-v1.yaml`, `openapi-v1.yaml`), the API contract. |\n| `skills/` | Bundled process skills (markdown + frontmatter). |\n| `session_templates/` | Multi-agent session templates (code-review, debate, design-critique, planning). |\n| `plugins/` | Plugin interface + example plugin manifest. |\n| `benchmarks/`, `tools/`, `data/` | Eval suites (`catalog.toml`, `suite/`, `targets/`), replay harnesses, dataset cache. |\n| `scripts/` | Sidecars (embeddings, LLM chat, curator, synthesis, ranker, planner) + build/boundary check scripts. |\n| `systemd/`, `service/`, `deploy/` | systemd user units, macOS launchd plists, container deploy config. |\n| `docs/` | Reference docs + the `proposals/` lifecycle (`pending` → `reviews`/`accepted` → `done`/`rejected`). |\n\nGenerated headers (checked in, regenerated on build): `schema_data.h` (DB schema","doc_id":"1916c60ad1371a12b259fda8","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:2724:{"content":"### 9.1 A pre-tool hook (the hot path)\n\n```mermaid\nsequenceDiagram\n    participant Tool as AI tool\n    participant CLI as aimee (client)\n    participant SRV as aimee-server\n    participant KB as aimee-kb\n    Tool->>CLI: PreToolUse JSON on stdin (Edit /etc/x)\n    CLI->>SRV: hooks.pre (Unix socket)\n    SRV->>SRV: classify path, check plan mode,<br/>worktree redirect, anti-patterns, drift\n    SRV-->>CLI: allow / block(exit 2) / warn(stderr)\n    CLI-->>Tool: exit code + message\n    Note over SRV,KB: anti-pattern + memory lookups hit KB only when needed\n```\n\nThe whole round-trip is ~1 ms at p50 because the client is already warm and the\nserver keeps DB1 and its KB connection open.","doc_id":"1a3be5bab32e55e999da4a1f","doc_kind":""}

The process-lifetime\n`g_remote_writes` policy is initialized once and has no in-process writer;\nconfiguration changes take effect only on restart, which closes the request. Read it at the final\ndispatch seam and prove by test/plant check that no live writer exists and that shutdown prevents\nthe old process from reaching the handler. The single\nbiggest simplification: **v1 audit writes are SYNCHRONOUS** — one `token_audit`\ninsert on the handler thread after the provider returns. A local DB1 insert is\nsub-millisecond against a multi-second LLM call, so it does not meaningfully load\nthe hot path, and synchronicity dissolves the entire async-queue blocker class\n(B1) and the reward-barrier (B7). The `ingress_audit_async` queue is **deferred to\na later, separately-gated phase**, and may only ship with the durability spec in\nB1.\n\n**B1 — Async audit queue overflow/backpressure (§2).** v1 has no queue: writes are\nsynchronous (above). The deferred async phase, if ever justified by a measured\nhot-path regression, MUST specify: a bounded queue (default 4096 rows); a\nblock-up-to-25ms-then-drop policy; a monotonic `ingress_audit_dropped_total` metric\nsurfaced to operators; and an explicit durability contract — \"best-effort: rows are\ndropped, never duplicated; drops are counted.\" Synchronous v1 is exactly-once\n(idempotent insert, B4).\n\n**B2 — Dedup confidentiality leak via shared webchat principal (§4).** The dedup\nkey MUST include the resolved principal/tenant id, and dedup is **fail-closed\ndisabled** for any request whose principal is shared/service (the anonymous\n`webchat` service principal, or any principal flagged `shared`). Two logged-out\nwebchat users can therefore never be cross-served. v1 dedup is enabled ONLY for\nrequests carrying a non-shared, authenticated per-user identity. Test: a request\nwith a shared principal is never served from the dedup cache, even on identical\nbody.\n\n**B3 — Backfill-from-`tool_name` misprices history (§2).** Do **not** backfill the\nmodel from `tool_name` (agent names are not pricing keys, §2a). /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:3363:{"content":"## Codebase grounding (verified)\n\n- **DB1 schema** = `src/db1/schema.sql` (one CREATE-IF-NOT-EXISTS per line, TEXT ISO\n  timestamps `DEFAULT (datetime('now'))`), embedded into `src/schema_data.h` as\n  `AIMEE_DB1_SCHEMA_SQL` by a CMake custom command (`CMakeLists.txt:1357`). **It is exec'd\n  in full at every DB1 open** by `db1_apply_schema_sqlite` (`src/db1/db_schema.c:52,66`), so a\n  new `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` **auto-creates on existing deployments** at next open — no\n  `user_version` bump needed (this is how every table shipped). `db1_reconcile_columns` adds\n  drift *columns*; tables are handled by the schema apply. `scripts/check-schema-sync.py` is a\n  CI gate → regenerate + commit `schema_data.h`.\n- **Accessor style:** `src/db1/wm.c`/`wm.h` — `db1_conn()`, sqlite3 prepare/bind/step/\n  finalize, `now_utc()`. **SHA-256:** OpenSSL `SHA256()` + `SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH` already used\n  in-tree (`src/db2/entity_nodes.c:43`); reuse directly.\n- **Op + HTTP routes:** op handlers in `src/server/server.c` table (`{\"wm.set\", …}`); routes\n  in `src/server/server_http_routes.inc` (`/v1/…`→op→handler, a `CAP_*`, `rh_dispatch_op`).\n- **Hook seam:** `aimee hooks pre`→`src/cmd_hooks.c`→`pre_tool_check`\n  (`src/guardrails_orchestrator.c:1196`); `guardrails_canonical_tool_name`. Cross-client via\n  `configure-hooks.sh`. **Session-start:** `src/cli_session_start.c`. **Unit tests:**\n  `aimee_add_test(name src.c …)` in `src/tests/CMakeLists.txt`. **CLI:** `src/cli_main.c` +\n  `cmd_*.c` (model `src/cmd_memory.c`).\n\nTimestamp domain: the design doc wrote `INTEGER`; the plan uses DB1's **TEXT-ISO**\n`datetime('now')` to match every neighbour (design doc carries an R5 erratum noting this).","doc_id":"2082ed75cfb351f3854f96e3","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:3374:{"content":"## What aimee-server is\n\n`aimee-server` is a single C11 process that owns **DB1** (local SQLite), runs the\nbounded compute pool, routes delegates, serves the lifecycle hooks, and exposes\nthe public HTTP `/v1` surface (its only client transport). The thin clients\n(`aimee`, `aimee-webchat`) hold no database; they reach this process over `/v1`\n(local `aimee-http.sock` or remote TCP) and forward typed requests. The expensive\nstate (open DB handles, a\nwarm KB connection, the worker pool) lives here, in a warm long-running process,\nwhich is what keeps CLI startup under 10 ms and a pre-tool hook check around 1 ms.\n\nIt links `-lsqlite3` (plus `-lssl`/`-lcrypto`/`-lpam`) and is built with\n`-DAIMEE_DB2_DISABLED`: it **never** links libpq and holds no DB2 SQL. All\nknowledge operations go through the typed **KB client** (`kb_client*.c`) to\n`aimee-kb`. The storage boundary is compile-enforced (`make check-linking`,\n`readelf` symbol checks).","doc_id":"20a78ff9be77b05cb453dbda","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:3463:{"content":"### 3.3 Single-box source build\n\nTo build and run everything on one host without Docker:\n\n```bash\ngit clone https://github.com/RakuenSoftware/aimee.git\ncd aimee\n./install-deps.sh   # system packages + PostgreSQL bootstrap (uses sudo)\n./install.sh        # build + install + configure (no sudo)\n```\n\n`install-deps.sh` installs the build/runtime packages and bootstraps the\n`aimee_shared` PostgreSQL database, the only steps that need root. (For a host\nthat uses a *remote* kb and needs no local database, run `AIMEE_KB_MODE=remote\n./install-deps.sh`.) Prerequisites by platform:\n\n| Need | Debian/Ubuntu | Fedora/RHEL | Arch | macOS |\n|------|---------------|-------------|------|-------|\n| C toolchain | `build-essential` | `gcc make` | `base-devel` | Xcode CLT |\n| pkg-config | `pkg-config` | `pkgconf-pkg-config` | `pkgconf` | `brew install pkg-config` |\n| SQLite3 (DB1) | `libsqlite3-dev sqlite3` | `sqlite-devel sqlite` | `sqlite` | system SQLite |\n| libpq (DB2) | `libpq-dev` | `libpq-devel` | `postgresql-libs` | `brew install libpq` |\n| libcurl | `libcurl4-openssl-dev` | `libcurl-devel` | `curl` | system curl |\n| libzstd | `libzstd-dev` | `libzstd-devel` | `zstd` | `brew install zstd` |\n| PAM (webchat) | `libpam0g-dev` | `pam-devel` | `pam` | built-in |\n| Postgres + pgvector | `postgresql postgresql-contrib` + pgvector | `postgresql-server` + `pgvector_NN` | `postgresql pgvector` | `brew install postgresql pgvector` |\n| ctags (indexing) | `universal-ctags` | `ctags` | `ctags` | `brew install universal-ctags` |\n| ripgrep (search) | `ripgrep` | `ripgrep` | `ripgrep` | `brew install ripgrep` |\n\nGo 1.25+ is required only to build `aimee-webchat`. Then `install.sh`, in order:\n\n1. **Check prerequisites** (FTS5 + the dev headers); if any are missing it stops\n   and points you back at `install-deps.sh` rather than escalating privileges.\n2. **Build** (only if sources changed): `cd src && make all server`, producing\n   `aimee`, `aimee-server`, and `aimee-kb` at the repo root, plus `aimee-webchat`","doc_id":"218f1bc4cdc7775100722197","doc_kind":""}

The real topology exposed and fixed a `db_postgres` decoded-BYTEA lifetime bug by retaining the envelope before reading later BYTEA columns. The real PG gate exposed and corrected the original owner-held facade design because the table owner is intentionally NOBYPASSRLS; roundtable runner `p5c2c-definer-decision-v2-20260722` converged on the dedicated, non-login, exact-closure definer role now implemented.\n\nValidation completed:\n\n- Local hardened server and kb builds, focused cache/token tests, schema sync, target/publisher isolation and plant checks, full lint, ASAN/UBSAN cache/token tests, and token fuzz corpus.\n- Full CT103 PostgreSQL 17 gate, including exact facade ownership/attributes/ACL closure and active, mismatched, pending, revoked, expired, sealed, and non-final fixtures.\n- CT260 root-run trust-file hardening and cache tests, including wrong mode, hard link, and symlink rejection.\n- Production CT260 kb to CT262 client topology with real mTLS enrollment/registry binding and byte-exact signed-envelope fetch.\n\nGeneration advancement, background pre-expiry scheduling, action dispatch composition, and the broader negative topology matrix remain explicitly in C2d/C3 rather than silently expanding this slice.\n\nBranch-review runner `p5c2c-branch-v9-20260722` identified one valid slice-local race: the facade captured its validity timestamp before waiting on the publication lock. The implementation now captures time after acquiring that lock. Four other reported regressions (mTLS worker stack, DB2 lease release, `agent_jobs.participant_token`, and `roundtable.review`) were confirmed as reverse-diff noise from 20 newer commits already on `origin/testing`; the branch is merged forward before convergence review so those base fixes remain intact.","doc_id":"25b240aba15bd53cdb9a2445","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:4509:{"content":"## Scaling contract: one server per user\n\n**`aimee-server` is strictly 1:1 with a user.** This is a design invariant, not a\ndeployment choice:\n\n- It owns **local, same-user runtime state** in DB1: sessions, working memory,\n  conversation windows, checkpoints, durable delegate jobs, secrets. That state is\n  private to one OS user on one host.\n- It authenticates callers by **`SO_PEERCRED`** (the connecting process's UID).\n  The trust model is \"same Unix user = same principal\"; there is no notion of a\n  remote tenant.\n- It is therefore **single-tenant and local by construction**. You do not shard\n  it, replicate it, or put it behind a load balancer. Each developer (each OS\n  login) runs exactly one `aimee-server` on their own machine, normally as a\n  systemd user unit or launchd agent.\n\nScale-out happens **below** the server, in the shared tier: many independent\n`aimee-server` instances (= many users) point at one shared `aimee-kb`/Postgres\ndeployment. The server is the per-user front; the KB is the many-user back. See\n[`src/kb/README.md`](../kb/README.md) for that side of the boundary.","doc_id":"2c319212105fbc127a030697","doc_kind":""}

The client and webchat talk only to the local `aimee-server`; runtime\nstate stays in server-owned DB1, knowledge lives behind `aimee-kb` in DB2 (local or\nshared Postgres). /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:4724:{"content":"### 6.1 Additive v2 tables\n\n`src/db1/schema.sql` gains new versioned tables; `schema_data.h` is regenerated through\nthe existing build rule. The legacy tables remain unchanged and read-only during the\ntransition.\n\nThe conceptual ownership is:\n\n- `rewind_change_sets`: execution/session/worktree identity, state, coverage, counts,\n  schema version, manifest hash, timestamps;\n- `rewind_preimages`: insert-only relative path, kind/mode/size/digest/blob ref,\n  sensitivity ruleset version;\n- `rewind_blob_refs`: the mutable active-retention edge from a set/entry to a blob;\n  expiry removes this edge only after the set becomes non-restorable, so immutable\n  preimage evidence can retain its digest and historical blob id without pinning bytes\n  forever;\n- `rewind_postimages`: insert-only sealed kind/mode/size/digest;\n- `rewind_operations`: bounded append-only tool evidence;\n- `rewind_restore_runs` and `rewind_restore_steps`: preview binding, durable apply journal,\n  compensation refs, per-step state, terminal outcome;\n- `rewind_worktree_leases`: DB1-backed root-identity lease with owner, fencing token,\n  heartbeat, and expiry, so a daemon replacement or offline maintenance process cannot\n  overlap restore with capture;\n- `rewind_incidents`: one-way security/integrity quarantine and acknowledgement state;\n- `rewind_blobs`: per-principal namespace, digest, size, refcount, lifecycle state.\n\nDB constraints/triggers prevent UPDATE/DELETE of sealed preimages, postimages, and\noperation evidence. State transitions use compare-and-swap updates. The implementation\nplan must include upgrade-from-current and downgrade/read-compatibility tests; it may not\nrely on the current best-effort ignored-`ALTER TABLE` loop for integrity-critical DDL.","doc_id":"2e489a328165fb9e4e9288f7","doc_kind":""}

For usage and getting started,\nsee the [root README](../README.md) and the full [Manual](../MANUAL.md). For the\nsystem-level architecture (process topology, trust/storage boundaries, request\nlifecycles) see [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). This document is\nthe code-level companion: module map, server internals, the RPC and HTTP\nsurfaces, the KB split, the build system, and testing.\n\naimee's core services are written in C11 for performance and minimal footprint. The current tree is a large C codebase (hundreds of `.c` files, plus generated headers and split `*.inc` units), shipped with the standalone Go `aimee-webchat` service plus `aimee`, `aimee-server`, and `aimee-kb`. Runtime DB ownership is pinned: clients are DB-free, the local server owns DB1 (sqlite), and KB owns DB2 (postgres + pgvector), which can be local or shared by deployment. MCP support is built into `aimee mcp-serve`.","doc_id":"2e83ae743d398e990af5ac1e","doc_kind":""}

It must not reuse or imply\nthe adjacent thread/branch stubs.\n\n- `turn_changes` enables a per-turn “Changes” affordance.\n- The webchat relay binds the authenticated cookie principal and session id; it rejects\n  caller-supplied identity.\n- The UI fetches durable preview data for the complete set and sends the short-lived\n  preview id for confirmation. Path-selected restore is not exposed in P0–P5.\n- Coverage, conflict, expiry, and restore-incident states are first-class; no partial\n  outcome becomes a green toast.\n- Reconnect queries DB1 by session/turn; correctness never depends on presence-ring\n  retention.","doc_id":"2eb9c1b27ad8c7e8579602be","doc_kind":""}

Per-connection buffered I/O; `EPOLLOUT` added only while a write is pending. |\n| Entry / signals | `server_main.c` | Startup handshake, SIGTERM/SIGINT graceful drain, unclean-exit forensics to DB1. |\n| Auth | `server_auth.c` | Capability lookup + a 16-bit capability mask declared per method (unknown methods default to deny). The local `/v1` UDS is filesystem-trusted (full surface); the optional TCP listener is bearer-gated (`server_http_authorize`, constant-time compare via `server_ct_equal`). |\n| Sessions | `server_session.c` | Session create/list/get/close, per-session worktrees and state. |\n| State handlers | `server_state.c` | Fast handlers: memory, index, rules, working memory, dashboard (routed to tier-owned APIs). |\n| Compute pool | `server_compute*.c`, `compute_pool.c`, `server_jobs_aux.c` | Bounded worker threads for anything that blocks (DB, network, subprocess, delegate inference); a compute-budget gate serializes heavyweight inference. Durable/background delegate jobs survive client disconnect. |\n| KB client | `kb_client*.c` | Typed RPC wrappers (memory, index, docs, agent, dashboard, roadmap, notes, curiosity, status) to `aimee-kb` over a Unix socket or HTTP (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`, port 8741). The server holds **no** DB2 SQL. |\n| Delegation | `agent_runtime.c`, `agent_loop.c`, `agent_policy.c`, `agent_tools.c`, `delegate_routing.c`, `delegate_openai.c`, `http_retry.c` | Cost-based route selection, tool-use loop (bash/read/write), provider HTTP shaping, retry/fallback. |\n| HTTP `/v1` | `server_http.c`, `server_api.c` | OpenAI-compatible inference, run management, read/control surfaces. UDS callers auth by peer UID; TCP callers present a bearer token (optionally `scope:`-prefixed). Contract: [`api/openapi-server-v1.yaml`](../../api/openapi-server-v1.yaml). |","doc_id":"2edd4bb99c88c0ede243812a","doc_kind":""}

The dominant `Write`/`Edit` path is covered\n  exactly; an inotify/fanotify watcher that closes the at-write gap is a **follow-up, not a\n  v1-correctness requirement** (R1 #3, R2 #4, R3 #2). This is stated, not hidden.\n- **Canonicalization is not byte-exact (R3 #1/#21).** We store a client-neutral\n  normalization and render per client, so a client re-reading its own write sees a\n  semantically-equivalent — not byte-identical — file. The render codec is audited for\n  round-trip fidelity (write→render→write→hash compare) and mismatches are logged; this is\n  the deliberate cost of cross-client sharing under one `(project,name)` key.\n- **Per-client deny contract is required (R3 #4/#10).** The deny-with-redirect is validated\n  per client; any client lacking a deny-with-message hook protocol is out of v1 scope and\n  listed as unsupported rather than silently mis-handled.\n- **DENY-as-success wording** depends on the model interpreting the reason correctly;\n  mitigated by live-run validation (R1 #14) but behavioral, not structural.\n- **Shared-memory content is untrusted.** Agent-authored bodies are stored and re-read by\n  other agents — a prompt-injection surface. Mitigations: body size cap, no auto-execution,\n  documented file perms; deeper review/tagging is a follow-up (R1 #22).","doc_id":"313b9634f5e808f414ba5ab9","doc_kind":""}
