Two servers:\n\n```\nbrowser ──/api/*──▶ webchat (Go)  ──/v1/*, UDS──▶ aimee-server (C)  ──▶ DB1 (sqlite)\n                     v1RequestWebuser                lifecycle_work_item / lifecycle_event\n                     (X-Aimee-Webuser + server.token)  wfe scheduler (autonomy engine)\n```\n\n- The Go webchat proxies each `/api/*` call to the C server's `/v1/*` HTTP surface\n  over a trusted unix socket, asserting the caller's identity with the\n  `X-Aimee-Webuser` header + `server.token` bearer (`v1RequestWebuser`). This is how\n  the C server resolves the caller's `webuser:<subject>` principal, which the\n  read endpoints use for ownership scoping (below).\n- The C server owns all state. Submitting writes the proposal markdown to\n  `$AIMEE_HOME/edit-workflows/workflow-actions/wi-*.md` and a `lifecycle_work_item` row; the wfe\n  scheduler drives that item through its workflow, appending a `lifecycle_event` per\n  transition.\n\n---","doc_id":"3882b524ac7c68e10eef8dd8","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:5836:{"content":"## What aimee-kb is\n\n`aimee-kb` is a single C11 process that owns the DB2 schema and all knowledge\noperations: the memory inference pipeline (dedup, contradiction detection,\ntemporal versioning, promotion/decay), the vector collections, the code index,\ndocument ingest, and the curator. `aimee-server` holds **no** DB2 SQL; it reaches\nall of this through the typed KB client over a Unix socket or HTTP. KB service\nentry, dispatcher, background workers, mining, curator, ingest, and the HTTP\nsurface live here (`kb_main.c`, `kb_service*.c`, `kb_ingest_workers.c`,\n`kb_curator_*.c`, `kb_background.c`, `http/`); remaining KB-owned flat modules\nmove here incrementally behind the same build targets.\n\nIt links `-lpq` (plus `-lzstd`/`-lssl`/`-lcrypto`) and is built with\n`-DAIMEE_DB1_DISABLED -DAIMEE_DISABLE_DB2_SQLITE_SHIM`: it **never** links SQLite.\nThe boundary is compile-enforced (`make check-linking`, `readelf` symbol checks,\n`scripts/check_tier_deps.sh`).","doc_id":"38e6ca4cf7e6ed8ee8d07e6c","doc_kind":""}

The schema SQL contains\n    * objects (e.g. a partial UNIQUE index over a later-added column) that\n    * reference columns added to a CREATE TABLE after the table first shipped.\n    * On a legacy DB the table pre-exists, so the table's `IF NOT EXISTS` is a\n    * no-op and the dependent index would fail (\"no such column\"), aborting the\n    * whole apply and leaving DB1 uninitialised. Adding the drift columns first\n    * makes the index creation succeed. On a fresh DB the ALTERs no-op (\"no such\n    * table\") and the schema SQL builds every table at full shape. */\n   db1_run_migrations(db);\n   char *err = NULL;\n   int rc = sqlite3_exec(db, AIMEE_DB1_SCHEMA_SQL, NULL, NULL, &err);\n   if (rc != SQLITE_OK)\n   {\n      copy_err(errbuf, errlen, err ? err : sqlite3_errmsg(db));\n      sqlite3_free(err);\n      return -1;\n   }\n   return 0;\n}\n\n/* ── declarative column reconciliation ─────────────────────────────────── */\n\n#define RECONCILE_MAX_COLS 128\n#define RECONCILE_NAME_MAX 64\n#define RECONCILE_SQL_MAX  512\n\nvoid db1_reconcile_columns(sqlite3 *db)\n{\n   if (!db)\n      return;\n\n   /* Build reference shape from canonical schema in an in-memory DB */\n   sqlite3 *ref = NULL;\n   if (sqlite3_open(\":memory:\", &ref) != SQLITE_OK)\n      return;\n   sqlite3_exec(ref, AIMEE_DB1_SCHEMA_SQL, NULL, NULL, NULL","doc_id":"3aade4a1eca0096457985dff","doc_kind":"code_unit_body"}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:6460:{"content":"## Attack Surfaces\n\nThe primary attack surfaces are:\n\n1. Unix socket interface\n   - Local IPC endpoint to `aimee-server`\n   - Protected primarily by filesystem permissions, local host access, and `SO_PEERCRED`\n   - Main concern: unauthorized local access, confused-deputy behavior, or misuse by same-user processes\n\n2. Capability tokens\n   - Used to authorize operational actions\n   - Main concern: token theft, overbroad grants, replay within the valid lifetime, or incorrect scope enforcement\n\n3. Browser webchat\n   - HTTPS endpoint with PAM-backed authentication and self-signed TLS\n   - Main concern: session misuse, local browser trust assumptions, and weaker guarantees than the Unix-socket channel\n\n4. Delegate execution path\n   - Server fork/exec of delegate agents and sub-agent orchestration\n   - Main concern: privilege misuse, unsafe parameter forwarding, or unintended expansion of allowed actions\n\n5. Delegate HTTP client to external providers\n   - Outbound HTTPS to OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or similar providers using API keys or OAuth\n   - Main concern: disclosure of prompts, metadata, or outputs to third parties; dependency on remote provider security and policy\n\n6. DB1-backed local state\n   - Local persistence used by the server\n   - Main concern: tampering by same-user processes, accidental over-retention, or unauthorized reads on a compromised host account\n\n7. aimee-server `/v1` HTTP listener (optional, off by default)\n   - A loopback-only TCP endpoint (`http://<IP_ADDRESS>:<port>/v1`) turned on with `aimee api enable`; it exposes the OpenAI-compatible surface to local editors\n   - Bearer-authenticated, per-bearer rate-limited, and gated by token scope; a scoped token is denied with `403` when it requests an action outside its grant\n   - Main concern: bearer theft by a same-host process, overbroad token scope, or exposing the port past loopback through a misconfigured proxy\n\n8. aimee-kb (DB2) transport\n   - The knowledge store is reached over a same-host Unix socket, or over TLS to a shared host","doc_id":"3f2295dc1f26de0daa057f6b","doc_kind":""}

The two tiers scale\ndifferently *by design*, and understanding which is which is the whole story:\n\n| Tier | Scope | How it scales |\n|------|-------|---------------|\n| `aimee-server` | **1:1 with a user** | Vertical only. One server per OS login, on that user's machine. |\n| `aimee-kb` | **Many users** | Horizontal. N stateless replicas behind a load balancer over one Postgres. |\n| Postgres (DB2) | The shared substrate | Standard Postgres scaling: instance sizing, pooling, read replicas; pgvector → pgvectorscale for large vector corpora. |\n\n#### `aimee-server` is one-per-user\n\n`aimee-server` owns DB1, the local, same-user runtime state (sessions, working\nmemory, conversation windows, checkpoints, jobs, secrets), and authenticates\ncallers by `SO_PEERCRED` peer UID. Its trust model is \"same Unix user = same\nprincipal.\" It is therefore **single-tenant and local by construction**: you do\nnot shard it, replicate it, or place it behind a load balancer. Each developer\n(each OS login) runs exactly one `aimee-server`, normally as a systemd user unit\nor launchd agent. You scale a single user's server *vertically* (more in-flight\ndelegates and parallel tool calls) with the thread-pool and concurrency knobs in\n[§27.4](#274-resource-tuning); that does not, and is not meant to, make it serve\nother users.\n\n#### `aimee-kb` is the horizontally-scalable, many-user tier\n\n`aimee-kb` owns DB2 and is where multi-user scale-out lives. Three properties make\nit horizontally scalable:\n\n1. **State lives in Postgres, not in the process.** A KB instance holds only\n   transient state (connection pools, request buffers, worker loops); all durable\n   knowledge is in DB2. Each instance is effectively a **stateless request server\n   over a shared database**.\n2. **It is reachable over the network.** KB serves its full `/v1` contract over\n   HTTP on `:8741` (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`, optional bearer token via","doc_id":"4a19bb566856eb170dabb5d4","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:7680:{"content":"## What already exists (why this is wiring, not green-field)\n\nThe four-way code survey (2026-07-17) found aimee already owns most of the hard primitives the commercial tools charge enterprise money for:\n\n- **Cost accounting — strong.** Per-request token→USD in the `token_audit` DB1 table (`src/db1/token_audit.c`, `src/server/token_tracker.c`): multi-source pricing (static table → registry/models.dev → authoritative DB1 `model_pricing`), attributed by model/source/role/tool/session/principal/delegation with parent cost-fold. Read surface exists: `GET /v1/insights/overview`, `/v1/dashboard/*`, React `CostPanel`. **Missing only the per-team/project dimension.**\n- **Credential vault — encrypted at rest**, keyed by attested principal (`src/server/vault_service.c`, `src/headers/vault_principal.h`).\n- **OIDC/JWT verifier — real** (RS256/JWKS, alg-pinned), in aimee-kb and kb-console (`src/kb/auth_oidc.c`, `kb-console/auth.go`) — opt-in via env today.\n- **PKI + mTLS enrollment CA** (`src/kb/enroll.c`, `src/kb/pki.c`, `src/server/kb_client_mtls.c`) — `aimee://` single-use tokens, `cert:CN` principals. Reusable for enrolling servers.\n- **Canonical IR + provider drivers** (`src/headers/aimee_ir.h`, `src/server/delegate_driver.c`, `aimee-universal-gateway.md`, done) — Anthropic / OpenAI-Chat / Responses / Gemini wire adapters through a protocol-neutral pivot. This is the egress machinery kb needs.\n- **Keyless roster + attested credential handling already exist** — the shipped `deploy/container/agents.json` ships no keys. The old client-push `POST /v1/session/credentials` was retired; provider secrets now live in the server vault (`/v1/vault/*`), and vault writes require an attested transport (UDS or confidential TLS+bearer — never plaintext TCP; `server_cert.c:18-22`, `server_http_identity.c:113-123`). The org-egress work reuses this attested-transport discipline rather than inventing a new one — org keys simply never leave kb in the first place.\n\nAbsent (the actual gaps, one sub-proposal each): a team/project entity; per-team/project cost attribution; per-team budgets and per-key rate limits (spend is tracked but never capped; the rate limiter is a single global bucket); OIDC on the aimee-server data plane + a kb→server control plane; and AWS Bedrock.","doc_id":"4ae8738e9a2b00bd4911be43","doc_kind":""}

Two tools, all\nheavy lifting on the CPU/local lane:\n\n**1. `web_search(query, k)` → a compact ranked index with stable handles.**\nTrim each result to `r<i>  <title>  ·  <host>  ·  ≤120-char snippet`; drop the\nblank-line-padded block formatting. The `handle → full-URL` map is held\nserver-side in DB1 (TTL-scoped). The model refers to results as `r1…rk` and\n**never re-emits a URL**.\n\n```\nr1  Zig 0.14 release notes  ·  ziglang.org  ·  async removed; new IO interface…\nr2  std.Io migration guide  ·  ziglang.org  ·  passing an Io implementation to…\n```\n\n**2. `web_read(ref, query?, span?, mode?)` → only the query-relevant spans, cited\nby id.** Server fetches the page (once; cached), strips to text, chunks it, and\nranks chunks against `query` (defaulting to the original search query). Returns\nthe top-N spans (target ≤1.5 KB), each tagged:\n\n```\nr2#1  (std.Io migration guide § \"Constructing an Io\")\n      Pass an Io implementation explicitly; the previous global event loop is gone…\nr2#3  (§ \"Blocking vs. evented\")\n      …\n```\n\n**Hybrid ranking with a mandatory literal pass (blocking fix #3).** Pure semantic\nranking can bury exactly the tokens an agent came for — an exact API name, an\nerror string, a version number, a flag. So `web_read` fuses two legs, literal\n*first*:\n\n- **Literal leg (mandatory, runs first):** if `query` (or quoted sub-phrases /\n  identifier-shaped tokens within it) occurs verbatim in the page, those spans are\n  **guaranteed into the result set**, above the semantic spans. Exact-substring and\n  identifier matches are never displaced by a higher embedding score. This reuses\n  the same lexical/BM25 leg `kb_ranker` already fuses for code search.\n  - **Budget reservation + omission signal (MEDIUM fix).** The literal leg gets a\n    **reserved share of the ≤1.5 KB budget** (default ~60%, tunable) that semantic","doc_id":"4fc997b0d1785d0724026e79","doc_kind":""}

Deployment topologies\n\n| Topology | Shape | Notes |\n|----------|-------|-------|\n| **Containerized server + KB (recommended)** | `aimee-server` + `aimee-kb` run as separate containers brought up together with Postgres/pgvector and the `aimee-llm` CPU inference gateway (embeddings, reranking, synthesis); the server fronts `/v1` on `:8740` and reaches the kb over HTTP on `:8741`. Developers install only the cross-platform thin client and point it at the server. | `compose.server.yaml` (split stack); `Dockerfile.server`, `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.aimee-llm`. |\n| **Single developer, source build** | All processes on one host from `install.sh`; service units keep server/KB running; DB1 in `~/.config/aimee`, DB2 in local Postgres. | Service-managed via `systemd/user/*.service` (Linux) or `service/com.aimee.*.plist` (macOS). KB starts first; server depends on it. |\n| **Shared KB** | Multiple `aimee-server` instances (containerized or local) point at one `aimee-kb`/Postgres deployment over HTTP. DB1 remains per-user/per-machine; DB2 carries only project, workspace, global, or otherwise shareable knowledge. | Set `AIMEE_KB_API_URL` (+ optional bearer); promote scopes deliberately. |\n| **KB-only container** | `aimee-kb` + Postgres/pgvector + a CPU inference gateway (embeddings, reranking, synthesis) via `compose.yaml`; KB binds `<IP_ADDRESS>:8741` and calls the gateway over HTTP. | The building block behind a shared/scaled KB; `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.aimee-llm`, `deploy/container/aimee.yaml`. |\n| **Standalone server** | `aimee-server` only (SQLite DB1, no kb), via `compose.server-standalone.yaml`. | DB1-backed `/v1` endpoints with no shared knowledge until a kb is wired in. |\n\nIn every topology the contracts are identical: thin clients speak the `/v1`\nprotocol to the server (local `aimee-http.sock` or a remote `host:port`); the\nserver speaks the typed KB `/v1` HTTP API to `aimee-kb` (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`; the\nlegacy Unix-socket KB transport was retired in #2747); the storage boundary holds.","doc_id":"503fa2092d1308ff8f2c7ad3","doc_kind":""}

Nothing extra to install; this is what a fresh\n  `install.sh` gives you.\n- **pgvectorscale (StreamingDiskANN) is the opt-in scale-up** for large corpora.\n  It is *additive*: built on top of pgvector, it reuses the same `vector` column\n  type and distance operators and only adds the `USING diskann` index, disk-backed\n  with bounded build memory, for the large/RAM-constrained regime where HNSW's\n  in-memory graph becomes the bottleneck. Select it per corpus table:\n\n  ```yaml\n  db2:\n    vector:\n      corpus_index: auto          # auto | hnsw | diskann\n      corpus_diskann_threshold: 1000000   # rows/table before \"auto\" picks diskann\n  ```\n\n  `auto` uses HNSW until a corpus table exceeds the threshold *and* the\n  `vectorscale` extension is installed, then picks diskann; it falls back to HNSW\n  with a notice when the extension is absent (so schema apply never hard-fails).\n  Memory/hot-path vectors stay HNSW unconditionally.\n- **Switching index type is a reindex, not a migration.** Data and queries are\n  identical across HNSW and diskann; `aimee kb repair --reindex-corpus` rebuilds\n  corpus indexes to the configured/`auto` type with no re-embedding and no query\n  rewrite. This is what makes \"started local on pgvector, grew, flipped to\n  pgvectorscale\" a config change rather than a data move.\n\n#### Deployment topologies\n\n| Topology | Shape | When |\n|----------|-------|------|\n| **Containerized server + KB (default)** | `aimee-server` + `aimee-kb` as containers (brought up together via `compose.server.yaml`) + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway ([§27.1](#271-containerized-deployment)); developers run only the thin client. | The recommended deployment for one user or a team. |\n| **Single developer, source build** | One `aimee-server` + one local `aimee-kb` + local Postgres, all on one host via service units. | The `install.sh` no-Docker setup. |\n| **Shared KB** | Many users' `aimee-server` instances point at one `aimee-kb`/Postgres over HTTP. DB1 stays per-user/per-machine; only KB-scoped knowledge crosses the boundary. | A team or a single user across several machines wanting shared knowledge. |","doc_id":"5148c516f4d1e11e64ce33b5","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:8465:{"content":"## §3 Fold freeze (byte-identical prefix reuse)\n\n**Principle.** The folded prefix is computed once and **reused byte-for-byte**\nacross subsequent turns; only the raw tail grows. The provider then reads the prefix\nfrom cache instead of re-billing it.\n\n- **Freeze the fold.** After a fold advances, its rendered view (skeleton + closet)\n  is frozen. New turns append only to the raw tail. The frozen bytes are emitted\n  identically next turn — this is what keeps cache-read rates high.\n- **Recompute only at epoch boundaries.** Re-derive the frozen prefix only when:\n  first call; freeze TTL expired; tail exceeded its cap; the retained band's\n  conclusions/claims changed; or a boundary rewrite is forced. Otherwise reuse.\n- **Single prefix-state owner (decision).** `payload_rewrite.c` remains the *sole*\n  owner of the cache-prefix state and the FNV-1a stable-prefix hash. This proposal\n  does **not** introduce a second writer. Instead it adopts a **layered contract**:\n  the transcript fold registers its frozen span with `payload_rewrite` via a new\n  helper (proposed `fold_emit_stable_span`), and the pending\n  `ingress-compression-and-cache-alignment` work registers the envelope span the\n  same way. `payload_rewrite` composes the registered spans into one prefix and\n  hashes once. Two independent writers mutating the prefix — the cache-thrash\n  hazard the review flagged — is thereby ruled out by construction. §0 reflects\n  that the two proposals *converge on one owner* rather than forking it.\n- **Pipeline order (normative).** The stages run in exactly this order so the frozen\n  bytes are never mutated after hashing:\n  1. raw DB1 transcript (append-only) →\n  2. transcript fold view + frozen-prefix assembly (§1/§2) →\n  3. provider-shape normalization (§1 atomic-pair rendering for Anthropic blocks /\n     OpenAI `tool_calls` / Gemini `parts`) →\n  4. `payload_rewrite` stable-span registration + single cache-prefix hash →\n  5. final payload to the provider.","doc_id":"528793c2009de491b2bd4660","doc_kind":""}

Fuzz the bounded bundle/envelope consumer and cache-state decoder under ASAN/UBSAN.\n\nTemp-DB1 tests cover install, exact replay, conflict, rollback/future-generation denial, restart persistence, trust-pin change, validity boundaries, busy/commit failure, schema corruption, and 32-thread single-flight/concurrent install. Crash/fault tests prove an interrupted transaction leaves the old valid cache or no cache, never a partially authoritative row.\n\nReal PostgreSQL 17 tests cover facade owner/prosecdef/proconfig and ACL closure; exact active triple success; every issuer/serial/fingerprint mutation; wrong enrollment purpose; pending/revoked registry; revoked/expired enrollment; sealed vault; future/expired publication; EMPTY/STAGED/CAS_DONE non-disclosure; FINAL exact byte equality; table/join tampering; public-schema/temp shadowing; runtime's lack of table/publisher/provider access; and fetch/revoke linearization with the following request denied.\n\nOn the isolated CT260/CT262 two-node topology, run production kb on CT260 and the server cache consumer on CT262. Prove authenticated fetch/install, exact response bytes, offline currently-valid restart use, expiry plus outage denial, and one unknown-kid refresh. Prove no cert, wrong CA/hostname/EKU/pin, revoked client on a reused connection, authority outage, spoof identity header, wrong method/query/body/path alias, plaintext/bearer access, malformed/rollback response, and truncated durable cache all fail closed without replacing the last valid row. Use only CT260/CT262 unless a full `pct list` is reread before allocating another throwaway guest.\n\nRun hardened server/kb/status/root-provisioner/publisher builds, target-isolation and publisher-isolation (including plant) checks, schema sync/alter-order/SQLite-shape checks, focused release and sanitizer/fuzz tests, the full real-PG gate, and an adversarial full-branch roundtable. After convergence, move this plan to done, update the offering delivery table and tally memory, create a PR against `testing`, merge with admin, and verify GitHub CI.","doc_id":"52cc80f80e7ff5731b721895","doc_kind":""}

It may not invent bytes, rewrite a digest,\nguess a path, promote partial coverage, or silently delete evidence. Security path\nviolations enter one-way quarantine and require acknowledgement before the worktree\nunfreezes.\n\nStartup performs only a bounded read-only check of open/restore-in-progress rows and emits\nhealth state. Deep scans and repairs remain operator initiated, keeping DB1 initialization\npredictable. The appliance recovery runbook consumes these classifications rather than\nduplicating them.","doc_id":"53b1911e4d52c46fbf07e339","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:8669:{"content":"## 3. Storage tiers (the DB1 / DB2 boundary)\n\naimee has exactly **two storage tiers**. They are pinned ownership boundaries,\nnot user-selectable backends. See [`STORAGE_TIERS.md`](STORAGE_TIERS.md) for the\ncanonical statement; this section explains why the boundary exists and how it is\nenforced.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n    subgraph S[\"aimee-server\"]\n        D1code[\"src/db1/* (SQLite)\"]\n    end\n    subgraph K[\"aimee-kb\"]\n        D2code[\"src/db2/* (Postgres + pgvector)\"]\n    end\n    D1code --> DB1[(\"DB1 · SQLite<br/>~/.config/aimee/aimee.db\")]\n    D2code --> DB2[(\"DB2 · Postgres<br/>aimee_shared\")]\n    S -->|typed RPC, never SQL| K\n```\n\n| Tier | Backed by | Owned by | Holds |\n|------|-----------|----------|-------|\n| **DB1** | SQLite (`~/.config/aimee/aimee.db`) | local `aimee-server` (`src/db1/`) | Local, same-user runtime state: sessions, working-memory key/values, conversation windows, checkpoints, durable delegate jobs, eval results, local caches, local interaction/learning signals, secrets. |\n| **DB2** | Postgres + pgvector (`aimee_shared` by default) | `aimee-kb` (`src/db2/`) | Durable knowledge for the configured KB scope: memories, rules, KB metadata, tasks and decisions, code-index metadata, learning records, roadmaps, **plus** the dense vector collections derived from those records. |\n\nKey consequences of the split:\n\n- **DB1 is local.** `aimee-server` is a local, same-user process and DB1 holds\n  local information for that server: sessions, secrets, working memory,\n  checkpoints, local evidence, and operational state.\n- **DB2 can be local or shared.** `aimee-kb` owns the Postgres knowledge store.\n  In the default topology it can be a local single-user DB; in team or\n  multi-host topologies it can be a shared KB. In either case, only information\n  appropriate for the KB scope is reflected or promoted from DB1/server flows\n  into DB2.\n- **The vector tier is inside DB2.** It was originally a separate Qdrant sidecar\n  and was folded into Postgres as the `vector` (pgvector)","doc_id":"546d5fe0d4d4e38655fec2e7","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:8864:{"content":"## Separate TLS trust domain\n\nAdd a process-owned management `SSL_CTX` in `server_tls`, with a context-selecting accept helper and\n`server_tls_management_begin`. The management context always requires a client certificate,\nenforces TLS 1.2 or newer and client-auth chain/time/purpose verification against its dedicated CA,\nand uses the configured management server leaf/key. A separate management context builder has no\ngeneric DB1 roster callback parameter or registration call by construction: management leaves are\nprimary-issued and their online next-request authority is the B3 nonce/staple protocol. A focused\ntest marks the same leaf revoked in the generic roster and proves this TLS context still performs\nonly CA/time/EKU verification while application status revocation remains fail-closed. The data\ncontext and optional→required ramp are unchanged.\n\nThe context is published only after it is completely built and remains process-lifetime owned\nbecause detached HTTP workers are not joined by current server shutdown. Once published it is\nnever freed or replaced before process exit; each `SSL_new` also holds its OpenSSL reference.\nStart failure before publication frees the private candidate. Same-process HTTP restart may reuse\nonly a byte-identical cert/key/CA configuration packet; any difference is a fatal start while the\npublished context remains untouched. Live `SSL` objects share the existing\nregistered-connection shutdown. Management TLS reload is explicitly restart-required; data\nSIGHUP never replaces or frees the management context.\n\n“Byte-identical” is a stored SHA-256 tuple over the bounded raw PEM bytes in fixed\n`certificate || private-key || client-CA` order, read through no-follow regular-file descriptors\nat context build time. Deployment topologies\n\n| Topology | Shape | Notes |\n|----------|-------|-------|\n| **Containerized server + KB (recommended)** | `aimee-server` + `aimee-kb` run as separate containers brought up together with Postgres/pgvector and the `aimee-llm` CPU inference gateway (embeddings, reranking, synthesis); the server fronts `/v1` on `:8740` and reaches the kb over HTTP on `:8741`. Developers install only the cross-platform thin client and point it at the server. | `compose.server.yaml` (split stack); `Dockerfile.server`, `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.aimee-llm`. |\n| **Single developer, source build** | All processes on one host from `install.sh`; service units keep server/KB running; DB1 in `~/.config/aimee`, DB2 in local Postgres. | Service-managed via `systemd/user/*.service` (Linux) or `service/com.aimee.*.plist` (macOS). Circuit breaker: where does the state live?\n\nItem 4 wants a consecutive-failure breaker with cooldown and a half-open probe,\ncounting **empty results as failure** (a scraper returning 200-with-nothing is\ntelling you it has decided you are a bot).\n\nThe design question is state location:\n\n- **(a) Process-local static.** Simple, no schema. Lost on restart, and not\n  shared across processes.\n- **(b) DB1 table.** Survives restart, shared. Heavier, and a breaker that\n  persists a stale \"engine is dead\" verdict across a restart may suppress a\n  working engine.\n\n**I propose (a).** The breaker's whole purpose is to avoid hammering a dead\nengine inside a working session; forgetting on restart is acceptable and\narguably correct. I want this checked — the counter-argument is that a server\nrestarting frequently never accumulates enough state for the breaker to fire.\n\nThresholds (all guesses, and I will label them as such in the header): 3\nconsecutive failures to open, 60s cooldown, one half-open probe.","doc_id":"5edf166a7821359b0f3ef08d","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:10005:{"content":"# Storage Tiers\n\naimee uses two pinned storage tiers. They are not user-selectable runtime\nbackends.\n\n| Tier | Ownership | Contents |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| DB1 | `src/db1/` | Local user and session information, credentials, checkpoints, multi-agent ensembles, local caches, local interaction/learning signals, and other same-user state. Backed by SQLite, owned by the local `aimee-server`. |\n| DB2 | `src/db2/` | Durable knowledge for the configured KB scope: memories, rules, KB metadata, task and decision records, code index metadata, coordination records, and the dense vector indexes for that knowledge (pgvector extension, in-process). Backed by Postgres, owned by `aimee-kb`, and deployable as either a local single-user KB or a shared KB. |\n\nCode outside a tier must call typed APIs instead of depending on a tier's\nstorage handles or provider vocabulary. The tier-boundary check in\n`scripts/check_tier_deps.sh` enforces the public surface that has been cleaned\nup so far.\n\nOperationally, DB1 is local to the user profile and belongs to one\n`aimee-server` process. It is where private runtime state and local evidence are\ncaptured first. DB2 is the durable knowledge source for project, workspace, and\nglobal facts plus their dense embeddings; it may be local to the same machine or\nshared by multiple servers. Shared deployments should receive only information\nappropriate for that shared scope, through the memory, learning, reflection, and\nKB APIs that promote or reflect local server evidence into durable knowledge.\n\nThe vector tier was originally a separate Qdrant sidecar; it was folded\ninto DB2 as a pgvector extension in #1575, vectors live in the same Postgres\ninstance as the rest of DB2 and need no separate connection or service.","doc_id":"615cb1d392e695ef0d723361","doc_kind":""}

Move delegate/provider execution, vault and policy enforcement into isolated\n   Go services. Preserve durable admission-before-dispatch semantics.\n5. Rewrite the KB service and DB2 ownership in Go, retaining typed HTTP boundaries.\n6. Replace thin-client and gateway behavior where needed. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:10843:{"content":"## Design: on-demand threads + high safety ceiling\n\nEach sessionless delegate runs on **its own detached thread**, spawned on\ndemand and reaped on completion (`delegate_spawn_ondemand` in\n`server_compute.c`). No fixed pool; no compute-budget gate. Throttling is the\nper-model limiter. A configurable **backstop ceiling** (`delegate_max_inflight`,\ndefault **512**, env `AIMEE_DELEGATE_MAX_INFLIGHT`) prevents a pathological\nfan-out from exhausting fds/memory — \"effectively unlimited\" for any real\nworkload, but not literally unbounded.\n\nMechanics:\n- An atomic-by-mutex in-flight counter; spawn rejects (`-1`, job marked failed)\n  only at the ceiling — unreachable under the per-model limiter in normal use.\n- Detached threads carry the same 32 MB stack as compute-pool workers (the\n  agent loop has deep frames).\n- The compute **budget is bypassed** exactly as session delegates already do:\n  a positive `compute_executor_threads` grant makes `compute_ctx_begin_budget`\n  take its non-blocking path (verified: `compute_ctx_release_budget` then never\n  touches the global budget). /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11239:{"content":"## Server Architecture\n\nThe shipped artifacts are four binaries: `aimee`, `aimee-webchat`, `aimee-server`, and `aimee-kb`. Common runtime code and git MCP handlers are linked directly into the binaries that need them instead of being shipped as separate executables or shared libraries. Long-running work uses `aimee-server`'s in-process compute pool; there is no separate worker binary.\n\n| Binary | Libraries | External deps |\n|--------|-----------|---------------|\n| `aimee` | Thin CLI transport + MCP stdio bridge | pthread |\n| `aimee-webchat` | DB-free webchat launcher; talks only to `aimee-server` through `webchat.serve` | pthread |\n| `aimee-server` | Local DB1 daemon, agent/runtime orchestration, KB RPC client | sqlite3, ssl, crypto, pam |\n| `aimee-kb` | Local-or-shared DB2 RPC service + memory/KB pipeline (incl. pgvector) | libpq, ssl, crypto |\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    CLI[aimee\\nCLI + MCP stdio] -->|JSON RPC| SRV[aimee-server\\nDB1 + compute pool]\n    WEB[aimee-webchat\\nbrowser-facing client] -->|JSON RPC| SRV\n    SRV -->|typed KB /v1 HTTP| KB[aimee-kb\\nDB2 + pgvector]\n    SRV --> DB1[src/db1/*]\n    KB --> DB2[src/db2/*]\n```","doc_id":"6d681f4dbb43a35b1c39daba","doc_kind":""}

Until a Go runner\nimplements every production block, the Go control plane may call an isolated\ncompatibility worker over the typed runner protocol. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11502:{"content":"## Scaling model\n\nThe scaling boundary is the storage boundary: the per-user server and the shared\nknowledge service scale independently and in different ways.\n\n**`aimee-server` is 1:1 with a user.** It owns DB1 (local SQLite, same-user\nruntime state) and authenticates by `SO_PEERCRED` peer UID, so it is single-tenant\nand local by construction: one per OS login, never sharded or load-balanced. Its\nonly scaling axis is *vertical*: the compute pool and concurrency knobs\n(`compute_threads` / `worker_threads` / `background_threads` / `session_threads`,\n`concurrency.per_model`) raise a single user's in-flight delegate and tool-call\nthroughput.\n\n**`aimee-kb` is the horizontally-scalable, many-user tier.** All durable state\nlives in DB2 (Postgres); a KB process holds only connection pools and worker\nloops, making each instance an effectively stateless request server over a shared\ndatabase. Many `aimee-server` instances (many users) reach one KB over HTTP `:8741`\n(`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`). Critically, the background pipeline claims work straight off\nDB2 with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (`db2_kb_ingest_queue_claim_next` in\n`src/kb/kb_ingest_workers.c`; the curator drain in `kb_curator_extract_code.c`), so\nconcurrent KB replicas never double-claim a row; Postgres is the only\ncoordinator. The scale-out recipe is therefore: **run N `aimee-kb` replicas behind\na load balancer over one Postgres.**\n\n**DB2 is standard Postgres.** It is one `aimee_shared` database with `pg_trgm` +\n`vector` (pgvector), scaled with the normal Postgres playbook (instance sizing,\npooling, read replicas; `db2_pool_size` bounds each instance's pool, 1-32). Vector\nsearch scales inside it: pgvector HNSW by default (and always for memory vectors),\nwith **pgvectorscale (StreamingDiskANN)** as an additive, opt-in scale-up for large\ncorpus tables. The index type is chosen per corpus table by\n`db2.vector.corpus_index` (`auto`|`hnsw`|`diskann`) /\n`db2.vector.corpus_diskann_threshold` (`pgvec_corpus_index_choose` in\n`src/db2/pgvec_transport.c`); because the `vector` column and queries are identical","doc_id":"6fceedb28b4162696ec7f4e8","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11708:{"content":"## Attack Surfaces\n\nThe primary attack surfaces are:\n\n1. Unix socket interface\n   - Local IPC endpoint to `aimee-server`\n   - Protected primarily by filesystem permissions, local host access, and `SO_PEERCRED`\n   - Main concern: unauthorized local access, confused-deputy behavior, or misuse by same-user processes\n\n2. Capability tokens\n   - Used to authorize operational actions\n   - Main concern: token theft, overbroad grants, replay within the valid lifetime, or incorrect scope enforcement\n\n3. Browser webchat\n   - HTTPS endpoint with PAM-backed authentication and self-signed TLS\n   - Main concern: session misuse, local browser trust assumptions, and weaker guarantees than the Unix-socket channel\n\n4. Delegate execution path\n   - Server fork/exec of delegate agents and sub-agent orchestration\n   - Main concern: privilege misuse, unsafe parameter forwarding, or unintended expansion of allowed actions\n\n5. Delegate HTTP client to external providers\n   - Outbound HTTPS to OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or similar providers using API keys or OAuth\n   - Main concern: disclosure of prompts, metadata, or outputs to third parties; dependency on remote provider security and policy\n\n6. DB1-backed local state\n   - Local persistence used by the server\n   - Main concern: tampering by same-user processes, accidental over-retention, or unauthorized reads on a compromised host account\n\n7. aimee-server `/v1` HTTP listener (optional, off by default)\n   - A loopback-only TCP endpoint (`http://<IP_ADDRESS>:<port>/v1`) turned on with `aimee api enable`; it exposes the OpenAI-compatible surface to local editors\n   - Bearer-authenticated, per-bearer rate-limited, and gated by token scope; a scoped token is denied with `403` when it requests an action outside its grant\n   - Main concern: bearer theft by a same-host process, overbroad token scope, or exposing the port past loopback through a misconfigured proxy\n\n8. aimee-kb (DB2) transport\n   - The knowledge store is reached over a same-host Unix socket, or over TLS to a shared host","doc_id":"71d1bd7361d3f980ddb4ed1f","doc_kind":""}

DB2 belongs to\n     aimee-kb and can be local or shared; local evidence is reflected or\n     promoted there only when it is appropriate for the configured KB scope.\n```","doc_id":"738103dfb23ceec4555859b1","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:11875:{"content":"### Scaling and multi-user deployment\n\nScaling follows the storage boundary: per-user state and shared knowledge live in\ndifferent processes and scale differently.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph Users[\"Many users / machines\"]\n        S1[\"aimee-server (user A)<br/>DB1 · SQLite (local)\"]\n        S2[\"aimee-server (user B)<br/>DB1 · SQLite (local)\"]\n        S3[\"aimee-server (user C)<br/>DB1 · SQLite (local)\"]\n    end\n    LB[\"Load balancer<br/>HTTP :8741\"]\n    subgraph KB[\"aimee-kb replicas (stateless)\"]\n        K1[\"aimee-kb\"]\n        K2[\"aimee-kb\"]\n        K3[\"aimee-kb\"]\n    end\n    PG[(\"PostgreSQL · aimee_shared<br/>pgvector → pgvectorscale at scale\")]\n\n    S1 --> LB\n    S2 --> LB\n    S3 --> LB\n    LB --> K1\n    LB --> K2\n    LB --> K3\n    K1 --> PG\n    K2 --> PG\n    K3 --> PG\n```\n\n- **`aimee-server` is 1:1 with a user.** It owns local same-user state (DB1/SQLite)\n  and authenticates by peer UID, so each developer runs exactly one server on their\n  own machine. Single-tenant and local by design; never sharded or replicated.\n- **`aimee-kb` is the shared, horizontally-scalable tier.** All durable state lives\n  in Postgres; a KB process is otherwise a stateless request server plus background\n  workers. One KB deployment serves many `aimee-server` instances; scale it by\n  running **multiple `aimee-kb` replicas behind a load balancer** on HTTP `:8741`.\n  The ingest/curator workers coordinate purely through Postgres\n  (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), so adding replicas needs no external coordinator.\n- **The database is standard Postgres.** Knowledge rows and their vector embeddings\n  live in one database (`aimee_shared`) with the `pg_trgm` and `vector` (pgvector)\n  extensions. Scale it like any Postgres: bigger instance, pooling, read replicas.\n  For large vector corpora add **`pgvectorscale`** (StreamingDiskANN) on top of\n  pgvector, with identical data and queries, so switching is a reindex, not a migration.\n  Small and local installs stay on plain pgvector (HNSW).","doc_id":"739a4afd8b4b888b92bece1a","doc_kind":""}

They are\nrealized in code and enforced in review; their standalone proposal documents are\n**not currently in the tree** (see [Documentation integrity](#documentation-integrity)):\n\n1. **Architecture Charter** — fixes role division across neural, symbolic,\n   statistical, planning, and deterministic passes (Recall / Rerank / Rewrite /\n   Extract / Synthesize / Judge / Reflect / Classify-Score / Plan-Search / Reason /\n   Rank-Fuse / Calibrate / Detect-Cluster / Constrain-Verify / Evaluate-Optimize /\n   Gate-Promote / Enforce), one artifact schema, one audit schema, the sidecar\n   protocol, and evaluation/calibration discipline. Any new intelligence-surface\n   proposal must name its charter role(s).\n2. **Two-DB Split** — DB1 (SQLite, local user store) and DB2 (Postgres, shared\n   knowledge store) with a tier-pinned Data Access Layer; the boundary is\n   compile-enforced. The vector tier lives **inside DB2** as a pgvector extension\n   (folded in from a former Qdrant sidecar in #1575) — vectors share the same\n   connection and transaction domain as the rows they embed. See\n   [`STORAGE_TIERS.md`](STORAGE_TIERS.md).\n3. **Memory Public Contract** — the caller-facing memory contract (scope, filters,\n   typed mutation verbs, profile packs, stable `--explain`) shared across CLI, MCP,\n   and the aimee-kb `/v1/` API.","doc_id":"7436f6956270a7f6b5dc07d9","doc_kind":""}

Issuance is operator-gated.\n- **Commands**: `aimee cert issue <client-name>` (CN=`<client-name>`, short-lived,\n  returns cert+key or signs a CSR), `aimee cert list`, `aimee cert revoke <name|serial>`.\n- **Revocation = online DB1 serial denylist** checked in the verify callback (no\n  CRL distribution problem; revoke takes effect on the next handshake). Fail-closed\n  if the denylist can't be read.\n- **Enrollment bootstrap**: a one-time, **bearer-authenticated** `/v1/cert/enroll`\n  that issues a client cert (server-generated keypair or CSR sign), solving the\n  first-hand-off trust problem by leaning on the existing shared bearer for\n  enrollment only. (For a host\nthat uses a *remote* kb and needs no local database, run `AIMEE_KB_MODE=remote\n./install-deps.sh`.) Prerequisites by platform:\n\n| Need | Debian/Ubuntu | Fedora/RHEL | Arch | macOS |\n|------|---------------|-------------|------|-------|\n| C toolchain | `build-essential` | `gcc make` | `base-devel` | Xcode CLT |\n| pkg-config | `pkg-config` | `pkgconf-pkg-config` | `pkgconf` | `brew install pkg-config` |\n| SQLite3 (DB1) | `libsqlite3-dev sqlite3` | `sqlite-devel sqlite` | `sqlite` | system SQLite |\n| libpq (DB2) | `libpq-dev` | `libpq-devel` | `postgresql-libs` | `brew install libpq` |\n| libcurl | `libcurl4-openssl-dev` | `libcurl-devel` | `curl` | system curl |\n| libzstd | `libzstd-dev` | `libzstd-devel` | `zstd` | `brew install zstd` |\n| PAM (webchat) | `libpam0g-dev` | `pam-devel` | `pam` | built-in |\n| Postgres + pgvector | `postgresql postgresql-contrib` + pgvector | `postgresql-server` + `pgvector_NN` | `postgresql pgvector` | `brew install postgresql pgvector` |\n| ctags (indexing) | `universal-ctags` | `ctags` | `ctags` | `brew install universal-ctags` |\n| ripgrep (search) | `ripgrep` | `ripgrep` | `ripgrep` | `brew install ripgrep` |\n\nGo 1.25+ is required only to build `aimee-webchat`. Then `install.sh`, in order:\n\n1. **Check prerequisites** (FTS5 + the dev headers); if any are missing it stops\n   and points you back at `install-deps.sh` rather than escalating privileges.\n2. **Build** (only if sources changed): `cd src && make all server`, producing\n   `aimee`, `aimee-server`, and `aimee-kb` at the repo root, plus `aimee-webchat`","doc_id":"774b7cc3eb398c6f4c129e30","doc_kind":""}

DB1 is authoritative; an external\n  edit does not silently become the source of truth.\n- aimee's **own** re-materialize writes use direct filesystem syscalls in the server/CLI\n  process and therefore **cannot** re-enter a PreToolUse hook (hooks fire only on *agent\n  tool calls*, not on aimee's own process I/O). This makes the no-loop property\n  **structural**, not flag-based (R1 #2, #23); a test exercises aimee's writer with the\n  hook installed to prove it.\n\nAccepted scope: **single host.** DB1 is local SQLite, so \"shared across all agents/\nsessions\" means *on this machine*. Working memory\n\nWorking memory (`aimee wm`) is fast, session-scoped scratch stored in DB1 with an\noptional TTL. Use it for the current task, intermediate state, or anything the AI\nshould remember within a session but not promote to durable knowledge.\n\n```bash\naimee wm set current-task \"Review PR #42 for security issues\"\naimee wm set scratch.findings \"3 issues, see notes\" --category review --ttl 3600\naimee wm get current-task\naimee wm list --category review\n```\n\nValues fold into L1 memory at session end if relevant; otherwise they expire.\n\n---","doc_id":"7f88787e5a745f5d4ba3f1d3","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:13121:{"content":"## Scaling model\n\nThe scaling boundary is the storage boundary: the per-user server and the shared\nknowledge service scale independently and in different ways.\n\n**`aimee-server` is 1:1 with a user.** It owns DB1 (local SQLite, same-user\nruntime state) and authenticates by `SO_PEERCRED` peer UID, so it is single-tenant\nand local by construction: one per OS login, never sharded or load-balanced. Its\nonly scaling axis is *vertical*: the compute pool and concurrency knobs\n(`compute_threads` / `worker_threads` / `background_threads` / `session_threads`,\n`concurrency.per_model`) raise a single user's in-flight delegate and tool-call\nthroughput.\n\n**`aimee-kb` is the horizontally-scalable, many-user tier.** All durable state\nlives in DB2 (Postgres); a KB process holds only connection pools and worker\nloops, making each instance an effectively stateless request server over a shared\ndatabase. Many `aimee-server` instances (many users) reach one KB over HTTP `:8741`\n(`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`). Critically, the background pipeline claims work straight off\nDB2 with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (`db2_kb_ingest_queue_claim_next` in\n`src/kb/kb_ingest_workers.c`; the curator drain in `kb_curator_extract_code.c`), so\nconcurrent KB replicas never double-claim a row; Postgres is the only\ncoordinator. The scale-out recipe is therefore: **run N `aimee-kb` replicas behind\na load balancer over one Postgres.**\n\n**DB2 is standard Postgres.** It is one `aimee_shared` database with `pg_trgm` +\n`vector` (pgvector), scaled with the normal Postgres playbook (instance sizing,\npooling, read replicas; `db2_pool_size` bounds each instance's pool, 1-32). Vector\nsearch scales inside it: pgvector HNSW by default (and always for memory vectors),\nwith **pgvectorscale (StreamingDiskANN)** as an additive, opt-in scale-up for large\ncorpus tables. The index type is chosen per corpus table by\n`db2.vector.corpus_index` (`auto`|`hnsw`|`diskann`) /\n`db2.vector.corpus_diskann_threshold` (`pgvec_corpus_index_choose` in\n`src/db2/pgvec_transport.c`); because the `vector` column and queries are identical","doc_id":"80205e68b60ffaa462355169","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:13147:{"content":"## Goal\n\nIntercept **any** agent writing to its own local memory and redirect the write to a\nsingle central store, **without** the agent being able to keep a private copy:\n\n1. **Capture** — agent memory writes are detected at the existing cross-client hook seam\n   and persisted to the aimee-server store.\n2. **Block** — the agent's own write is denied; the agent never owns the bytes on disk.\n3. **Re-materialize** — aimee (not the agent) writes the authoritative file back, so\n   native reads (`Read`/`Glob`/`Grep`) and the harness's automatic recall keep working.\n4. **Share** — memory is keyed per-project and shared across every agent/session/client\n   working that project on the host.\n\nDestination is **DB1** — aimee-server's own SQLite database\n(`~/.config/aimee/aimee.db`, `src/db1/`), opened by the server at\n`src/server/server.c:1616` via `db1_init` (`src/db1/db1_init.c:54`). **Explicitly not**\nthe kb's db2/Postgres, where the existing `memory.store` RPC lands\n(`src/kb/kb_service_memory.c:1418` → `src/db2/kb_service_backend_memory.c:1171`). This is\na new, parallel store; the kb memory path is untouched.","doc_id":"806915738e893fb1f4ca028e","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:13308:{"content":"## §3 Fold freeze (byte-identical prefix reuse)\n\n**Principle.** The folded prefix is computed once and **reused byte-for-byte**\nacross subsequent turns; only the raw tail grows. The provider then reads the prefix\nfrom cache instead of re-billing it.\n\n- **Freeze the fold.** After a fold advances, its rendered view (skeleton + closet)\n  is frozen. New turns append only to the raw tail. The frozen bytes are emitted\n  identically next turn — this is what keeps cache-read rates high.\n- **Recompute only at epoch boundaries.** Re-derive the frozen prefix only when:\n  first call; freeze TTL expired; tail exceeded its cap; the retained band's\n  conclusions/claims changed; or a boundary rewrite is forced. Otherwise reuse.\n- **Single prefix-state owner (decision).** `payload_rewrite.c` remains the *sole*\n  owner of the cache-prefix state and the FNV-1a stable-prefix hash. This proposal\n  does **not** introduce a second writer. Instead it adopts a **layered contract**:\n  the transcript fold registers its frozen span with `payload_rewrite` via a new\n  helper (proposed `fold_emit_stable_span`), and the pending\n  `ingress-compression-and-cache-alignment` work registers the envelope span the\n  same way. `payload_rewrite` composes the registered spans into one prefix and\n  hashes once. Two independent writers mutating the prefix — the cache-thrash\n  hazard the review flagged — is thereby ruled out by construction. §0 reflects\n  that the two proposals *converge on one owner* rather than forking it.\n- **Pipeline order (normative).** The stages run in exactly this order so the frozen\n  bytes are never mutated after hashing:\n  1. raw DB1 transcript (append-only) →\n  2. transcript fold view + frozen-prefix assembly (§1/§2) →\n  3. provider-shape normalization (§1 atomic-pair rendering for Anthropic blocks /\n     OpenAI `tool_calls` / Gemini `parts`) →\n  4. `payload_rewrite` stable-span registration + single cache-prefix hash →\n  5. final payload to the provider.","doc_id":"8210f9737a753f411ad82881","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:13445:{"content":"### 6.2 Blob store\n\nPreimage bytes move out of unbounded inline SQLite blobs into a DB1-owned store beneath\n`$AIMEE_HOME/rewind/blobs`, following Aimee's existing content-addressed-store durability\npattern:\n\n- per-principal namespace; no cross-principal deduplication or equality oracle;\n- SHA-256 content identity, opaque refs at external surfaces;\n- `0700` directories, `0600` regular files, `O_NOFOLLOW`;\n- unique temp write → file `fsync` → atomic rename → directory `fsync`;\n- DB ref committed only after the blob is durable;\n- blobs with an active `rewind_blob_refs` edge are never deleted;\n- oldest eligible sealed sets expire under both count and byte ceilings;\n- manifest/audit rows survive blob expiry.\n\nExpiry is ordered: compare-and-swap the set from restore-eligible to `EXPIRED`, remove its\nactive ref edges in the same DB1 transaction, then let asynchronous GC delete now-unreferenced\nblob files after a grace period. A preimage row is never rewritten merely because its\nretained bytes expired.\n\nGarbage collection is bounded and asynchronous. If it cannot make space, protected\ncapture blocks before mutation with `store_budget_exhausted`; it does not delete a live\nref or silently degrade to partial coverage.","doc_id":"835f45c77a99311b3bb4e3c8","doc_kind":""}

Pin a version (or a fork/registry) by overriding\n`AIMEE_SERVER_IMAGE` / `AIMEE_KB_IMAGE` / `AIMEE_EMBEDDER_IMAGE` (e.g.\n`AIMEE_SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/rakuensoftware/aimee-server:v0.2.41`).\n\nEach container runs as a non-root user. Durable state lives in **named volumes**,\nso `down`/recreate is safe and `down -v` is the only thing that erases data:\n\n| Volume | Holds |\n|--------|-------|\n| `*-postgres` | DB2 (`aimee_shared`): all shared knowledge + vectors |\n| `*-home` (`/var/lib/aimee`) | server/kb runtime state (DB1 SQLite, config) |\n| `*-workspaces` (`/var/lib/aimee-workspaces`) | mirror-tier bare mirrors + reconstructed worktrees |","doc_id":"8453a19e7db0c2bdbb794cc1","doc_kind":""}

The dominant `Write`/`Edit` path is covered\n  exactly; an inotify/fanotify watcher that closes the at-write gap is a **follow-up, not a\n  v1-correctness requirement** (R1 #3, R2 #4, R3 #2). This is stated, not hidden.\n- **Canonicalization is not byte-exact (R3 #1/#21).** We store a client-neutral\n  normalization and render per client, so a client re-reading its own write sees a\n  semantically-equivalent — not byte-identical — file. The render codec is audited for\n  round-trip fidelity (write→render→write→hash compare) and mismatches are logged; this is\n  the deliberate cost of cross-client sharing under one `(project,name)` key.\n- **Per-client deny contract is required (R3 #4/#10).** The deny-with-redirect is validated\n  per client; any client lacking a deny-with-message hook protocol is out of v1 scope and\n  listed as unsupported rather than silently mis-handled.\n- **DENY-as-success wording** depends on the model interpreting the reason correctly;\n  mitigated by live-run validation (R1 #14) but behavioral, not structural.\n- **Shared-memory content is untrusted.** Agent-authored bodies are stored and re-read by\n  other agents — a prompt-injection surface. Mitigations: body size cap, no auto-execution,\n  documented file perms; deeper review/tagging is a follow-up (R1 #22).","doc_id":"862b62d9c05695255feda569","doc_kind":""}

The legacy tables remain unchanged and read-only during the\ntransition.\n\nThe conceptual ownership is:\n\n- `rewind_change_sets`: execution/session/worktree identity, state, coverage, counts,\n  schema version, manifest hash, timestamps;\n- `rewind_preimages`: insert-only relative path, kind/mode/size/digest/blob ref,\n  sensitivity ruleset version;\n- `rewind_blob_refs`: the mutable active-retention edge from a set/entry to a blob;\n  expiry removes this edge only after the set becomes non-restorable, so immutable\n  preimage evidence can retain its digest and historical blob id without pinning bytes\n  forever;\n- `rewind_postimages`: insert-only sealed kind/mode/size/digest;\n- `rewind_operations`: bounded append-only tool evidence;\n- `rewind_restore_runs` and `rewind_restore_steps`: preview binding, durable apply journal,\n  compensation refs, per-step state, terminal outcome;\n- `rewind_worktree_leases`: DB1-backed root-identity lease with owner, fencing token,\n  heartbeat, and expiry, so a daemon replacement or offline maintenance process cannot\n  overlap restore with capture;\n- `rewind_incidents`: one-way security/integrity quarantine and acknowledgement state;\n- `rewind_blobs`: per-principal namespace, digest, size, refcount, lifecycle state.\n\nDB constraints/triggers prevent UPDATE/DELETE of sealed preimages, postimages, and\noperation evidence. State transitions use compare-and-swap updates. The implementation\nplan must include upgrade-from-current and downgrade/read-compatibility tests; it may not\nrely on the current best-effort ignored-`ALTER TABLE` loop for integrity-critical DDL.","doc_id":"8831fcb023cf1cc6e27f75d7","doc_kind":""}

They are\nrealized in code and enforced in review; their standalone proposal documents are\n**not currently in the tree** (see [Documentation integrity](#documentation-integrity)):\n\n1. **Architecture Charter** — fixes role division across neural, symbolic,\n   statistical, planning, and deterministic passes (Recall / Rerank / Rewrite /\n   Extract / Synthesize / Judge / Reflect / Classify-Score / Plan-Search / Reason /\n   Rank-Fuse / Calibrate / Detect-Cluster / Constrain-Verify / Evaluate-Optimize /\n   Gate-Promote / Enforce), one artifact schema, one audit schema, the sidecar\n   protocol, and evaluation/calibration discipline. Any new intelligence-surface\n   proposal must name its charter role(s).\n2. **Two-DB Split** — DB1 (SQLite, local user store) and DB2 (Postgres, shared\n   knowledge store) with a tier-pinned Data Access Layer; the boundary is\n   compile-enforced. The vector tier lives **inside DB2** as a pgvector extension\n   (folded in from a former Qdrant sidecar in #1575) — vectors share the same\n   connection and transaction domain as the rows they embed. See\n   [`STORAGE_TIERS.md`](STORAGE_TIERS.md).\n3. **Memory Public Contract** — the caller-facing memory contract (scope, filters,\n   typed mutation verbs, profile packs, stable `--explain`) shared across CLI, MCP,\n   and the aimee-kb `/v1/` API.","doc_id":"88cc5e357f371bb95b83af9e","doc_kind":""}

Storage tiers (the DB1 / DB2 boundary)\n\naimee has exactly **two storage tiers**. They are pinned ownership boundaries,\nnot user-selectable backends. See [`STORAGE_TIERS.md`](STORAGE_TIERS.md) for the\ncanonical statement; this section explains why the boundary exists and how it is\nenforced.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n    subgraph S[\"aimee-server\"]\n        D1code[\"src/db1/* (SQLite)\"]\n    end\n    subgraph K[\"aimee-kb\"]\n        D2code[\"src/db2/* (Postgres + pgvector)\"]\n    end\n    D1code --> DB1[(\"DB1 · SQLite<br/>~/.config/aimee/aimee.db\")]\n    D2code --> DB2[(\"DB2 · Postgres<br/>aimee_shared\")]\n    S -->|typed RPC, never SQL| K\n```\n\n| Tier | Backed by | Owned by | Holds |\n|------|-----------|----------|-------|\n| **DB1** | SQLite (`~/.config/aimee/aimee.db`) | local `aimee-server` (`src/db1/`) | Local, same-user runtime state: sessions, working-memory key/values, conversation windows, checkpoints, durable delegate jobs, eval results, local caches, local interaction/learning signals, secrets. |\n| **DB2** | Postgres + pgvector (`aimee_shared` by default) | `aimee-kb` (`src/db2/`) | Durable knowledge for the configured KB scope: memories, rules, KB metadata, tasks and decisions, code-index metadata, learning records, roadmaps, **plus** the dense vector collections derived from those records. |\n\nKey consequences of the split:\n\n- **DB1 is local.** `aimee-server` is a local, same-user process and DB1 holds\n  local information for that server: sessions, secrets, working memory,\n  checkpoints, local evidence, and operational state.\n- **DB2 can be local or shared.** `aimee-kb` owns the Postgres knowledge store.\n  In the default topology it can be a local single-user DB; in team or\n  multi-host topologies it can be a shared KB. In either case, only information\n  appropriate for the KB scope is reflected or promoted from DB1/server flows\n  into DB2.\n- **The vector tier is inside DB2.** It was originally a separate Qdrant sidecar\n  and was folded into Postgres as the `vector` (pgvector)","doc_id":"8902f6dbc278c9d7154f0202","doc_kind":""}

DB2 belongs to\n     aimee-kb and can be local or shared; local evidence is reflected or\n     promoted there only when it is appropriate for the configured KB scope.\n```","doc_id":"89456bdfcdf39b499fbc0dc0","doc_kind":""}

P1–P4 (DB1 store + routes/CLI + interception + session-start hydration) plus\n  the v1.1/v1.2 follow-ups (multi-client scope registry, spill durability + audit log,\n  Bash-write interception, full reconcile, config-file scope override, remote-server\n  project key, real-time inotify backstop) and two e2e-found fixes (#817 startup segfault,\n  #819 split-server wiring). Design history: roundtable reviews R1 (design, 28 items),\n  R2 (degraded), R3/R4 (clean) — see the \"Review revisions\" sections.\n- **Thesis:** An agent's *local, self-owned* memory (today: the Claude Code harness\n  file-memory at `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/*.md` + `MEMORY.md`, written via the\n  `Write`/`Edit` tools) should not be owned by the agent. aimee already hooks every\n  agent's tool calls cross-client; it should **intercept memory writes, persist them\n  centrally in the aimee-server database (DB1), and own the on-disk projection** so that\n  memory is shared per-project across all agents/sessions on the host, curatable, and\n  never silently owned by a single ephemeral agent.","doc_id":"8fbaac27f72125d20f78bf47","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:14813:{"content":"void cmd_hooks(app_ctx_t *ctx, int argc, char **argv)\n{\n   if (argc < 1)\n      fatal(\"hooks requires 'pre' or 'post'\");\n\n   const char *phase = argv[0];\n   argc--;\n   argv++;\n\n   config_t cfg;\n   config_load(&cfg);\n   audit_log_open();\n   audit_ensure_key(); /* provision the per-action audit key (best-effort) */\n\n   /* Read JSON from stdin -- hook input is small (tool name + args) */\n   char input[65536];\n   size_t total = 0;\n   while (total < sizeof(input) - 1)\n   {\n      ssize_t n = read(STDIN_FILENO, input + total, sizeof(input) - 1 - total);\n      if (n <= 0)\n         break;\n      total += (size_t)n;\n   }\n   input[total] = '\\0';\n\n   cJSON *json = cJSON_Parse(input);\n\n   char hook_sid[64] = \"\";\n   if (hook_payload_session_id(json, hook_sid, sizeof(hook_sid)))\n      session_id_set_override(hook_sid);\n\n   const char *tool_name = \"\";\n   char *tool_input_heap = NULL;\n   const char *tool_input = \"{}\";\n\n   if (json)\n   {\n      cJSON *tn = cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive(json, \"tool_name\");\n      if (cJSON_IsString(tn))\n         tool_name = tn->valuestring;\n\n      cJSON *ti = cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive(json, \"tool_input\");\n      if (cJSON_IsString(ti))\n         tool_input = ti->valuestring;\n      else if (cJSON_IsObject(ti) || cJSON_IsArray(ti))\n      {\n         tool_input_heap = cJSON_PrintUnformatted(ti);\n         tool_input = tool_input_heap;\n      }\n   }\n\n   /* DB1 owns its own connection; session_state_load/save delegate to DB1. */\n   if (db1_init(cfg.db1_path) != 0)\n      fatal(\"cannot open database\")","doc_id":"90645d27c8368378303fe2b8","doc_kind":"code_unit_body"}

Reuses DB1 `checkpoints`\n  for persistence.\n- **Hard-epoch rebirth.** When the window is force-reset, the wake seed is computed\n  deterministically from the rail + closet + sealed episodes — derived from the\n  trace, not model-summarized.","doc_id":"9247420f5ab3c86d1dae6c00","doc_kind":""}

This must be a DB1\ncheckpoint surface, not `/v1/runs`: the current `openai_runs_store` is a bounded,\nin-process live store and is not durable across restart. `/v1/runs` IDs are child\nexecution handles that may be stored in pass history, never the source of truth\nfor the pipeline.\n\nAimee already has a durable DB1 `pipelines` table for autopilot-style plan/job\nstate (`task`, `status`, `current_phase`, `plan_id`, `job_id`, attempts, and\nclassification). That schema is too narrow for this workflow, so implementation\nmust choose one explicit path:\n\n- create a namespaced `roundtable_pipeline_runs` table plus child\n  `roundtable_pipeline_passes` / `roundtable_pipeline_gates` tables; or\n- migrate/extend the existing `pipelines` table in a backwards-compatible way,\n  with the old autopilot actions continuing to work.\n\nEither way, the durable record holds:\n\n- pipeline id, state (§1), phase, admission class (`active` vs `parked` /\n  `waiting_human` if parked gates release the single active slot), created/updated\n  timestamps, and schema version (#48);\n- artifact refs: proposal path/blob/ref, implementation branch, diff ref or\n  chunk manifest, whole-origin ref/hash (working blob/path, db2 `docs` row, or\n  explicit artifact payload), review-chunk index refs (`kb_documents` rows if that\n  backend is used), and content hashes — not unbounded inline text as the primary\n  representation;\n- assembly manifests for orchestrator-built review units and aggregate checks:\n  selected origin/chunk span refs, ranges, hashes, input budget estimates, and\n  omitted candidate spans (#39);\n- the current brief plus compact gate digest;\n- per-pass history: each outer pass's status, aggregate child `run_id` if\n  single-call, `converged`, blocking/suggestion counts, `cost_usd`, `rounds_run`,\n  `best_round`, result hash, and any payload/chunk refs; for chunked passes, a","doc_id":"9369431d1dcb6d7e14bf6058","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:15110:{"content":"## Scaling contract: one server per user\n\n**`aimee-server` is strictly 1:1 with a user.** This is a design invariant, not a\ndeployment choice:\n\n- It owns **local, same-user runtime state** in DB1: sessions, working memory,\n  conversation windows, checkpoints, durable delegate jobs, secrets. That state is\n  private to one OS user on one host.\n- It authenticates callers by **`SO_PEERCRED`** (the connecting process's UID).\n  The trust model is \"same Unix user = same principal\"; there is no notion of a\n  remote tenant.\n- It is therefore **single-tenant and local by construction**. You do not shard\n  it, replicate it, or put it behind a load balancer. Each developer (each OS\n  login) runs exactly one `aimee-server` on their own machine, normally as a\n  systemd user unit or launchd agent.\n\nScale-out happens **below** the server, in the shared tier: many independent\n`aimee-server` instances (= many users) point at one shared `aimee-kb`/Postgres\ndeployment. The server is the per-user front; the KB is the many-user back. See\n[`src/kb/README.md`](../kb/README.md) for that side of the boundary.","doc_id":"937577b3dc6cbf3bc0c69f16","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:15193:{"content":"## P2 — server routes + codec + CLI (PR: `feat/harness-memory-p2`)\n\n**Files:** `src/server/harness_memory_routes.c` (ops) + `server.c`/`server_http_routes.inc`\nregistration; `src/harness_memory_codec.{c,h}` (`encode`/`decode`, not \"render\" — R1 #23);\n`src/server/harness_memory_store.{c,h}` (the serialized upsert+rematerialize writer + per-key\nlock); `src/cmd_harness_memory.c` + `cli_main.c`; tests for codec, routes, concurrency.\n\n**Ops/routes** (`rh_dispatch_op`): `harness_memory.{upsert,get,list,search,tombstone,\ntombstone_prefix,render,render_index}` → `/v1/harness_memory/{…}` with the contract-#4 caps.\nThe request carries `client` (from `AIMEE_HOOK_CLIENT`, defaulting `claude`); unknown client →\nidentity codec + a warn logged **at the route layer** (R1 #30).\n\n**Serialized write (R1 #4/#7/#8/#16).** `harness_memory_store_upsert(project,name,client,raw)`:\nacquire the **per-`(project,name)` lock** from a map guarded by its own map-mutex (lazy\ninsert); the per-key lock is an **rwlock** (reads don't block on same-key writes). Under the\nwrite lock: `decode`→canonical row, **server-side path validation** (realpath-chase, name\ncomponent check, `realpath(dirname) ⊂ realpath(memdir)` — same checks as P3, R1 #16),\n`hmem_upsert`, then rematerialize. This is **serialized, not transactional** (R1 #7): the DB\ncommit can succeed and the file write fail → P4 reconcile recovers the DB-without-file case.\n**Single-process model** is an invariant (one aimee-server owns DB1 + the file dir); a startup\nassert documents it (R1 #8). Rematerialize: `mkstemp` **in `dirname(target)`** → `fsync` →\n`rename` — always intra-directory so EXDEV cannot occur; the EXDEV branch is replaced with an\n**assert + audit** (R1 #13).\n\n**Codec:** `hmem_decode(client, raw_file, hmem_row_t*)` / `hmem_encode(client, row)→char*` /\n`hmem_encode_index(client, rows, n)→char*`. v1 `claude` (YAML frontmatter + body; MEMORY.md\nbullets). Round-trip audit helper used in tests; canonicalization is **not byte-exact**.","doc_id":"943417de16df67798f63e254","doc_kind":""}

The same routine is exposed\nas a **manual `aimee harness-memory reconcile`** command so a user can force a sync mid-\nsession without waiting for the next session-start (R4 #1).\n\n**Hook-independence + fail-loud (R4 #5).** Reconcile is **not** gated on the hook: it runs\nat session-start regardless, so on-disk state is always pulled into DB1 even if no hook is\ninstalled. Session-start additionally **verifies the memory hook is installed** and, if it\nis missing or mis-wired, emits a loud warning to the user (and an audit event, §7) that\n**at-write interception is OFF for this session — memory is import-only until the hook is\nrestored**. So a missing hook degrades to \"session-start import\" (no data loss), never to\nsilent escape. **Durability boundary:** only on-disk state present *at a reconcile* is\ncaptured; an external edit made and then reverted entirely within one session, between\nreconciles, is not observed (R4 #1) — documented, with the manual trigger as the mitigation.\n\n1. **Consume spills** first (§3): replay each well-formed spill envelope through the normal\n   server upsert/tombstone path, then delete it; partial spills are logged and skipped.\n2. **Deterministic, bidirectional reconcile (R3 #3/#5).** Compute each on-disk file's\n   canonical `content_hash` and compare to DB1, applying a single precedence rule:\n   - **DB1 row present, no file** → re-materialize from DB1 (covers a `rm`/bulk-delete the\n     hook missed; DB1 wins, so an un-intercepted delete is *restored*, not honored — the\n     supported way to delete is the intercepted path, §3).\n   - **File present, no DB1 row** → import it (one-time/orphan case, R1 #13/#27): canonicalize\n     and upsert, then re-materialize canonical.\n   - **Both present, hashes differ** → **DB1 wins**: overwrite the file from DB1 and log a\n     `reconcile-divergence` event (§7) naming the file. (An external edit never silently","doc_id":"976e265fa0fa368c65db8177","doc_kind":""}

So the recorded review-passed + roundtable-passed\n  advance events, and the deliver-advance itself, are the authoritative audit\n  chain; a *separate* surface event on the terminal executor would only duplicate\n  that. Not required for §8.\n- **INC 3b — cross-session resume-with-auth.** §4 states: *\"Primary disconnect /\n  crash mid-workflow: the work-item is orphaned, not lost — resumable by rebinding\n  (state is already durable in DB1).\"* That property is delivered by the shipped\n  same-session rebind (proposal_path=`interactive/<sid>` + resume-on-collision +\n  lease-reclaim). Resuming under a *different* re-attested principal is a\n  strictly-stronger enhancement **beyond the §4 text**; the auth-principal source\n  exists (SO_PEERCRED / attested `submitter`) but is not plumbed to the bind seam.\n  A future hardening, not a §4 gap.","doc_id":"98d619c9eeec28e98a7a2427","doc_kind":""}

Discovers and indexes the projects under every registered workspace.\n7. Ships with `code-review`, `debate`, `planning`, and `design-critique`\ntemplates; drop a project-local template in `ensemble_templates/` (the legacy\n`session_templates/` path still resolves). /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:16038:{"content":"### 10.3 Doctor integration\n\n`aimee doctor` includes a rewind summary. `aimee rewind doctor --json` exposes the same\nfindings with optional explicit `--repair`, `--quarantine`, and `--ack-incident` actions;\ndefault is report-only and every mutation supports dry-run.\n\nClassifications include:\n\n- `healthy`;\n- `recoverable_open` or `entry_count_mismatch`;\n- `missing_blob`, `hash_mismatch`, `orphan_blob`, `orphan_entry`;\n- `wrong_schema`;\n- `legacy_unverified`;\n- `root_identity_changed`, `path_resolution_denied`;\n- `restore_in_progress`, `compensation_required`, `restore_incident`.\n\nRepair may rebuild refcounts/indexes from immutable manifests, expire a set with missing\nbytes, or resume a journaled compensation. It may not invent bytes, rewrite a digest,\nguess a path, promote partial coverage, or silently delete evidence. Security path\nviolations enter one-way quarantine and require acknowledgement before the worktree\nunfreezes.\n\nStartup performs only a bounded read-only check of open/restore-in-progress rows and emits\nhealth state. Deep scans and repairs remain operator initiated, keeping DB1 initialization\npredictable. The appliance recovery runbook consumes these classifications rather than\nduplicating them.","doc_id":"9c6fd30fd9decc5520c9ddef","doc_kind":""}

The server's `/v1` is TLS-only off-loopback; `https://` works with certificate verification on by default (Schannel against the Windows cert store), so set `AIMEE_TLS_INSECURE=1` for the auto-provisioned self-signed cert (or trust/pin it). Alternatives to `aimee remote set`: set `AIMEE_SERVER_URL` / `AIMEE_SERVER_TOKEN` environment variables, or pass `--server https://YOUR_SERVER:8743 --server-token=...` per command. Result caching — ADOPT\n\n**Theirs.** `cache.py`: two SQLite layers, page text by URL and ranked results by\nquery key, lazy TTL expiry.\n\n**aimee.** No retrieval cache anywhere (`semcache|semantic_cache|retrieval_cache`\nreturns nothing). `tool_web_read` refetches on every call, including repeated\nreads of the same page inside one investigation.\n\nDB1 is already the local SQLite store. The design work is the key, not the\nstorage: it must include the query, the budget, and a policy version, or it is a\npage cache pretending to be a result cache. See\n[retrieval-result-cache-schema.md](retrieval-result-cache-schema.md).\n\n**Verdict: ADOPT.** Small-to-medium. Optional\nfeatures are pkg-config-gated: `-DWITH_PAM`, `-DWITH_LIBSECRET`. The version\nstring is embedded from `git describe`.\n\nBoundary gates (run in CI): `make check-linking` (no SQLite in client, no libpq\nin server, no SQLite in KB, verified with `ldd`/`otool` and `readelf` symbol\nchecks), `make module-boundary-check`, `make kb-target-isolation-check`,\n`make kb-container-packaging-check`, plus `scripts/check_tier_deps.sh` and\n`scripts/check-module-boundary.py`. Current Aimee state and concrete gaps\n\nThe shipped path is small and useful:\n\n- `src/server/agent_tools.c::agent_tools_begin_turn()` resets a thread-local snapshot id\n  for each internal model/tool round.\n- `src/posix/agent_tools_dispatch.c` calls `auto_snapshot_record()` before the anchored\n  edit, legacy edit, and write-file paths.\n- `src/posix/agent_tools.c::auto_snapshot_record()` creates one DB1 snapshot for that\n  internal round when `rewind.auto_snapshot` is enabled.\n- `src/db1/fsnap.c` stores absolute paths and inline bytes in `file_snapshots` /\n  `file_snapshot_entries`.\n- `src/cmd_rewind.c` reads and mutates local DB1 directly.\n- `webchat/chat.go::handleChatRewind()` is explicitly a branch-management stub.\n\nThe current behavior has seven correctness or ownership gaps:\n\n1. `db1_fsnap_record_file()` deletes and reinserts an existing entry. Two writes in one\n   snapshot preserve the intermediate state, not the first preimage. The existing\n   `test_record_overwrite_within_snapshot` test codifies this unsafe latest-wins behavior.\n2. Capture errors are ignored and the file mutation proceeds. The resulting checkpoint\n   does not record that coverage is incomplete.\n3. Snapshot grouping uses the internal model/tool-loop integer. A single server-owned\n   user turn may span several such rounds, so one UI turn can produce multiple unrelated\n   checkpoints and lose first-preimage semantics across them.\n4. Capture reads the server filesystem directly even when file mutation routes through\n   `workspace_provider_active()`. A detached or container-bound turn can therefore\n   snapshot the wrong filesystem.\n5. Restore follows stored absolute paths, has no owner/worktree check, no no-follow\n   resolver, no current-state compare-and-swap, no whole-set journal, and can report a\n   partially applied restore only as “with errors.”\n6. `aimee rewind` is a stateful direct-DB CLI, so a thin client can inspect a different\n   DB1 than the server that owns its session.\n7. `--no-restore` deletes DB1 context windows and labels that action “conversation","doc_id":"a6bd7ab608f6e8f05c65176e","doc_kind":""}

But the deeper fact is that\n  **every** UDS HTTP client is indistinguishable: `server_http_authorize` returns\n  0 for `!is_tcp` (\"UDS: filesystem-permission auth, no token\") and\n  `server_http_conn_caps` grants `CAPS_ALL`, so the thin CLI, MCP, and webchat all\n  arrive as anonymous trusted-local with no caller identity. Notably the **HTTP-\n  over-UDS path captures no peer identity, whereas the legacy NDJSON socket already\n  derives `uid:<peer_uid>`** (`server_auth.c:263-265`). Two complementary fixes:\n  (a) capture the UDS peer UID on accept as a baseline principal (parity with\n  NDJSON), and (b) require forwarding proxies — webchat first — to stamp trusted\n  internal headers for source, principal/session, original request id, and\n  idempotency. Attribution cannot rely on the forwarded HTTP request alone. **Both\n  are net-new code:** `handle_conn` never calls `platform_ipc_peer_cred()` today\n  (it exists but is uncalled on the HTTP path), and there is no trusted-peer\n  allowlist — so distinguishing a trusted proxy (webchat) from an arbitrary UDS\n  peer, and gating forwarded-header acceptance on it, must be built before any\n  forwarded source/principal is trusted (it is a security prerequisite, not a\n  config knob). A UID allowlist by itself is insufficient in a same-user local\n  deploy (proxy and arbitrary clients share a UID) — though in the container\n  deploy webchat is root and the server is uid 1000, so UID *can* separate them\n  there. The robust cross-deploy answer is a proxy credential, and aimee already\n  ships the pattern: webchat reads `$AIMEE_HOME/server.token`, so reuse that\n  shared-secret/HMAC rather than invent a new factor.\n- **DB1 is a single shared SQLite handle, and audit writes are best-effort.** DB1\n  is one process-wide `sqlite3*` (`db1_init.c:19`) opened `SQLITE_OPEN_FULLMUTEX`\n  with `journal_mode=WAL` and a busy handler that retries 15× (20–150 ms) then","doc_id":"a776dbc7daf111e942bc0906","doc_kind":""}

The fold function does not touch prefix state.\n4. **provider-shape normalization**: runtime renders the step-3 view into the active\n   provider shape (Anthropic content blocks / OpenAI `tool_calls` / Gemini `parts`)\n   into a **runtime-owned byte buffer**, with the **atomic tool-pair** rule (a\n   `tool_use`+`tool_result` fold together or not at all; folded regions are plain\n   non-tool text).
