/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:17651:{"content":"### Scaling and multi-user deployment\n\nScaling follows the storage boundary: per-user state and shared knowledge live in\ndifferent processes and scale differently.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph Users[\"Many users / machines\"]\n        S1[\"aimee-server (user A)<br/>DB1 · SQLite (local)\"]\n        S2[\"aimee-server (user B)<br/>DB1 · SQLite (local)\"]\n        S3[\"aimee-server (user C)<br/>DB1 · SQLite (local)\"]\n    end\n    LB[\"Load balancer<br/>HTTP :8741\"]\n    subgraph KB[\"aimee-kb replicas (stateless)\"]\n        K1[\"aimee-kb\"]\n        K2[\"aimee-kb\"]\n        K3[\"aimee-kb\"]\n    end\n    PG[(\"PostgreSQL · aimee_shared<br/>pgvector → pgvectorscale at scale\")]\n\n    S1 --> LB\n    S2 --> LB\n    S3 --> LB\n    LB --> K1\n    LB --> K2\n    LB --> K3\n    K1 --> PG\n    K2 --> PG\n    K3 --> PG\n```\n\n- **`aimee-server` is 1:1 with a user.** It owns local same-user state (DB1/SQLite)\n  and authenticates by peer UID, so each developer runs exactly one server on their\n  own machine. Single-tenant and local by design; never sharded or replicated.\n- **`aimee-kb` is the shared, horizontally-scalable tier.** All durable state lives\n  in Postgres; a KB process is otherwise a stateless request server plus background\n  workers. One KB deployment serves many `aimee-server` instances; scale it by\n  running **multiple `aimee-kb` replicas behind a load balancer** on HTTP `:8741`.\n  The ingest/curator workers coordinate purely through Postgres\n  (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), so adding replicas needs no external coordinator.\n- **The database is standard Postgres.** Knowledge rows and their vector embeddings\n  live in one database (`aimee_shared`) with the `pg_trgm` and `vector` (pgvector)\n  extensions. Scale it like any Postgres: bigger instance, pooling, read replicas.\n  For large vector corpora add **`pgvectorscale`** (StreamingDiskANN) on top of\n  pgvector, with identical data and queries, so switching is a reindex, not a migration.\n  Small and local installs stay on plain pgvector (HNSW).","doc_id":"abc57720cc0f78b378ca93ab","doc_kind":""}

(The\n   original draft asked the test to fail against the stock endpoint; that was\n   unachievable, since the stock build has no `/v1/ready` to point it at. A dependency probe exceeding its timeout is reported `fail`/`timeout`, and a\n   test asserts the handler's own latency stays bounded and independent of that\n   probe's duration — i.e. the request path did no I/O.\n7. `server_http.c`'s existing unit test gains no new dependency linkage. With no\n   provider registered, `/v1/ready` reports `unknown`/503.\n8. The route, its schema, and the 200-vs-503 boundary are added to the OpenAPI\n   surface, and generated docs regenerate cleanly.","doc_id":"abdc30cc597efc6e39f95fb0","doc_kind":""}

The **primary agent** is the AI coding surface the user interacts with (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, direct Codex, direct Mistral, Codex CLI legacy mode, Mistral Vibe, GitHub Copilot). aimee integrates through hooks, provider-CLI adapters, or direct primary-session adapters, intercepting tool calls, injecting memory and rules, enforcing guardrails, and managing session isolation. **Delegate agents** are sub-agents configured in `agents.json` that handle offloaded work via `aimee delegate <role> <prompt>`.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph Primary[\"Primary Agent Integration\"]\n        PA[Claude Code / Gemini / Codex / Vibe / Copilot]\n        SS[SessionStart<br/>Load rules, assemble context,<br/>create worktrees]\n        Pre[PreToolUse<br/>Classify path, check plan mode,<br/>worktree enforce, anti-patterns]\n        Post[PostToolUse<br/>Re-index edited files]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Core[\"aimee Core\"]\n        Mem[(DB2 Knowledge<br/>local/shared KB scope<br/>memories, rules, tasks)]\n        Vec[(pgvector<br/>memory + KB indexes)]\n        Guard[Guardrails<br/>Path classification,<br/>sensitive file blocking]\n        Idx[Code Index<br/>Symbol lookup,<br/>blast radius]\n        Rules[Rules Engine<br/>Feedback-derived rules]\n        WM[DB1 Local State<br/>sessions, windows, caches]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Delegate[\"Delegate Agent System\"]\n        Router[Agent Router<br/>Cost-based selection]\n        Loop[Tool-use Loop<br/>bash, read, write]\n        HTTP[HTTP Client<br/>OpenAI / ChatGPT / Anthropic]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Server[\"Server\"]\n        Srv[aimee-server<br/>HTTP /v1<br/>UDS + optional TCP]\n        MCP[aimee mcp-serve<br/>Stdio MCP server]\n    end\n\n    PA --> SS\n    PA --> Pre\n    PA --> Post\n    SS --> Mem\n    SS --> Rules\n    Pre --> Guard\n    Pre --> Idx\n    Post --> Idx\n    Mem --> Vec\n    Router --> HTTP\n    Router --> Loop\n    Srv --> Core\n    MCP --> Core\n```","doc_id":"ac48e072a57566d0e866f570","doc_kind":""}

The product must\nsay **journaled compensating restore**, not atomic restore.\n\nBefore the first target write:\n\n1. acquire the DB1-backed per-worktree lease, retain its fencing token through every\n   journal update, and prove no turn is active for the session/worktree;\n2. authorize and no-follow-resolve every manifest path;\n3. verify root/provider identity, blob integrity, free space, same-device constraints,\n   and compare-and-swap tuples;\n4. capture the current state of every manifest target as a terminal compensation set;\n5. durably write `rewind_restore_runs` and every ordered step as `STAGED`;\n6. prepare same-filesystem, fd-relative temp objects and `fsync` them.\n\nCommit processes paths in deterministic order, using fd-relative rename/unlink, with file\nand parent-directory `fsync` after each rename group. Each completed step is journaled.\nThe fencing token is revalidated immediately before every target mutation; an expired or\nsuperseded owner cannot continue applying after daemon replacement.\nOnly after all filesystem steps land does one DB1 transaction mark the operational result\n`RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING` and enqueue a stable audit event id. The common audit bridge then\nappends that event to its separate sink and a final DB1 compare-and-swap marks `RESTORED`.\nThis does not pretend SQLite and the WORM/file audit sink share a transaction. Because the\ncurrent append-only sinks have no idempotency key, crash recovery is explicitly\nat-least-once: doctor retries the same event id and readers collapse duplicate terminal\nevents by that id. A future authoritative sink may add native deduplication or require\ncompensation on audit failure; this proposal does not claim cross-store exactly-once.\n\nOn a normal apply failure, the same journal drives compensation in reverse order. A crash\nleaves `RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS`; doctor can deterministically resume compensation from the","doc_id":"ae38e28a09dd4d24a68e93ee","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18053:{"content":"## Acceptance criteria\n\n- An org call writes a **DB2 `org_token_audit`** row carrying resolved\n  `team_id`/`project_id`; a personal `direct` call writes to the **server's DB1\n  `token_audit`** unchanged (that table has no team/project columns — the org\n  dimension exists only in DB2).\n- `/v1/insights/spend?team=X` returns that team's realized spend, per project\n  and per model, matching the sum of its rows.\n- A team lead can read their team's spend; cannot read another team's (authz).\n- `--json` export round-trips; totals reconcile with `_by_model`.\n- Every kb instance prices a given `(model, version)` identically from the DB2\n  `org_model_pricing` table; a price update is observed as a new version, never a\n  mid-flight change to an in-flight call's price.","doc_id":"af4b37dffe4ed60ce7b3badb","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18057:{"content":"## 1. Design goals\n\naimee is a local-first memory, safety, and delegation layer that sits between a\ndeveloper's AI coding tool and the work it performs. Its architecture is shaped\nby four hard constraints:\n\n1. **Invisible latency.** Hooks run in the critical path of every file edit, so\n   the client must start and respond in milliseconds. This drives the thin\n   client / persistent server split: a process that pays no database or\n   connection cost on startup.\n2. **Pinned storage ownership.** Knowledge must outlive any single session and\n   may need to be shared across tools or hosts, while same-user runtime state\n   stays local, private, and fast. This drives the DB1 / DB2 tier split with\n   strict, compile-enforced ownership.\n3. **Zero cloud dependencies for the core.** Everything required to run aimee,\n   memory, guardrails, indexing, delegation routing, works on the local\n   machine. External model providers are reached only when the user explicitly\n   delegates.\n4. **One install, many tools.** The same server backs Claude Code, Gemini CLI,\n   Codex CLI, Mistral Vibe, and GitHub Copilot, so integration logic lives in\n   one place and switching tools preserves all memory and context.\n\n---","doc_id":"af675bc55518a9efff3e733b","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18124:{"content":"## Cross-cutting guardrails (apply to every packet)\n\n- **Uphold the ten invariants** in the master plan's \"Security & transport invariants\" — reviewers check each PR against them, **including #9 (stateless kb / Postgres source of truth / atomic-on-primary) and #10 (Postgres hardened, ciphertext-only at rest)**.\n- **Postgres hardening (invariant #10) is delivered by P1 as foundation** and extended by later migrations: `verify-full` + replica TLS on every kb↔Postgres connection, separate migration vs. runtime DB roles (runtime role = DML on its own schemas, no DDL/superuser), mandatory team-scoped predicates / row-level security on tenant tables, and encrypted backups + WAL. Every packet that adds a DB2 table (P1 teams, P3 audit, P4 budgets, P5 registry, P7 vault) ships its tenant-isolation predicate and its migration/runtime-role grants with it, tested.\n- **kb tier = Postgres/DB2; server tier = SQLite/DB1.** Never put multi-tenant state on the server. New shared tables are DB2, behind the KB service (server/CLI must not touch DB2 directly).\n- **Migrations are first-class and reversible.** Additive columns, backfill, and a down path. Follow the `agent_load_config` identity-cache pattern (PR #1372) so a refreshed roster/config is never served stale.\n- **Every new `/v1` route** is added to OpenAPI and `v1-method-coverage` (conformance-tested), not a side door, and gated by an explicit capability.\n- **Streaming:** build kb egress + Bedrock stream-clean from the start — honor the buffered-replay vs. true-stream distinction (`stream=false` on the non-responses buffered-replay wire); add a deterministic streaming probe per packet that touches egress.","doc_id":"b0036b6e6051282ba2541718","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18132:{"content":"## Delta 2 — Per-action policy-verdict audit (enrich the audit call that already fires)\n\n**Problem.** The only genuinely *partial* pillar. `db1_lifecycle_event_add()` records\n*workflow-stage* decisions with attribution; `trajectory_export.c` replays interactions — but the\ngeneral governed **tool-call** stream is only coarsely logged. Sechroom's \"checked at the point of\naction and **recorded with its verdict** … so a sequence can be replayed\" holds for workflow stages,\nnot per tool call.\n\n**Build (enrich the existing `audit_log()` call, single sink, off the enforcement path).**\n- The block sites in `pre_tool_check()` **already call `audit_log(stable_key, …)`** (§G1). Enrich\n  that existing JSON row with the structured fields: `{ts, actor, tool, args_hash, mode,\n  reason_code, verdict}`. Add **one** `audit_log()` call on the allow path (`return 0`,\n  `guardrails_orchestrator.c:1999`) so allows are audited too. **One sink** = the existing\n  `audit.log` (already JSON lines, 0600, rotated) — no DB1 write, no second surface (§Disposition\n  D2c, D2e).\n- **`reason_code`, not prose** = the stable event key that already exists (`read_before_write`,\n  `stale_edit`, …). Free-form `msg_buf` is **never persisted** — kills the reason-PII finding\n  (§Disposition D2b).\n- **Fail-open by construction.** `audit_log()` is side-effect-only logging invoked *after* the int\n  verdict is decided; a log failure cannot alter the returned `0/1/2`. State this as an invariant:\n  **audit loss is acceptable, enforcement drift is not** (§Disposition D2a). No hot-path\n  transactional write → the perf finding is moot (§Disposition D2d).\n- **`args_hash` = keyed HMAC over a pinned canonicalization**, not a bare digest of low-entropy\n  args: reuse the server-secret HMAC that `wfe_approval` already uses; canonical form = sorted-key\n  JSON with a static volatile-field redaction allow-list (drop timestamps/request-ids/tokens);\n  version the scheme (`args_hash_v1`). Raw args and any arg-bearing prose never enter the row","doc_id":"b015c8e0f104b7cb0c8293c1","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18147:{"content":"## Observability\n\n- **Webchat Workflow Actions page**, live progress per work item: current stage, gate\n  verdicts, parked state, and the actionable approve/reject controls for human\n  gates.\n- **Event stream**, a run publishes its full turn stream (text, tool calls,\n  usage, boundaries) to the presence event ring; the webchat replays it live and,\n  after a disconnect, from a cursor.\n- **Durable audit**, every step, verdict, and cost is recorded in the DB1\n  `lifecycle_*` tables (per work item), including the commit hashes produced and\n  the gate decisions. This is the source of truth for \"what did the run do\".\n- **Attribution**, autonomous commits and PRs are attributed to the run and\n  carry **no** AI co-authorship trailers.","doc_id":"b043ec3edf7b3643f705b606","doc_kind":""}

The single\nbiggest simplification: **v1 audit writes are SYNCHRONOUS** — one `token_audit`\ninsert on the handler thread after the provider returns. A local DB1 insert is\nsub-millisecond against a multi-second LLM call, so it does not meaningfully load\nthe hot path, and synchronicity dissolves the entire async-queue blocker class\n(B1) and the reward-barrier (B7). The `ingress_audit_async` queue is **deferred to\na later, separately-gated phase**, and may only ship with the durability spec in\nB1.\n\n**B1 — Async audit queue overflow/backpressure (§2).** v1 has no queue: writes are\nsynchronous (above). The deferred async phase, if ever justified by a measured\nhot-path regression, MUST specify: a bounded queue (default 4096 rows); a\nblock-up-to-25ms-then-drop policy; a monotonic `ingress_audit_dropped_total` metric\nsurfaced to operators; and an explicit durability contract — \"best-effort: rows are\ndropped, never duplicated; drops are counted.\" Synchronous v1 is exactly-once\n(idempotent insert, B4).\n\n**B2 — Dedup confidentiality leak via shared webchat principal (§4).** The dedup\nkey MUST include the resolved principal/tenant id, and dedup is **fail-closed\ndisabled** for any request whose principal is shared/service (the anonymous\n`webchat` service principal, or any principal flagged `shared`). Two logged-out\nwebchat users can therefore never be cross-served. v1 dedup is enabled ONLY for\nrequests carrying a non-shared, authenticated per-user identity. Test: a request\nwith a shared principal is never served from the dedup cache, even on identical\nbody.\n\n**B3 — Backfill-from-`tool_name` misprices history (§2).** Do **not** backfill the\nmodel from `tool_name` (agent names are not pricing keys, §2a). Both are additive, reversible\nmigrations (master-plan constraint) — org rows never go into the server's DB1 table.\n\nEach org row also carries the **authoritative originating server `cert:CN`** and,\nseparately, the **user identity only when a kb-verified actor token was present** (else\nnull — invariant #7's composite tagging, immutable fields). Every billable call\nproduces **exactly one** row via the durable request lifecycle of P2/P4/P7. The row's\nidempotency/uniqueness key is the **composite `(origin_cert_cn, request_id)`** (a bare\nrequest_id could collide/replay across mutually-untrusted origins), and the first\naccepted request binds the immutable team/project/pricing-version. Terminal and not restorable;\n  blob refs are released.\n- `INVALID`: capture, coverage, identity, evidence, or integrity failure. Terminal and\n  never shown as safe.\n- `RECOVERABLE_OPEN`: startup/doctor classification only; no automatic restore.\n- `SEALED_INCOMPLETE`: an interrupted turn with fully verifiable mutated entries. It may\n  be previewed but restore remains an explicit operator action.\n- `SEALED`: immutable manifest and final postimages exist.\n- `RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS`: durable restore journal written before the first filesystem\n  mutation.\n- `RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING`: filesystem and DB1 operational state committed, but the\n  separate audit sink has not yet acknowledged the terminal event. Doctor retries the\n  bounded event; this state is never reported as fully complete.\n- `RESTORED`: requested entries and audit outcome committed.\n- `RESTORE_INCIDENT`: apply or compensation could not converge automatically. The\n  worktree is write-frozen at `mutation_begin` until operator acknowledgement.\n- `EXPIRED`: manifest retained; one or more required blobs were policy-pruned.\n\nNo state transition makes a sealed manifest mutable. A later restore attempt receives a\nnew restore-run id and journal.","doc_id":"b44405d42c8b6819387c9992","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:18987:{"content":"## Durable server cache and refresh policy\n\nUse DB1 as the server-local authority so cache bytes and the monotonic generation/HWM commit atomically with the existing FULLMUTEX/WAL transaction gate and backup lifecycle. Add an immutable generation row plus singleton current pointer bound to generation, validity, exact JWKS/payload/envelope bytes and digests, previous/manifest digests, manifest id/public-root digest, trust-bundle digest, and fetch time. A `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction validates current state, inserts only an absent byte-identical generation, and advances the singleton pointer atomically. Commit ambiguity is unavailable; it never authorizes from presumed state. DB1 unavailable, busy, corrupt, inconsistent, or constraint failure denies and clears output.\n\nAt startup, after DB1 initialization and before listener acceptance, validate the configured trust bundle and any cached row. One authenticated refresh is allowed when configured. Consumer authorization uses the exact half-open interval `valid_from <= now && now < valid_until`; it grants no clock-skew extension beyond signed times. A refresh should be scheduled before expiry, but failure may continue using the artifact only until `valid_until`. Startup outage is nonfatal only if the cache is already cryptographically valid and currently in that interval; an empty or stale cache leaves management authorization unavailable and emits a bounded operator warning/availability metric without artifact or token bytes. This slice does not make the server data plane unavailable, and the existing unconditional `/v1/management/action` 503 remains unchanged regardless of cache state.\n\nExpose a cache lookup/refresh orchestrator with a single-flight mutex/condition. A known `kid` uses a currently valid cache without network. An empty cache or a strictly well-formed cache missing an otherwise valid token header `kid` makes exactly one authenticated mTLS fetch; concurrent waiters share that attempt; the verifier retries once and then rejects. A malformed JWKS, token header, signature, or claims is INVALID and never triggers network access. Transient fetch failure never deletes or replaces the last valid cache, but an expired/not-yet-valid cache cannot authorize.","doc_id":"b83d78e2739f210cb6f67d97","doc_kind":""}

Dynamic-alpha fusion and\ningest-lab are retrieval-quality polish on that stack. A team\n  lead sees their own team; an org admin sees all (reuse P1 resolution).\n- Extend `CostPanel` with a team/project breakdown on the org tier view;\n  `--json` export for finance.\n- CLI: `aimee spend --team X [--project Y] [--since …]` reports **org** spend by calling kb's `/v1/insights/spend` over mTLS — the CLI runs on the *server*, which **never queries DB2 directly** (storage boundary); kb is the only tier that touches org rows. A user's personal `direct` spend stays in the server's local `token_audit` and is shown by the existing local cost surfaces; the two are **not silently merged**. A combined \"everything I spent\" view, if offered, dedupes by tier (org rows are DB2, personal rows are the server's DB1 — no overlap) and labels each source.","doc_id":"bea9c6a668c9d1e7a7bc709f","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:19664:{"content":"### Authentication and capabilities\n\nThe local `/v1` UDS (`aimee-http.sock`) is filesystem-permission gated and fully\ntrusted: it reaches the entire dispatch surface with no token. The optional TCP\nlistener requires a configured bearer token (`server_http_authorize`,\nconstant-time compare). Authorization is a 16-bit capability mask declared per\nmethod in a registry (`src/server/server_auth.c`); unknown methods default to\ndeny, and TCP connections are capability-scoped.\n\n| Flag | Bit | Grants |\n|------|-----|--------|\n| `CAP_CHAT` | 0x0001 | chat streaming |\n| `CAP_DELEGATE` | 0x0002 | delegate / inference |\n| `CAP_TOOL_EXECUTE` | 0x0004 | tool invocation |\n| `CAP_TOOL_BASH` | 0x0008 | bash tool |\n| `CAP_TOOL_WRITE` | 0x0010 | file-write tools |\n| `CAP_MEMORY_READ` | 0x0020 | memory recall/search |\n| `CAP_MEMORY_WRITE` | 0x0040 | memory store |\n| `CAP_RULES_READ` | 0x0080 | rules list |\n| `CAP_RULES_ADMIN` | 0x0100 | rules delete/approve |\n| `CAP_DESCRIBE_READ` | 0x0200 | graph describe |\n| `CAP_DESCRIBE_ADMIN` | 0x0400 | graph describe mutation |\n| `CAP_INDEX_READ` | 0x0800 | code-index reads |\n| `CAP_INDEX_ADMIN` | 0x1000 | index scan/rebuild |\n| `CAP_SESSION_READ` | 0x2000 | session / wm reads |\n| `CAP_SESSION_ADMIN` | 0x4000 | session / tool mutation |\n| `CAP_DASHBOARD_READ` | 0x8000 | dashboard metrics |\n\nComposite sets exist for authenticated (all-but-index-admin) and read-only\ncallers. Auth failures are rate-limited per UID (5 / 60 s → cooldown); the HTTP\nsurface can rate-limit per source. SIGTERM/SIGINT drain pending I/O and record\nunclean-exit forensics (`shutdown_forensics.c`) to DB1.","doc_id":"becc637277ce2ea7dce6e423","doc_kind":""}

Current Aimee state and concrete gaps\n\nThe shipped path is small and useful:\n\n- `src/server/agent_tools.c::agent_tools_begin_turn()` resets a thread-local snapshot id\n  for each internal model/tool round.\n- `src/posix/agent_tools_dispatch.c` calls `auto_snapshot_record()` before the anchored\n  edit, legacy edit, and write-file paths.\n- `src/posix/agent_tools.c::auto_snapshot_record()` creates one DB1 snapshot for that\n  internal round when `rewind.auto_snapshot` is enabled.\n- `src/db1/fsnap.c` stores absolute paths and inline bytes in `file_snapshots` /\n  `file_snapshot_entries`.\n- `src/cmd_rewind.c` reads and mutates local DB1 directly.\n- `webchat/chat.go::handleChatRewind()` is explicitly a branch-management stub.\n\nThe current behavior has seven correctness or ownership gaps:\n\n1. `db1_fsnap_record_file()` deletes and reinserts an existing entry. Two writes in one\n   snapshot preserve the intermediate state, not the first preimage. The existing\n   `test_record_overwrite_within_snapshot` test codifies this unsafe latest-wins behavior.\n2. Capture errors are ignored and the file mutation proceeds. The resulting checkpoint\n   does not record that coverage is incomplete.\n3. Snapshot grouping uses the internal model/tool-loop integer. A single server-owned\n   user turn may span several such rounds, so one UI turn can produce multiple unrelated\n   checkpoints and lose first-preimage semantics across them.\n4. Capture reads the server filesystem directly even when file mutation routes through\n   `workspace_provider_active()`. A detached or container-bound turn can therefore\n   snapshot the wrong filesystem.\n5. Restore follows stored absolute paths, has no owner/worktree check, no no-follow\n   resolver, no current-state compare-and-swap, no whole-set journal, and can report a\n   partially applied restore only as “with errors.”\n6. `aimee rewind` is a stateful direct-DB CLI, so a thin client can inspect a different\n   DB1 than the server that owns its session.\n7. `--no-restore` deletes DB1 context windows and labels that action “conversation","doc_id":"c2bbf9dcfca2016e01731bd3","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:20098:{"content":"### 27.5 Scaling and multi-user deployment\n\naimee's scaling model follows its storage boundary exactly. The two tiers scale\ndifferently *by design*, and understanding which is which is the whole story:\n\n| Tier | Scope | How it scales |\n|------|-------|---------------|\n| `aimee-server` | **1:1 with a user** | Vertical only. One server per OS login, on that user's machine. |\n| `aimee-kb` | **Many users** | Horizontal. N stateless replicas behind a load balancer over one Postgres. |\n| Postgres (DB2) | The shared substrate | Standard Postgres scaling: instance sizing, pooling, read replicas; pgvector → pgvectorscale for large vector corpora. |\n\n#### `aimee-server` is one-per-user\n\n`aimee-server` owns DB1, the local, same-user runtime state (sessions, working\nmemory, conversation windows, checkpoints, jobs, secrets), and authenticates\ncallers by `SO_PEERCRED` peer UID. Its trust model is \"same Unix user = same\nprincipal.\" It is therefore **single-tenant and local by construction**: you do\nnot shard it, replicate it, or place it behind a load balancer. Each developer\n(each OS login) runs exactly one `aimee-server`, normally as a systemd user unit\nor launchd agent. You scale a single user's server *vertically* (more in-flight\ndelegates and parallel tool calls) with the thread-pool and concurrency knobs in\n[§27.4](#274-resource-tuning); that does not, and is not meant to, make it serve\nother users.\n\n#### `aimee-kb` is the horizontally-scalable, many-user tier\n\n`aimee-kb` owns DB2 and is where multi-user scale-out lives. Three properties make\nit horizontally scalable:\n\n1. **State lives in Postgres, not in the process.** A KB instance holds only\n   transient state (connection pools, request buffers, worker loops); all durable\n   knowledge is in DB2. Each instance is effectively a **stateless request server\n   over a shared database**.\n2. **It is reachable over the network.** KB serves its full `/v1` contract over\n   HTTP on `:8741` (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`, optional bearer token via","doc_id":"c2cfbbe41b46daf845de4c78","doc_kind":""}

Concepts and mental model\n\n**Primary agent vs delegate agent.** The *primary agent* is the AI coding\nsurface you interact with (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Vibe, Copilot, or\naimee's own chat). aimee integrates with it through hooks, provider-CLI\nadapters, or direct primary-session adapters. *Delegate agents* are sub-agents\nconfigured in `agents.json` that handle offloaded work via\n`aimee delegate <role> <prompt>`.\n\n**The two storage tiers.** DB1 (SQLite, owned by the local `aimee-server`) holds\nsame-user runtime state, sessions, working memory, conversation windows,\ncheckpoints, jobs, local signal streams, and secrets. DB2 (Postgres + pgvector,\nowned by `aimee-kb`) holds durable knowledge, memories, rules, the code index,\ntasks/decisions, and the vector embeddings of all of it. DB2 can run locally for\none user or as a shared KB; only knowledge that is appropriate for its configured\nscope is reflected or promoted there from local server state. The boundary is\npinned and compile-enforced; you never choose a different backend for either\ntier. It is also the **scaling boundary**: `aimee-server` is one-per-user, while\n`aimee-kb` and its Postgres are the shared, horizontally-scalable tier (see\n[§27.5](#275-scaling-and-multi-user-deployment)). See\n[`docs/STORAGE_TIERS.md`](docs/STORAGE_TIERS.md).\n\n**Memory tiers (L0-L3).** Stored knowledge moves through four lifetimes: L0\nsession scratch, L1 recent (≈30 days), L2 long-term stable facts, L3 episodic\n(past attempts/outcomes with decay). Promotion and decay are automatic. This is\n*different* from the storage tiers above, L0-L3 is the *semantic* lifecycle of a\nmemory; DB1/DB2 is *where bytes live*.\n\n**Sessions and worktrees.** Each session gets its own git worktree, branch, and\nstate file, so parallel sessions never collide. Guardrails redirect writes that\ntarget a workspace path with an active worktree.\n\n**Hooks.** aimee registers `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, and `PostToolUse`\nhooks with your tool. The **primary agent** is the AI coding surface the user interacts with (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, direct Codex, direct Mistral, Codex CLI legacy mode, Mistral Vibe, GitHub Copilot). aimee integrates through hooks, provider-CLI adapters, or direct primary-session adapters, intercepting tool calls, injecting memory and rules, enforcing guardrails, and managing session isolation. **Delegate agents** are sub-agents configured in `agents.json` that handle offloaded work via `aimee delegate <role> <prompt>`.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph Primary[\"Primary Agent Integration\"]\n        PA[Claude Code / Gemini / Codex / Vibe / Copilot]\n        SS[SessionStart<br/>Load rules, assemble context,<br/>create worktrees]\n        Pre[PreToolUse<br/>Classify path, check plan mode,<br/>worktree enforce, anti-patterns]\n        Post[PostToolUse<br/>Re-index edited files]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Core[\"aimee Core\"]\n        Mem[(DB2 Knowledge<br/>local/shared KB scope<br/>memories, rules, tasks)]\n        Vec[(pgvector<br/>memory + KB indexes)]\n        Guard[Guardrails<br/>Path classification,<br/>sensitive file blocking]\n        Idx[Code Index<br/>Symbol lookup,<br/>blast radius]\n        Rules[Rules Engine<br/>Feedback-derived rules]\n        WM[DB1 Local State<br/>sessions, windows, caches]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Delegate[\"Delegate Agent System\"]\n        Router[Agent Router<br/>Cost-based selection]\n        Loop[Tool-use Loop<br/>bash, read, write]\n        HTTP[HTTP Client<br/>OpenAI / ChatGPT / Anthropic]\n    end\n\n    subgraph Server[\"Server\"]\n        Srv[aimee-server<br/>HTTP /v1<br/>UDS + optional TCP]\n        MCP[aimee mcp-serve<br/>Stdio MCP server]\n    end\n\n    PA --> SS\n    PA --> Pre\n    PA --> Post\n    SS --> Mem\n    SS --> Rules\n    Pre --> Guard\n    Pre --> Idx\n    Post --> Idx\n    Mem --> Vec\n    Router --> HTTP\n    Router --> Loop\n    Srv --> Core\n    MCP --> Core\n```","doc_id":"ca9ec59d6d733fd789f909b0","doc_kind":""}

Session-start additionally **verifies the memory hook is installed** and, if it\nis missing or mis-wired, emits a loud warning to the user (and an audit event, §7) that\n**at-write interception is OFF for this session — memory is import-only until the hook is\nrestored**. The optional TCP\nlistener requires a configured bearer token (`server_http_authorize`,\nconstant-time compare). Authorization is a 16-bit capability mask declared per\nmethod in a registry (`src/server/server_auth.c`); unknown methods default to\ndeny, and TCP connections are capability-scoped.\n\n| Flag | Bit | Grants |\n|------|-----|--------|\n| `CAP_CHAT` | 0x0001 | chat streaming |\n| `CAP_DELEGATE` | 0x0002 | delegate / inference |\n| `CAP_TOOL_EXECUTE` | 0x0004 | tool invocation |\n| `CAP_TOOL_BASH` | 0x0008 | bash tool |\n| `CAP_TOOL_WRITE` | 0x0010 | file-write tools |\n| `CAP_MEMORY_READ` | 0x0020 | memory recall/search |\n| `CAP_MEMORY_WRITE` | 0x0040 | memory store |\n| `CAP_RULES_READ` | 0x0080 | rules list |\n| `CAP_RULES_ADMIN` | 0x0100 | rules delete/approve |\n| `CAP_DESCRIBE_READ` | 0x0200 | graph describe |\n| `CAP_DESCRIBE_ADMIN` | 0x0400 | graph describe mutation |\n| `CAP_INDEX_READ` | 0x0800 | code-index reads |\n| `CAP_INDEX_ADMIN` | 0x1000 | index scan/rebuild |\n| `CAP_SESSION_READ` | 0x2000 | session / wm reads |\n| `CAP_SESSION_ADMIN` | 0x4000 | session / tool mutation |\n| `CAP_DASHBOARD_READ` | 0x8000 | dashboard metrics |\n\nComposite sets exist for authenticated (all-but-index-admin) and read-only\ncallers. Auth failures are rate-limited per UID (5 / 60 s → cooldown); the HTTP\nsurface can rate-limit per source. SIGTERM/SIGINT drain pending I/O and record\nunclean-exit forensics (`shutdown_forensics.c`) to DB1.","doc_id":"cd5ff0a87c0263f5a3744a0f","doc_kind":""}

Concepts and mental model\n\n**Primary agent vs delegate agent.** The *primary agent* is the AI coding\nsurface you interact with (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Vibe, Copilot, or\naimee's own chat). aimee integrates with it through hooks, provider-CLI\nadapters, or direct primary-session adapters. *Delegate agents* are sub-agents\nconfigured in `agents.json` that handle offloaded work via\n`aimee delegate <role> <prompt>`.\n\n**The two storage tiers.** DB1 (SQLite, owned by the local `aimee-server`) holds\nsame-user runtime state, sessions, working memory, conversation windows,\ncheckpoints, jobs, local signal streams, and secrets. DB2 (Postgres + pgvector,\nowned by `aimee-kb`) holds durable knowledge, memories, rules, the code index,\ntasks/decisions, and the vector embeddings of all of it. DB2 can run locally for\none user or as a shared KB; only knowledge that is appropriate for its configured\nscope is reflected or promoted there from local server state. The boundary is\npinned and compile-enforced; you never choose a different backend for either\ntier. It is also the **scaling boundary**: `aimee-server` is one-per-user, while\n`aimee-kb` and its Postgres are the shared, horizontally-scalable tier (see\n[§27.5](#275-scaling-and-multi-user-deployment)). See\n[`docs/STORAGE_TIERS.md`](docs/STORAGE_TIERS.md).\n\n**Memory tiers (L0-L3).** Stored knowledge moves through four lifetimes: L0\nsession scratch, L1 recent (≈30 days), L2 long-term stable facts, L3 episodic\n(past attempts/outcomes with decay). Promotion and decay are automatic. This is\n*different* from the storage tiers above, L0-L3 is the *semantic* lifecycle of a\nmemory; DB1/DB2 is *where bytes live*.\n\n**Sessions and worktrees.** Each session gets its own git worktree, branch, and\nstate file, so parallel sessions never collide. Guardrails redirect writes that\ntarget a workspace path with an active worktree.\n\n**Hooks.** aimee registers `SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, and `PostToolUse`\nhooks with your tool. SessionStart injects context; PreToolUse classifies and","doc_id":"cef49fe8d4f0c0dfd93ecc46","doc_kind":""}

Linkage and dependency profiles\n\nThe build deliberately produces binaries with disjoint dependency graphs so that\nthe storage boundary cannot be violated even by accident.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    Core[\"Core objects<br/>db, config, util, text,<br/>render, cJSON, platform, mcp_git\"]\n    Data[\"Data + policy objects<br/>memory, index, rules, tasks,<br/>guardrails, workspace, learning\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent objects<br/>delegate loop, tools, HTTP,<br/>policy, plan, eval\"]\n    Cmd[\"RPC handlers<br/>session, compute, MCP, dashboard\"]\n\n    aimee[\"aimee (client)<br/>-lpthread\"]\n    server[\"aimee-server<br/>-lsqlite3 +ssl +pam\"]\n    kb[\"aimee-kb<br/>-lpq +zstd +ssl\"]\n    webchat[\"aimee-webchat<br/>pure Go\"]\n\n    aimee --> Core\n    server --> Core --> Data\n    server --> Data --> Agent\n    server --> Agent --> Cmd\n    server --> Cmd\n    kb --> Core\n    kb --> Data\n    webchat -.->|socket| server\n    server -.->|KB RPC| kb\n```\n\n| Library | Used by | Purpose |\n|---------|---------|---------|\n| SQLite3 | `aimee-server` only | DB1 local store |\n| libpq | `aimee-kb` only | DB2 access (incl. pgvector) |\n| libcurl / WinHTTP | `aimee-server` | delegate HTTP client |\n| libssl / libcrypto | server, kb | TLS, auth provider support |\n| libpam | server (Linux), webchat | PAM authentication |\n| libsecret | server, kb (Linux, optional) | credential storage |\n| libzstd | `aimee-kb` | payload compression |\n| libm / libpthread | all C binaries | math, threads |\n| cJSON | all C binaries | JSON (vendored, compiled in) |\n\nThe CMake build (`CMakeLists.txt`) mirrors the Makefile for Windows (MinGW) and\nmacOS cross-platform builds; the `src/Makefile` is canonical for development and\nCI.\n\n---","doc_id":"d39dd7bd1687e878837c94bc","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:21955:{"content":"## 1. Design goals\n\naimee is a local-first memory, safety, and delegation layer that sits between a\ndeveloper's AI coding tool and the work it performs. Its architecture is shaped\nby four hard constraints:\n\n1. **Invisible latency.** Hooks run in the critical path of every file edit, so\n   the client must start and respond in milliseconds. This drives the thin\n   client / persistent server split: a process that pays no database or\n   connection cost on startup.\n2. **Pinned storage ownership.** Knowledge must outlive any single session and\n   may need to be shared across tools or hosts, while same-user runtime state\n   stays local, private, and fast. This drives the DB1 / DB2 tier split with\n   strict, compile-enforced ownership.\n3. **Zero cloud dependencies for the core.** Everything required to run aimee,\n   memory, guardrails, indexing, delegation routing, works on the local\n   machine. External model providers are reached only when the user explicitly\n   delegates.\n4. **One install, many tools.** The same server backs Claude Code, Gemini CLI,\n   Codex CLI, Mistral Vibe, and GitHub Copilot, so integration logic lives in\n   one place and switching tools preserves all memory and context.\n\n---","doc_id":"d44930fb615d12763e05cc3e","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:21965:{"content":"### Window search\n\nConversation history search combines four scoring signals:\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    Q[Query] --> TM[Term Match<br/>exact lowercase match<br/>through DB1 API]\n    Q --> LM[DB1 Lexical Match<br/>summary-token recall<br/>through DB1 API]\n    Q --> GB[Graph Boost<br/>2-hop entity edges<br/>decay by 1/hop]\n\n    TM --> Combine[Combine scores]\n    LM --> Combine\n    GB --> Combine\n\n    Combine --> TD2[Apply time decay<br/>1 / 1 + days * 0.02]\n    TD2 --> TW[Apply tier weight<br/>raw:1.0 summary:0.7 fact:0.4]\n    TW --> Final[Final score<br/>sorted, top N]\n```","doc_id":"d470125c5207c4fd8e2217de","doc_kind":""}

(For getting started, see the\n[root README](../README.md#get-started) and the\n[Quickstart](../docs/QUICKSTART.md).)\n\naimee ships four artifacts: `aimee`, `aimee-webchat`, `aimee-server`, and\n`aimee-kb`. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:22089:{"content":"/capabilities\n```\n\nThe LLM-backed synthesis/curator passes are wired but disabled until you point an\nOpenAI-compatible endpoint at them: bring up a local llama.cpp server with\n`docker compose -f compose.yaml --profile llm up` (the same flag works with the\nsplit stack).\n\n#### Managing the containers\n\nThe binaries run as **long-lived container processes** (PID 1), supervised by\nDocker's restart policy:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d        # start (detached); add --build after a code change\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml ps           # container + health status\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml logs -f      # follow logs (add a service name to scope)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml restart aimee-server aimee-kb\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down         # stop + remove containers (named volumes persist)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down -v      # also drop the data volumes (DESTROYS DB2 + state)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml pull && \\\n  docker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d           # update: pull the latest published image + recreate\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d --build     # alternative: rebuild from local source\n```\n\nThe compose services point at the published `ghcr.io/rakuensoftware/aimee-*` images\n(built and pushed on every merge to `main`), so `pull` fetches the latest release\nwithout a local build. Pin a version (or a fork/registry) by overriding\n`AIMEE_SERVER_IMAGE` / `AIMEE_KB_IMAGE` / `AIMEE_EMBEDDER_IMAGE` (e.g.\n`AIMEE_SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/rakuensoftware/aimee-server:v0.2.41`).\n\nEach container runs as a non-root user. It reaches DB2 through the **KB client**\n(`src/modules/kb_client/kb_client*.c`), typed wrappers (memory, index, docs, agent,\ndashboard, roadmap, notes, curiosity, status) that call `aimee-kb` over its\nHTTP `/v1` API (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`, port 8741). The legacy Unix-socket transport\nwas retired in #2747; HTTP is now the only KB transport. DB1 remains local to the server;\nDB2 can be a local single-user KB or a shared KB, and server-side reflection or\npromotion flows send only scoped knowledge artifacts across that boundary.\n`aimee-kb` (`src/kb/`) owns the DB2 schema, the memory inference pipeline, the\nvector collections, the code index, document ingest, and the curator. It exposes\n43 HTTP /v1 endpoints\n(`/v1/code/*`, `/v1/docs/*`, `/v1/search`, `/v1/ingest/*`, `/v1/entities/*`,\n`/v1/reflections/*`, `/v1/maintenance/*`, `/v1/releases/*`), see\n`api/openapi-v1.yaml`. The server no longer auto-starts the KB: `AIMEE_KB_API_URL`\nmust point at an already-running `aimee-kb` (started by its service unit, container,\nor `aimee-kb --http-port`). `AIMEE_KB_NO_AUTOSTART` is now a deprecated no-op.","doc_id":"d9cbd3536d1c4d1e94c292b8","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:22923:{"content":"## What already exists (why this is wiring, not green-field)\n\nThe four-way code survey (2026-07-17) found aimee already owns most of the hard primitives the commercial tools charge enterprise money for:\n\n- **Cost accounting — strong.** Per-request token→USD in the `token_audit` DB1 table (`src/db1/token_audit.c`, `src/server/token_tracker.c`): multi-source pricing (static table → registry/models.dev → authoritative DB1 `model_pricing`), attributed by model/source/role/tool/session/principal/delegation with parent cost-fold. Read surface exists: `GET /v1/insights/overview`, `/v1/dashboard/*`, React `CostPanel`. **Missing only the per-team/project dimension.**\n- **Credential vault — encrypted at rest**, keyed by attested principal (`src/server/vault_service.c`, `src/headers/vault_principal.h`).\n- **OIDC/JWT verifier — real** (RS256/JWKS, alg-pinned), in aimee-kb and kb-console (`src/kb/auth_oidc.c`, `kb-console/auth.go`) — opt-in via env today.\n- **PKI + mTLS enrollment CA** (`src/kb/enroll.c`, `src/kb/pki.c`, `src/server/kb_client_mtls.c`) — `aimee://` single-use tokens, `cert:CN` principals. Reusable for enrolling servers.\n- **Canonical IR + provider drivers** (`src/headers/aimee_ir.h`, `src/server/delegate_driver.c`, `aimee-universal-gateway.md`, done) — Anthropic / OpenAI-Chat / Responses / Gemini wire adapters through a protocol-neutral pivot. This is the egress machinery kb needs.\n- **Keyless roster + attested credential handling already exist** — the shipped `deploy/container/agents.json` ships no keys. The old client-push `POST /v1/session/credentials` was retired; provider secrets now live in the server vault (`/v1/vault/*`), and vault writes require an attested transport (UDS or confidential TLS+bearer — never plaintext TCP; `server_cert.c:18-22`, `server_http_identity.c:113-123`). The org-egress work reuses this attested-transport discipline rather than inventing a new one — org keys simply never leave kb in the first place.\n\nAbsent (the actual gaps, one sub-proposal each): a team/project entity; per-team/project cost attribution; per-team budgets and per-key rate limits (spend is tracked but never capped; the rate limiter is a single global bucket); OIDC on the aimee-server data plane + a kb→server control plane; and AWS Bedrock.","doc_id":"dda697a78df9eb34862d936f","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23030:{"content":"## Separate TLS trust domain\n\nAdd a process-owned management `SSL_CTX` in `server_tls`, with a context-selecting accept helper and\n`server_tls_management_begin`. The management context always requires a client certificate,\nenforces TLS 1.2 or newer and client-auth chain/time/purpose verification against its dedicated CA,\nand uses the configured management server leaf/key. A separate management context builder has no\ngeneric DB1 roster callback parameter or registration call by construction: management leaves are\nprimary-issued and their online next-request authority is the B3 nonce/staple protocol. A focused\ntest marks the same leaf revoked in the generic roster and proves this TLS context still performs\nonly CA/time/EKU verification while application status revocation remains fail-closed. The data\ncontext and optional→required ramp are unchanged.\n\nThe context is published only after it is completely built and remains process-lifetime owned\nbecause detached HTTP workers are not joined by current server shutdown. Once published it is\nnever freed or replaced before process exit; each `SSL_new` also holds its OpenSSL reference.\nStart failure before publication frees the private candidate. Same-process HTTP restart may reuse\nonly a byte-identical cert/key/CA configuration packet; any difference is a fatal start while the\npublished context remains untouched. Live `SSL` objects share the existing\nregistered-connection shutdown. Management TLS reload is explicitly restart-required; data\nSIGHUP never replaces or frees the management context.\n\n“Byte-identical” is a stored SHA-256 tuple over the bounded raw PEM bytes in fixed\n`certificate || private-key || client-CA` order, read through no-follow regular-file descriptors\nat context build time. On a later start, all three hashes must match before reuse; mismatch returns\n`SERVER_HTTP_START_MGMT_FATAL`, never swaps the context, and never rebinds a listener. Bind/port\nare separately revalidated but are not part of the TLS-context tuple.","doc_id":"dea338eada6c6edb7c3caf94","doc_kind":""}

It runs **both** aimee binaries as separate services: `aimee-kb` serving\n`/v1` on `:8741`, and the server fronting `/v1` over TLS on `:8743` (plaintext\n`:8740` is loopback-only) with `AIMEE_KB_API_URL=http://aimee-kb:8741`, so server\nand kb communicate over the internal network. The `aimee-llm` service provides the\nsynthesis and curator gateway; to run a standalone llama.cpp curator LLM instead,\nadd `--profile curator-llm` (works on `compose.server.yaml` and `compose.yaml`).\nEach container runs as a\nnon-root user; the kb uses Python sidecars (`scripts/embed-remote.py`,\n`llm-chat.py`, `curator-extract.py`, `learning-synthesize.py`) for embeddings,\nsynthesis, and curation, with container defaults from `deploy/container/aimee.yaml`.\n\n**Container lifecycle**: the binaries run as long-lived container processes\n(PID 1), supervised by Docker's restart policy, not systemd/launchd:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml ps           # container + health status\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml logs -f      # follow logs (add a service to scope)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml restart aimee-server aimee-kb\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down         # stop + remove containers (volumes persist)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down -v      # also DROP data volumes (destroys DB2 + state)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d --build # update: rebuild images, recreate containers\n```\n\n**State and volumes.** Durable data lives in named volumes, not the container\nfilesystem, so recreate is safe and only `down -v` erases it: `*-postgres` holds\nDB2 (`aimee_shared`); `*-home` (`/var/lib/aimee`) holds server/kb runtime state\n(DB1 SQLite + config); `*-workspaces` (`/var/lib/aimee-workspaces`,","doc_id":"dece3672c42a51c44cf9be0d","doc_kind":""}

Until a Go runner\nimplements every production block, the Go control plane may call an isolated\ncompatibility worker over the typed runner protocol. That worker is disposable:\nits death is a failed attempt, not a control-plane failure.","doc_id":"e0087d42621cc464cbeac50a","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23233:{"content":"## Design: on-demand threads + high safety ceiling\n\nEach sessionless delegate runs on **its own detached thread**, spawned on\ndemand and reaped on completion (`delegate_spawn_ondemand` in\n`server_compute.c`). No fixed pool; no compute-budget gate. Throttling is the\nper-model limiter. A configurable **backstop ceiling** (`delegate_max_inflight`,\ndefault **512**, env `AIMEE_DELEGATE_MAX_INFLIGHT`) prevents a pathological\nfan-out from exhausting fds/memory — \"effectively unlimited\" for any real\nworkload, but not literally unbounded.\n\nMechanics:\n- An atomic-by-mutex in-flight counter; spawn rejects (`-1`, job marked failed)\n  only at the ceiling — unreachable under the per-model limiter in normal use.\n- Detached threads carry the same 32 MB stack as compute-pool workers (the\n  agent loop has deep frames).\n- The compute **budget is bypassed** exactly as session delegates already do:\n  a positive `compute_executor_threads` grant makes `compute_ctx_begin_budget`\n  take its non-blocking path (verified: `compute_ctx_release_budget` then never\n  touches the global budget). This is the *second* 2-wide gate, also removed for\n  delegates.\n- **Shutdown:** `delegate_ondemand_drain(5000)` gives in-flight delegates a\n  bounded window. On-demand delegates bypass the budget (never touch\n  `compute_budget_mutex`) and own no socket (no `conns_mutex`); a straggler past\n  the window only touches DB1 + its own ctx, so teardown is safe.\n- **Observability:** `aimee workers` no longer shows delegates as pool slots\n  (they aren't pooled), so a `delegates_inflight` gauge is added to the workers\n  response. `compute_pool_set_job` is a safe no-op off a pool thread.","doc_id":"e0be27e9db8880d88a1f850a","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23236:{"content":"## `check_tier_deps.sh`, enforce DB1/DB2 tier boundaries\n\nValidates dependency boundaries for the two-database architecture (DB1 = local\nSQLite owned by `aimee-server`; DB2 = shared Postgres owned by `aimee-kb`,\nincluding the in-process pgvector extension):\n\n- `sqlite3.h` only in `src/db1/`\n- `libpq-fe.h` only in `src/db2/`\n- `aimee_stores_` / `aimee_stores_t` / `PGconn` / `PGresult` / `PQ*` helper symbols / `sqlite3_` only in tier-owned source trees\n- no legacy `project_store_` lifecycle aliases outside `src/db2`\n- no legacy DB2 backend selector outside `src/db2`\n- DB2 transitional SQLite lifecycle names stay inside `src/db2`\n- DB2 public lifecycle headers hide SQLite backend knowledge\n- DB2 public lifecycle headers hide shim backend vocabulary\n- DB2 shared-store lifecycle APIs expose neutral names outside `src/db2`\n- DB2 transaction primitives stay inside `src/db2`\n- Legacy/helper vocabulary outside `src/db1` avoids SQLite names\n- Worker-shell comments outside `src/db1` avoid SQLite names\n- Vector verify row-count fields expose DB2 names instead of SQLite names\n- Doctor DB output exposes DB2 names instead of Postgres names\n- Non-DB2 source comments avoid Postgres/libpq implementation names\n- No Qdrant HTTP collection/points URL paths in `src/` (vector store is now\n  pgvector inside DB2, in-process, no HTTP sidecar)\n\nMost checks scan `src/**/*.c`, `src/**/*.h`, and `src/**/*.inc` outside\n`src/db1`, `src/db2`, `src/tests`, and `src/webchat`.\n\nRun manually:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/check_tier_deps.sh\n```\n\nThe `lint` CI job also runs this check.\n\nBinary ownership is checked by `cd src && make check-linking`; that target\nverifies the process boundary:\n\n- `aimee-client` and `aimee-webchat` stay DB-free (`libsqlite3` and `libpq` absent).\n- `aimee-server` stays DB1-only (`libsqlite3` present, `libpq` absent, no\n  DB2 symbols).\n- `aimee-kb` stays DB2-only (`libpq` present, `libsqlite3` absent, no\n  DB1/sqlite symbols).","doc_id":"e0c2cb3d4fd7077e611b08df","doc_kind":""}

Add `/v1` operations for list/show, preview, restore, and\nfocused doctor actions. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23807:{"content":"## Server Architecture\n\nThe shipped artifacts are four binaries: `aimee`, `aimee-webchat`, `aimee-server`, and `aimee-kb`. Common runtime code and git MCP handlers are linked directly into the binaries that need them instead of being shipped as separate executables or shared libraries. Long-running work uses `aimee-server`'s in-process compute pool; there is no separate worker binary.\n\n| Binary | Libraries | External deps |\n|--------|-----------|---------------|\n| `aimee` | Thin CLI transport + MCP stdio bridge | pthread |\n| `aimee-webchat` | DB-free webchat launcher; talks only to `aimee-server` through `webchat.serve` | pthread |\n| `aimee-server` | Local DB1 daemon, agent/runtime orchestration, KB RPC client | sqlite3, ssl, crypto, pam |\n| `aimee-kb` | Local-or-shared DB2 RPC service + memory/KB pipeline (incl. pgvector) | libpq, ssl, crypto |\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    CLI[aimee\\nCLI + MCP stdio] -->|JSON RPC| SRV[aimee-server\\nDB1 + compute pool]\n    WEB[aimee-webchat\\nbrowser-facing client] -->|JSON RPC| SRV\n    SRV -->|typed KB /v1 HTTP| KB[aimee-kb\\nDB2 + pgvector]\n    SRV --> DB1[src/db1/*]\n    KB --> DB2[src/db2/*]\n```","doc_id":"e64e4ac0ea5c533fa635c6bb","doc_kind":""}

The pipeline uses Aimee's existing workspace-aware git/PR tool surface,\n  which may call `gh`/`git` underneath with the right workspace/forge authority.\n- Storing whole proposals or large diffs as unbounded DB blobs. DB1 stores refs,\n  manifests, hashes, and compact digests; working files/blobs, db2 `docs`, or an\n  explicit artifact payload carry the large origin content. `kb_documents` remains\n  a chunk index, not the canonical whole-origin store.\n- Expecting DRAFT mode to emit a complete proposal (#9). The 8 KB artifact cap\n  means DRAFT produces a skeleton; the author-revise loop expands it in the working\n  file. Generating long-form text inside the roundtable artifact is out of scope.\n- A fully autonomous, gate-less pipeline — the two human gates are mandatory by\n  design; \"configurable max passes\" bounds cost, it does not remove the human. This\n  is **enforced by authority separation (#53)**, not convention: the driving agent\n  cannot resolve a gate, so the pipeline cannot self-approve its way to a merge.\n- Engine changes to the roundtable. The pipeline is strictly on top.\n- Multi-proposal/parallel-pipeline scheduling beyond the explicit parked-gate\n  admission rule (#48). v1 may allow many parked/waiting-human rows only if they\n  do not count as active and branch/PR ownership prevents mutation overlap; it\n  still permits at most one active drafting/review/implementing runner unless a\n  later proposal adds scheduling.","doc_id":"e6a5a43688acf7269583456c","doc_kind":""}

Three compose files ship, built from two images: `aimee-server`\n(`Dockerfile.server`) and `aimee-kb` (`Dockerfile`). Every stack also brings up a\n`pgvector/pgvector:pg16` Postgres, and the kb auto-applies its DB2 schema\n(`pg_trgm` and `vector` extensions plus tables) on first boot. The stacks run the\n`aimee-llm` inference gateway (embeddings, reranking, and synthesis) as a service,\nwhich downloads its cpu-tier models on first boot, so embedding and reranking work\nwith nothing external. The tier is chosen by `AIMEE_LLM_TIER`: `cpu` serves\nQwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 1024 dims; the GPU tiers (`small` 16 GB, `mid` 24 GB,\n`large` 32 GB) serve Qwen3-Embedding-4B at 2560 dims.\nTo run a standalone embedder or curator LLM instead, use\nthe `curator-llm` compose profile. Backends and tiers:\n[KB_LLM_BACKENDS.md](docs/KB_LLM_BACKENDS.md) and\n[AIMEE_KB_SYNTH_TIERS.md](docs/AIMEE_KB_SYNTH_TIERS.md).\n\n| Compose file | Brings up | Use when |\n|--------------|-----------|----------|\n| `compose.server-managed.yaml` | `aimee-server` only; the wizard's Deploy step then launches `aimee-kb` + `aimee-llm` + Postgres via the mounted Docker socket | **Recommended default.** One container to deploy; the browser wizard brings up the rest. |\n| `compose.server.yaml` | `aimee-server` + `aimee-kb` + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway | Advanced: the full split stack brought up together, no socket mount. Scale/update/place server and kb independently. |\n| `compose.yaml` | `aimee-kb` + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway | The knowledge service alone: building block for a shared/scaled kb. |\n| `compose.server-standalone.yaml` | `aimee-server` only (SQLite DB1, no kb) | DB1-backed `/v1` with no shared knowledge. |\n\n**Bring up the self-deploying server:**\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server-managed.yaml up -d","doc_id":"ea04c8642b1328958f1f0d31","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24169:{"content":"### 3.2 State machine\n\n```text\n                 ┌──────────────→ INVALID\n                 │\nOPEN ────────────┼──→ ABORTED\n  │              │\n  ├── crash ─→ RECOVERABLE_OPEN ─→ SEALED_INCOMPLETE\n  │\n  └────────────→ SEALED ─→ RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS ─→ RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING ─→ RESTORED\n                       │             │\n                       │             └──────────→ RESTORE_INCIDENT\n                       └────────────────────────→ EXPIRED\n```\n\n- `OPEN`: accepts immutable preimages and append-only operation evidence.\n- `ABORTED`: no completed native mutation was observed. Terminal and not restorable;\n  blob refs are released.\n- `INVALID`: capture, coverage, identity, evidence, or integrity failure. Terminal and\n  never shown as safe.\n- `RECOVERABLE_OPEN`: startup/doctor classification only; no automatic restore.\n- `SEALED_INCOMPLETE`: an interrupted turn with fully verifiable mutated entries. It may\n  be previewed but restore remains an explicit operator action.\n- `SEALED`: immutable manifest and final postimages exist.\n- `RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS`: durable restore journal written before the first filesystem\n  mutation.\n- `RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING`: filesystem and DB1 operational state committed, but the\n  separate audit sink has not yet acknowledged the terminal event. Doctor retries the\n  bounded event; this state is never reported as fully complete.\n- `RESTORED`: requested entries and audit outcome committed.\n- `RESTORE_INCIDENT`: apply or compensation could not converge automatically. The\n  worktree is write-frozen at `mutation_begin` until operator acknowledgement.\n- `EXPIRED`: manifest retained; one or more required blobs were policy-pruned.\n\nNo state transition makes a sealed manifest mutable. A later restore attempt receives a\nnew restore-run id and journal.","doc_id":"ea1314bbd7f0f00dfd909a3f","doc_kind":""}

Ships with `code-review`, `debate`, `planning`, and `design-critique`\ntemplates; drop a project-local template in `ensemble_templates/` (the legacy\n`session_templates/` path still resolves). State lives in the DB1 `ensembles`\ntable.\n\nAgents drive sessions with the **MCP tools** `ensemble_start`, `ensemble_status`,\n`ensemble_pause`, `ensemble_advance`, and `ensemble_list` (the `session_*` names\nremain as hidden aliases). Each `ensemble_advance` records a turn and returns the\nnext expected participant and prompt.\n\n```jsonc\n// ensemble_start\n{ \"template\": \"code-review\", \"channel\": \"pr-482\",\n  \"assignments\": { \"reviewer\": [\"claude-1\", \"gemini\"], \"author\": [\"me\"] } }\n```\n\n`aimee ensemble session <start|status|pause|advance|list>` is the human-facing\ncounterpart; today it points at the MCP path (thin-client session control over\n`/v1` is a pending enhancement).","doc_id":"ed2674738a75f5753754a90e","doc_kind":""}

A test asserts this explicitly, so the liveness contract\n   and the kb symmetry cannot regress.\n3. **Red before green.** A test harness starts the server with an injected\n   failing dependency and asserts `/v1/ready` reports non-ok and status 503.\n   The same harness, run against a build where the readiness provider is\n   replaced by one that unconditionally reports ok, must **fail** — proving the\n   test detects blindness rather than merely observing a hardcoded string. (The\n   original draft asked the test to fail against the stock endpoint; that was\n   unachievable, since the stock build has no `/v1/ready` to point it at. This\n   is the corrected formulation.)\n4. Before the first sample completes, `/v1/ready` reports `unknown` and 503.\n   A test asserts this startup behavior.\n5. A snapshot older than the staleness bound degrades to `unknown`/503. A test\n   asserts a wedged refresher does not report ready indefinitely.\n6. A dependency probe exceeding its timeout is reported `fail`/`timeout`, and a\n   test asserts the handler's own latency stays bounded and independent of that\n   probe's duration — i.e. the request path did no I/O.\n7. `server_http.c`'s existing unit test gains no new dependency linkage. With no\n   provider registered, `/v1/ready` reports `unknown`/503.\n8. The route, its schema, and the 200-vs-503 boundary are added to the OpenAPI\n   surface, and generated docs regenerate cleanly.","doc_id":"ed6507fe9ffb5fb0cbc7b882","doc_kind":""}

Complete WFE block runners, roundtables, Git forge operations, worktree\n   isolation, and provider routing in Go.\n2. Shadow-read current DB1 and compare API responses; stop the C scheduler, then\n   transfer the workflow tables to the Go writer in one cutover.\n3. Move the remaining DB1 API families and session/auth control plane to Go one\n   family at a time, maintaining one writer per family.\n4. Move delegate/provider execution, vault and policy enforcement into isolated\n   Go services. Preserve durable admission-before-dispatch semantics.\n5. Rewrite the KB service and DB2 ownership in Go, retaining typed HTTP boundaries.\n6. Replace thin-client and gateway behavior where needed. Delete compatibility\n   adapters once no deployed client depends on them.\n7. Remove C build/runtime dependencies from production images. It owns DB1, runs the compute pool, routes delegates,\nserves hooks, and exposes both the internal RPC protocol and the public HTTP /v1\nAPI.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    L[\"Listen sockets<br/>aimee-http.sock (HTTP /v1) + optional localhost TCP\"]\n    EV[\"HTTP listener<br/>(accept loop hands each connection to its own worker thread)\"]\n    AUTH[\"Auth gate<br/>local UDS = filesystem-trusted (full surface)<br/>TCP = bearer-scoped + 16 capability flags\"]\n    POOL[\"Bounded compute pool<br/>(delegate exec, chat, tool calls)\"]\n    DB1[(\"DB1 SQLite\")]\n    KBC[\"KB client<br/>typed RPC to aimee-kb\"]\n    PROV[\"Delegate HTTP client<br/>libcurl\"]\n\n    L --> EV --> AUTH\n    AUTH -->|fast handlers| DB1\n    AUTH -->|blocking handlers| POOL\n    POOL --> DB1\n    POOL --> KBC\n    POOL --> PROV\n```\n\nKey properties:\n\n- **Per-connection workers, bounded compute pool.** The HTTP accept loop hands\n  each connection to its own detached worker thread, so a slow or streaming\n  request never blocks the listener and independent `/v1` requests run\n  concurrently. Heavyweight handlers (DB query, network, subprocess, delegate\n  inference) additionally run on a bounded compute pool; a compute budget gate\n  serializes heavyweight inference to bound resource use.\n- **Transport.** Clients reach the server over its `/v1` HTTP surface: the\n  always-on `~/.config/aimee/aimee-http.sock` Unix socket, plus an optional\n  localhost TCP listener. Dispatch methods use dedicated `/v1` routes; the\n  generic `POST /v1/rpc` endpoint is retired. Streaming chat uses\n  `POST /v1/chat/stream`, whose body is a sequence of newline-delimited aimee\n  events terminated by a final status object. (The legacy newline-delimited\n  JSON-RPC socket was removed.)\n- **Authentication.** The local UDS is filesystem-permission gated and fully\n  trusted: it reaches the entire dispatch surface, with no token. The optional\n  TCP listener requires a configured bearer token and is capability-scoped.","doc_id":"ee8788f3fc16ef5a146bad5e","doc_kind":""}

DB1 holds the canonical memory. The on-disk\n`memory/*.md` files are a rendered cache that aimee rebuilds — DB1 wins on any conflict.\n\n**Threat model — be honest about what is and isn't intercepted (R3 #2).** We do **not**\nclaim \"every mutation path is intercepted.\" We intercept exactly **agent-tool-mediated**\nwrites/deletes (the seam fires only on tool calls — §0). Writes that bypass the tool layer\nentirely — a human in `vim`, IDE autosave, a sync client (Dropbox/Syncthing), a container\nvolume mount, `python -c 'open(...).write()'` via `Bash`, or an agent **not** installed\nwith an `AIMEE_HOOK_CLIENT` hook — are **not** captured at write time. They are caught by a\n**session-start content-hash audit** (§5) that compares every on-disk file against its DB1\nrow and, per the deterministic reconcile policy, makes disk match DB1 (or imports\ndisk-only files). So the precise invariant is:\n\n- **Agent-tool writes** → intercepted (§3): denied, canonicalized into DB1, re-materialized.\n- **Agent-tool deletes** → intercepted (§3): tombstoned in DB1 (per-file *and* bulk/dir, §3).\n- **Non-tool / external changes** → **not prevented**, reconciled to DB1 at session-start\n  (§5) with the divergence surfaced in the audit log (§7). DB1 is authoritative; an external\n  edit does not silently become the source of truth.\n- aimee's **own** re-materialize writes use direct filesystem syscalls in the server/CLI\n  process and therefore **cannot** re-enter a PreToolUse hook (hooks fire only on *agent\n  tool calls*, not on aimee's own process I/O). This makes the no-loop property\n  **structural**, not flag-based (R1 #2, #23); a test exercises aimee's writer with the\n  hook installed to prove it.\n\nAccepted scope: **single host.** DB1 is local SQLite, so \"shared across all agents/\nsessions\" means *on this machine*. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25155:{"content":"### 6.2 Blob store\n\nPreimage bytes move out of unbounded inline SQLite blobs into a DB1-owned store beneath\n`$AIMEE_HOME/rewind/blobs`, following Aimee's existing content-addressed-store durability\npattern:\n\n- per-principal namespace; no cross-principal deduplication or equality oracle;\n- SHA-256 content identity, opaque refs at external surfaces;\n- `0700` directories, `0600` regular files, `O_NOFOLLOW`;\n- unique temp write → file `fsync` → atomic rename → directory `fsync`;\n- DB ref committed only after the blob is durable;\n- blobs with an active `rewind_blob_refs` edge are never deleted;\n- oldest eligible sealed sets expire under both count and byte ceilings;\n- manifest/audit rows survive blob expiry.\n\nExpiry is ordered: compare-and-swap the set from restore-eligible to `EXPIRED`, remove its\nactive ref edges in the same DB1 transaction, then let asynchronous GC delete now-unreferenced\nblob files after a grace period. A preimage row is never rewritten merely because its\nretained bytes expired.\n\nGarbage collection is bounded and asynchronous. If it cannot make space, protected\ncapture blocks before mutation with `store_budget_exhausted`; it does not delete a live\nref or silently degrade to partial coverage.","doc_id":"f33c1921048dcd99274cd8d4","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25172:{"content":"## Scope (P3a only)\n\n1. **DB2 `org_model_pricing`** — Postgres-authoritative, versioned price table:\n   `(id, provider, model, input_usd_per_mtok, output_usd_per_mtok,\n   cache_read_usd_per_mtok, version, effective_at, created_at)`, unique\n   `(model, version)`. A per-model `current_version` pointer table\n   `org_model_pricing_current(model, version)` advanced **atomically** on a price\n   change (new row + pointer update in one txn) — a price change is a NEW row, never\n   an in-place mutate, so every stateless kb instance agrees on `(model, version)`.\n   Seeded by promoting the existing static/registry/DB1 `model_pricing` prices.\n2. **DB2 `org_token_audit`** — per-request org cost ledger: `(id, request_id,\n   origin_cert_cn, actor_issuer, actor_subject, team_id, project_id, model,\n   served_model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_read_tokens,\n   estimated_cost_usd, pricing_version, state, created_at, settled_at)`. Idempotency\n   key **unique `(origin_cert_cn, request_id)`** (a bare request_id can replay across\n   mutually-untrusted origins). `pricing_version` is a **FK to\n   `org_model_pricing(model, version)`** (settlement references the exact immutable\n   row). Lifecycle `state ∈ {started, settled_success, settled_denied,\n   settled_failed, indeterminate}`.\n3. **`(team, project, model, day)` rollup table** — `org_spend_rollup`, maintained\n   incrementally (P3b writes it; P3a defines the table + the upsert contends only\n   per-key).\n4. **RLS (invariant #10):** all three are tenant tables — `FORCE ROW LEVEL\n   SECURITY`, membership-bound read policies keyed on `team_id ∈ principal's teams`\n   (reuse the P1 `set_tenant_context`/`aimee.principal` pattern), admin/team-lead\n   write via P3b. `org_model_pricing` is org-global read (all authenticated), admin\n   write.\n5. **Typed db2 modules:** `src/db2/org_pricing.{h,c}` (get_current_price(model) →\n   pins version; add_price_version; seed), `src/db2/org_token_audit.{h,c}`\n   (insert_started, settle, get by key), each guarded by `db2_tenant_require_pg()`.","doc_id":"f35acf7e26b35c3e1e7c4e89","doc_kind":""}

Registration and\nunregistration occur only while the HTTP listener is stopped. Dispatch borrows the handler under\nthe seam mutex, increments its in-flight count, releases the mutex for the full network call, and\ndecrements/signals on return; unregister first blocks new borrows and waits on a condition\nvariable without holding runtime/lifecycle/DB locks. The production runtime is its only owner;\ntests may inject a handler before requests begin. For exactly\n`GET /v1/servers/{id}/health`, parse the existing positive `team` parameter, require\n`kb_reqctx_actor()` to be authenticated, and invoke the registered live handler. Do not perform\nthe old direct `db2_server_registry_get()` heartbeat read and do not manufacture an owner in\nauth-off mode.\n\nMap typed B3a results without string inspection: `OK→200`, `NOT_FOUND→404`, `DENIED→403`,\n`CONFLICT→409`, `UNAVAILABLE→503`, `INTEGRITY→502`, `INVALID→400`. Build bounded exact JSON and\nescape no dependency-controlled prose. Method mismatches remain 405. The registration seam is\nconsulted only by this exact health path; `/v1/servers` list behavior and all other routes remain\non their existing direct paths, with a regression test proving the list callback cardinality is\nzero.\n\nOn aimee-server, add a pure predicate for the dedicated management transport. It returns true\nonly for the exact two method/path pairs above and a TLS peer whose already chain-verified leaf\nhas the management profile and exact management-client CN. In `handle_conn`, evaluate this after\n`server_tls_peer_identity()` plus `server_tls_peer_cert()` have extracted the verified leaf and\nimmediately before the generic DB1 `pki_cert_check`, required-mTLS ramp accounting, transport,\nbearer, bootstrap-bearer, and capability gates. The classifier is three-way: `NOT_MANAGEMENT`,","doc_id":"f4c53bdd01bdcc0570b299bd","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25527:{"content":"## The KB split\n\n`aimee-server` owns no DB2 SQL. It reaches DB2 through the **KB client**\n(`src/modules/kb_client/kb_client*.c`), typed wrappers (memory, index, docs, agent,\ndashboard, roadmap, notes, curiosity, status) that call `aimee-kb` over its\nHTTP `/v1` API (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`, port 8741). The legacy Unix-socket transport\nwas retired in #2747; HTTP is now the only KB transport. DB1 remains local to the server;\nDB2 can be a local single-user KB or a shared KB, and server-side reflection or\npromotion flows send only scoped knowledge artifacts across that boundary.\n`aimee-kb` (`src/kb/`) owns the DB2 schema, the memory inference pipeline, the\nvector collections, the code index, document ingest, and the curator. It exposes\n43 HTTP /v1 endpoints\n(`/v1/code/*`, `/v1/docs/*`, `/v1/search`, `/v1/ingest/*`, `/v1/entities/*`,\n`/v1/reflections/*`, `/v1/maintenance/*`, `/v1/releases/*`), see\n`api/openapi-v1.yaml`. The server no longer auto-starts the KB: `AIMEE_KB_API_URL`\nmust point at an already-running `aimee-kb` (started by its service unit, container,\nor `aimee-kb --http-port`). `AIMEE_KB_NO_AUTOSTART` is now a deprecated no-op.","doc_id":"f6d89caab2ea853df7169a1d","doc_kind":""}

Revocations are rare; a flat\n * growable array consulted under the mutex is plenty and keeps the TLS verify\n * callback off the database. */\nstatic char **g_revoked = NULL;\nstatic int g_revoked_n = 0, g_revoked_cap = 0;\n\nvoid pki_reset_for_test(void)\n{\n   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_mu);\n   if (g_ca_key)\n      EVP_PKEY_free(g_ca_key);\n   if (g_ca_cert)\n      X509_free(g_ca_cert);\n   g_ca_key = NULL;\n   g_ca_cert = NULL;\n   for (int i = 0; i < g_revoked_n; i++)\n      free(g_revoked[i]);\n   free(g_revoked);\n   g_revoked = NULL;\n   g_revoked_n = g_revoked_cap = 0;\n   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_mu);\n}\n\nstatic void ca_cert_path(char *out, size_t n)\n{\n   snprintf(out, n, \"%s/tls/client-ca.crt\", config_default_dir());\n}\n\n/* --- DB1 (caller holds no lock; sqlite is serialized) --- */\nstatic void db_ensure_tables(void)\n{\n   sqlite3 *db = db1_conn();\n   if (db)\n      sqlite3_exec(db,\n                   \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pki_certs(serial TEXT PRIMARY KEY, cn TEXT NOT NULL,\"\n                   \" issued_at INTEGER, expires_at INTEGER, revoked INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)\",\n                   NULL, NULL, NULL);\n}\n\nstatic int ramp_tables_ensure(s","doc_id":"f7548c8ca163289d7c3eaf4d","doc_kind":"code_unit_body"}

Nothing extra to install; this is what a fresh\n  `install.sh` gives you.\n- **pgvectorscale (StreamingDiskANN) is the opt-in scale-up** for large corpora.\n  It is *additive*: built on top of pgvector, it reuses the same `vector` column\n  type and distance operators and only adds the `USING diskann` index, disk-backed\n  with bounded build memory, for the large/RAM-constrained regime where HNSW's\n  in-memory graph becomes the bottleneck. Select it per corpus table:\n\n  ```yaml\n  db2:\n    vector:\n      corpus_index: auto          # auto | hnsw | diskann\n      corpus_diskann_threshold: 1000000   # rows/table before \"auto\" picks diskann\n  ```\n\n  `auto` uses HNSW until a corpus table exceeds the threshold *and* the\n  `vectorscale` extension is installed, then picks diskann; it falls back to HNSW\n  with a notice when the extension is absent (so schema apply never hard-fails).\n  Memory/hot-path vectors stay HNSW unconditionally.\n- **Switching index type is a reindex, not a migration.** Data and queries are\n  identical across HNSW and diskann; `aimee kb repair --reindex-corpus` rebuilds\n  corpus indexes to the configured/`auto` type with no re-embedding and no query\n  rewrite. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-2b271a8c33e84f01/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:26134:{"content":"## Durable local replay consume\n\nAdd a DB1-owned `db1/server_management_jti.{c,h}` module and schema table dedicated to management\ntoken consumption, not a server TU reaching through `db1_internal.h` and not a generic idempotency\nstore:\n\n`server_management_jti(jti TEXT PRIMARY KEY, issuer, kid, audience, subject, team_id,\ncapability, peer_issuer, peer_serial, peer_fingerprint, request_sha256, correlation_id,\nissued_at, expires_at, consumed_at)`.\n\nSchema `CHECK`s mirror every application bound: jti 16..128, issuer 1..255, kid 1..64,\naudience 1..127, subject 1..576, positive team id, capability 1..64, peer issuer 1..511,\npeer serial 1..79 lowercase hex, both SHA-256 fields exactly 64 lowercase hex, correlation id\n1..128, and integer times with `0 <= issued_at < expires_at`. The application uses a compiled live\nrow ceiling of 4096; because the table can never exceed that ceiling, deletion of all expired rows\ninside the transaction is itself bounded. Index `(expires_at,jti)`. A single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`\ntransaction:\n\n1. deletes rows whose `expires_at` is strictly before the current time;\n2. checks a compiled live-row ceiling before insert;\n3. inserts the fully verified claim tuple with the current consume time; and\n4. commits before reporting success.\n\nThe unique insert is the authorization point. Constraint conflict means replay; saturation,\nbusy/locked DB, schema error, clock error, or commit ambiguity is unavailable/deny, never success.\nThe row is not deleted on downstream failure: C1a has no dispatch, and later packets must treat an\naccepted token as consumed before any action attempt. Persistence across process restart is\nmandatory. Expiry GC is bounded and indexed; tests use injected time and capacity rather than\nsleep. The existing DB1 transaction gate serializes in-process writers; external `SQLITE_BUSY`\ndoes not spin or sleep and fails unavailable. The promised crash boundary is process crash/restart,\nnot arbitrary power-loss durability: later dispatch occurs only after COMMIT returns success.
