/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:22089:{"content":"/capabilities\n```\n\nThe LLM-backed synthesis/curator passes are wired but disabled until you point an\nOpenAI-compatible endpoint at them: bring up a local llama.cpp server with\n`docker compose -f compose.yaml --profile llm up` (the same flag works with the\nsplit stack).\n\n#### Managing the containers\n\nThe binaries run as **long-lived container processes** (PID 1), supervised by\nDocker's restart policy:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d        # start (detached); add --build after a code change\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml ps           # container + health status\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml logs -f      # follow logs (add a service name to scope)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml restart aimee-server aimee-kb\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down         # stop + remove containers (named volumes persist)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down -v      # also drop the data volumes (DESTROYS DB2 + state)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml pull && \\\n  docker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d           # update: pull the latest published image + recreate\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d --build     # alternative: rebuild from local source\n```\n\nThe compose services point at the published `ghcr.io/rakuensoftware/aimee-*` images\n(built and pushed on every merge to `main`), so `pull` fetches the latest release\nwithout a local build. Pin a version (or a fork/registry) by overriding\n`AIMEE_SERVER_IMAGE` / `AIMEE_KB_IMAGE` / `AIMEE_EMBEDDER_IMAGE` (e.g.\n`AIMEE_SERVER_IMAGE=ghcr.io/rakuensoftware/aimee-server:v0.2.41`).\n\nEach container runs as a non-root user. The legacy Unix-socket transport\nwas retired in #2747; HTTP is now the only KB transport. DB1 remains local to the server;\nDB2 can be a local single-user KB or a shared KB, and server-side reflection or\npromotion flows send only scoped knowledge artifacts across that boundary.\n`aimee-kb` (`src/kb/`) owns the DB2 schema, the memory inference pipeline, the\nvector collections, the code index, document ingest, and the curator. The server no longer auto-starts the KB: `AIMEE_KB_API_URL`\nmust point at an already-running `aimee-kb` (started by its service unit, container,\nor `aimee-kb --http-port`). `AIMEE_KB_NO_AUTOSTART` is now a deprecated no-op.","doc_id":"d9cbd3536d1c4d1e94c292b8","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:22923:{"content":"## What already exists (why this is wiring, not green-field)\n\nThe four-way code survey (2026-07-17) found aimee already owns most of the hard primitives the commercial tools charge enterprise money for:\n\n- **Cost accounting — strong.** Per-request token→USD in the `token_audit` DB1 table (`src/db1/token_audit.c`, `src/server/token_tracker.c`): multi-source pricing (static table → registry/models.dev → authoritative DB1 `model_pricing`), attributed by model/source/role/tool/session/principal/delegation with parent cost-fold. Read surface exists: `GET /v1/insights/overview`, `/v1/dashboard/*`, React `CostPanel`. **Missing only the per-team/project dimension.**\n- **Credential vault — encrypted at rest**, keyed by attested principal (`src/server/vault_service.c`, `src/headers/vault_principal.h`).\n- **OIDC/JWT verifier — real** (RS256/JWKS, alg-pinned), in aimee-kb and kb-console (`src/kb/auth_oidc.c`, `kb-console/auth.go`) — opt-in via env today.\n- **PKI + mTLS enrollment CA** (`src/kb/enroll.c`, `src/kb/pki.c`, `src/server/kb_client_mtls.c`) — `aimee://` single-use tokens, `cert:CN` principals. Reusable for enrolling servers.\n- **Canonical IR + provider drivers** (`src/headers/aimee_ir.h`, `src/server/delegate_driver.c`, `aimee-universal-gateway.md`, done) — Anthropic / OpenAI-Chat / Responses / Gemini wire adapters through a protocol-neutral pivot. This is the egress machinery kb needs.\n- **Keyless roster + attested credential handling already exist** — the shipped `deploy/container/agents.json` ships no keys. The old client-push `POST /v1/session/credentials` was retired; provider secrets now live in the server vault (`/v1/vault/*`), and vault writes require an attested transport (UDS or confidential TLS+bearer — never plaintext TCP; `server_cert.c:18-22`, `server_http_identity.c:113-123`). The org-egress work reuses this attested-transport discipline rather than inventing a new one — org keys simply never leave kb in the first place.\n\nAbsent (the actual gaps, one sub-proposal each): a team/project entity; per-team/project cost attribution; per-team budgets and per-key rate limits (spend is tracked but never capped; the rate limiter is a single global bucket); OIDC on the aimee-server data plane + a kb→server control plane; and AWS Bedrock.","doc_id":"dda697a78df9eb34862d936f","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23030:{"content":"## Separate TLS trust domain\n\nAdd a process-owned management `SSL_CTX` in `server_tls`, with a context-selecting accept helper and\n`server_tls_management_begin`. The management context always requires a client certificate,\nenforces TLS 1.2 or newer and client-auth chain/time/purpose verification against its dedicated CA,\nand uses the configured management server leaf/key. A separate management context builder has no\ngeneric DB1 roster callback parameter or registration call by construction: management leaves are\nprimary-issued and their online next-request authority is the B3 nonce/staple protocol. A focused\ntest marks the same leaf revoked in the generic roster and proves this TLS context still performs\nonly CA/time/EKU verification while application status revocation remains fail-closed. The data\ncontext and optional→required ramp are unchanged.\n\nThe context is published only after it is completely built and remains process-lifetime owned\nbecause detached HTTP workers are not joined by current server shutdown. Once published it is\nnever freed or replaced before process exit; each `SSL_new` also holds its OpenSSL reference.\nStart failure before publication frees the private candidate. Same-process HTTP restart may reuse\nonly a byte-identical cert/key/CA configuration packet; any difference is a fatal start while the\npublished context remains untouched. Live `SSL` objects share the existing\nregistered-connection shutdown. Management TLS reload is explicitly restart-required; data\nSIGHUP never replaces or frees the management context.\n\n“Byte-identical” is a stored SHA-256 tuple over the bounded raw PEM bytes in fixed\n`certificate || private-key || client-CA` order, read through no-follow regular-file descriptors\nat context build time. On a later start, all three hashes must match before reuse; mismatch returns\n`SERVER_HTTP_START_MGMT_FATAL`, never swaps the context, and never rebinds a listener. Bind/port\nare separately revalidated but are not part of the TLS-context tuple.","doc_id":"dea338eada6c6edb7c3caf94","doc_kind":""}

It runs **both** aimee binaries as separate services: `aimee-kb` serving\n`/v1` on `:8741`, and the server fronting `/v1` over TLS on `:8743` (plaintext\n`:8740` is loopback-only) with `AIMEE_KB_API_URL=http://aimee-kb:8741`, so server\nand kb communicate over the internal network. The `aimee-llm` service provides the\nsynthesis and curator gateway; to run a standalone llama.cpp curator LLM instead,\nadd `--profile curator-llm` (works on `compose.server.yaml` and `compose.yaml`).\nEach container runs as a\nnon-root user; the kb uses Python sidecars (`scripts/embed-remote.py`,\n`llm-chat.py`, `curator-extract.py`, `learning-synthesize.py`) for embeddings,\nsynthesis, and curation, with container defaults from `deploy/container/aimee.yaml`.\n\n**Container lifecycle**: the binaries run as long-lived container processes\n(PID 1), supervised by Docker's restart policy, not systemd/launchd:\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml ps           # container + health status\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml logs -f      # follow logs (add a service to scope)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml restart aimee-server aimee-kb\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down         # stop + remove containers (volumes persist)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml down -v      # also DROP data volumes (destroys DB2 + state)\ndocker compose -f compose.server.yaml up -d --build # update: rebuild images, recreate containers\n```\n\n**State and volumes.** Durable data lives in named volumes, not the container\nfilesystem, so recreate is safe and only `down -v` erases it: `*-postgres` holds\nDB2 (`aimee_shared`); `*-home` (`/var/lib/aimee`) holds server/kb runtime state\n(DB1 SQLite + config); `*-workspaces` (`/var/lib/aimee-workspaces`,","doc_id":"dece3672c42a51c44cf9be0d","doc_kind":""}

Until a Go runner\nimplements every production block, the Go control plane may call an isolated\ncompatibility worker over the typed runner protocol. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23233:{"content":"## Design: on-demand threads + high safety ceiling\n\nEach sessionless delegate runs on **its own detached thread**, spawned on\ndemand and reaped on completion (`delegate_spawn_ondemand` in\n`server_compute.c`). No fixed pool; no compute-budget gate. Throttling is the\nper-model limiter. A configurable **backstop ceiling** (`delegate_max_inflight`,\ndefault **512**, env `AIMEE_DELEGATE_MAX_INFLIGHT`) prevents a pathological\nfan-out from exhausting fds/memory — \"effectively unlimited\" for any real\nworkload, but not literally unbounded.\n\nMechanics:\n- An atomic-by-mutex in-flight counter; spawn rejects (`-1`, job marked failed)\n  only at the ceiling — unreachable under the per-model limiter in normal use.\n- Detached threads carry the same 32 MB stack as compute-pool workers (the\n  agent loop has deep frames).\n- The compute **budget is bypassed** exactly as session delegates already do:\n  a positive `compute_executor_threads` grant makes `compute_ctx_begin_budget`\n  take its non-blocking path (verified: `compute_ctx_release_budget` then never\n  touches the global budget). This is the *second* 2-wide gate, also removed for\n  delegates.\n- **Shutdown:** `delegate_ondemand_drain(5000)` gives in-flight delegates a\n  bounded window. On-demand delegates bypass the budget (never touch\n  `compute_budget_mutex`) and own no socket (no `conns_mutex`); a straggler past\n  the window only touches DB1 + its own ctx, so teardown is safe.\n- **Observability:** `aimee workers` no longer shows delegates as pool slots\n  (they aren't pooled), so a `delegates_inflight` gauge is added to the workers\n  response. `compute_pool_set_job` is a safe no-op off a pool thread.","doc_id":"e0be27e9db8880d88a1f850a","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23236:{"content":"## `check_tier_deps.sh`, enforce DB1/DB2 tier boundaries\n\nValidates dependency boundaries for the two-database architecture (DB1 = local\nSQLite owned by `aimee-server`; DB2 = shared Postgres owned by `aimee-kb`,\nincluding the in-process pgvector extension):\n\n- `sqlite3.h` only in `src/db1/`\n- `libpq-fe.h` only in `src/db2/`\n- `aimee_stores_` / `aimee_stores_t` / `PGconn` / `PGresult` / `PQ*` helper symbols / `sqlite3_` only in tier-owned source trees\n- no legacy `project_store_` lifecycle aliases outside `src/db2`\n- no legacy DB2 backend selector outside `src/db2`\n- DB2 transitional SQLite lifecycle names stay inside `src/db2`\n- DB2 public lifecycle headers hide SQLite backend knowledge\n- DB2 public lifecycle headers hide shim backend vocabulary\n- DB2 shared-store lifecycle APIs expose neutral names outside `src/db2`\n- DB2 transaction primitives stay inside `src/db2`\n- Legacy/helper vocabulary outside `src/db1` avoids SQLite names\n- Worker-shell comments outside `src/db1` avoid SQLite names\n- Vector verify row-count fields expose DB2 names instead of SQLite names\n- Doctor DB output exposes DB2 names instead of Postgres names\n- Non-DB2 source comments avoid Postgres/libpq implementation names\n- No Qdrant HTTP collection/points URL paths in `src/` (vector store is now\n  pgvector inside DB2, in-process, no HTTP sidecar)\n\nMost checks scan `src/**/*.c`, `src/**/*.h`, and `src/**/*.inc` outside\n`src/db1`, `src/db2`, `src/tests`, and `src/webchat`.\n\nRun manually:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/check_tier_deps.sh\n```\n\nThe `lint` CI job also runs this check.\n\nBinary ownership is checked by `cd src && make check-linking`; that target\nverifies the process boundary:\n\n- `aimee-client` and `aimee-webchat` stay DB-free (`libsqlite3` and `libpq` absent).\n- `aimee-server` stays DB1-only (`libsqlite3` present, `libpq` absent, no\n  DB2 symbols).\n- `aimee-kb` stays DB2-only (`libpq` present, `libsqlite3` absent, no\n  DB1/sqlite symbols).","doc_id":"e0c2cb3d4fd7077e611b08df","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:23807:{"content":"## Server Architecture\n\nThe shipped artifacts are four binaries: `aimee`, `aimee-webchat`, `aimee-server`, and `aimee-kb`. Common runtime code and git MCP handlers are linked directly into the binaries that need them instead of being shipped as separate executables or shared libraries. Long-running work uses `aimee-server`'s in-process compute pool; there is no separate worker binary.\n\n| Binary | Libraries | External deps |\n|--------|-----------|---------------|\n| `aimee` | Thin CLI transport + MCP stdio bridge | pthread |\n| `aimee-webchat` | DB-free webchat launcher; talks only to `aimee-server` through `webchat.serve` | pthread |\n| `aimee-server` | Local DB1 daemon, agent/runtime orchestration, KB RPC client | sqlite3, ssl, crypto, pam |\n| `aimee-kb` | Local-or-shared DB2 RPC service + memory/KB pipeline (incl. pgvector) | libpq, ssl, crypto |\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart TD\n    CLI[aimee\\nCLI + MCP stdio] -->|JSON RPC| SRV[aimee-server\\nDB1 + compute pool]\n    WEB[aimee-webchat\\nbrowser-facing client] -->|JSON RPC| SRV\n    SRV -->|typed KB /v1 HTTP| KB[aimee-kb\\nDB2 + pgvector]\n    SRV --> DB1[src/db1/*]\n    KB --> DB2[src/db2/*]\n```","doc_id":"e64e4ac0ea5c533fa635c6bb","doc_kind":""}

DB1 stores refs,\n  manifests, hashes, and compact digests; working files/blobs, db2 `docs`, or an\n  explicit artifact payload carry the large origin content. `kb_documents` remains\n  a chunk index, not the canonical whole-origin store.\n- Expecting DRAFT mode to emit a complete proposal (#9). The 8 KB artifact cap\n  means DRAFT produces a skeleton; the author-revise loop expands it in the working\n  file. Generating long-form text inside the roundtable artifact is out of scope.\n- A fully autonomous, gate-less pipeline — the two human gates are mandatory by\n  design; \"configurable max passes\" bounds cost, it does not remove the human. Three compose files ship, built from two images: `aimee-server`\n(`Dockerfile.server`) and `aimee-kb` (`Dockerfile`). Every stack also brings up a\n`pgvector/pgvector:pg16` Postgres, and the kb auto-applies its DB2 schema\n(`pg_trgm` and `vector` extensions plus tables) on first boot. The stacks run the\n`aimee-llm` inference gateway (embeddings, reranking, and synthesis) as a service,\nwhich downloads its cpu-tier models on first boot, so embedding and reranking work\nwith nothing external. The tier is chosen by `AIMEE_LLM_TIER`: `cpu` serves\nQwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 1024 dims; the GPU tiers (`small` 16 GB, `mid` 24 GB,\n`large` 32 GB) serve Qwen3-Embedding-4B at 2560 dims.\nTo run a standalone embedder or curator LLM instead, use\nthe `curator-llm` compose profile. Backends and tiers:\n[KB_LLM_BACKENDS.md](docs/KB_LLM_BACKENDS.md) and\n[AIMEE_KB_SYNTH_TIERS.md](docs/AIMEE_KB_SYNTH_TIERS.md).\n\n| Compose file | Brings up | Use when |\n|--------------|-----------|----------|\n| `compose.server-managed.yaml` | `aimee-server` only; the wizard's Deploy step then launches `aimee-kb` + `aimee-llm` + Postgres via the mounted Docker socket | **Recommended default.** One container to deploy; the browser wizard brings up the rest. |\n| `compose.server.yaml` | `aimee-server` + `aimee-kb` + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway | Advanced: the full split stack brought up together, no socket mount. Scale/update/place server and kb independently. |\n| `compose.yaml` | `aimee-kb` + Postgres + the `aimee-llm` inference gateway | The knowledge service alone: building block for a shared/scaled kb. |\n| `compose.server-standalone.yaml` | `aimee-server` only (SQLite DB1, no kb) | DB1-backed `/v1` with no shared knowledge. |\n\n**Bring up the self-deploying server:**\n\n```bash\ndocker compose -f compose.server-managed.yaml up -d","doc_id":"ea04c8642b1328958f1f0d31","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:24169:{"content":"### 3.2 State machine\n\n```text\n                 ┌──────────────→ INVALID\n                 │\nOPEN ────────────┼──→ ABORTED\n  │              │\n  ├── crash ─→ RECOVERABLE_OPEN ─→ SEALED_INCOMPLETE\n  │\n  └────────────→ SEALED ─→ RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS ─→ RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING ─→ RESTORED\n                       │             │\n                       │             └──────────→ RESTORE_INCIDENT\n                       └────────────────────────→ EXPIRED\n```\n\n- `OPEN`: accepts immutable preimages and append-only operation evidence.\n- `ABORTED`: no completed native mutation was observed. Terminal and not restorable;\n  blob refs are released.\n- `INVALID`: capture, coverage, identity, evidence, or integrity failure. Terminal and\n  never shown as safe.\n- `RECOVERABLE_OPEN`: startup/doctor classification only; no automatic restore.\n- `SEALED_INCOMPLETE`: an interrupted turn with fully verifiable mutated entries. It may\n  be previewed but restore remains an explicit operator action.\n- `SEALED`: immutable manifest and final postimages exist.\n- `RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS`: durable restore journal written before the first filesystem\n  mutation.\n- `RESTORED_AUDIT_PENDING`: filesystem and DB1 operational state committed, but the\n  separate audit sink has not yet acknowledged the terminal event. Doctor retries the\n  bounded event; this state is never reported as fully complete.\n- `RESTORED`: requested entries and audit outcome committed.\n- `RESTORE_INCIDENT`: apply or compensation could not converge automatically. The\n  worktree is write-frozen at `mutation_begin` until operator acknowledgement.\n- `EXPIRED`: manifest retained; one or more required blobs were policy-pruned.\n\nNo state transition makes a sealed manifest mutable. A later restore attempt receives a\nnew restore-run id and journal.","doc_id":"ea1314bbd7f0f00dfd909a3f","doc_kind":""}

A test asserts this explicitly, so the liveness contract\n   and the kb symmetry cannot regress.\n3. **Red before green.** A test harness starts the server with an injected\n   failing dependency and asserts `/v1/ready` reports non-ok and status 503.\n   The same harness, run against a build where the readiness provider is\n   replaced by one that unconditionally reports ok, must **fail** — proving the\n   test detects blindness rather than merely observing a hardcoded string. (The\n   original draft asked the test to fail against the stock endpoint; that was\n   unachievable, since the stock build has no `/v1/ready` to point it at. This\n   is the corrected formulation.)\n4. Before the first sample completes, `/v1/ready` reports `unknown` and 503.\n   A test asserts this startup behavior.\n5. A snapshot older than the staleness bound degrades to `unknown`/503. A test\n   asserts a wedged refresher does not report ready indefinitely.\n6. A dependency probe exceeding its timeout is reported `fail`/`timeout`, and a\n   test asserts the handler's own latency stays bounded and independent of that\n   probe's duration — i.e. the request path did no I/O.\n7. `server_http.c`'s existing unit test gains no new dependency linkage. With no\n   provider registered, `/v1/ready` reports `unknown`/503.\n8. The route, its schema, and the 200-vs-503 boundary are added to the OpenAPI\n   surface, and generated docs regenerate cleanly.","doc_id":"ed6507fe9ffb5fb0cbc7b882","doc_kind":""}

Complete WFE block runners, roundtables, Git forge operations, worktree\n   isolation, and provider routing in Go.\n2. Shadow-read current DB1 and compare API responses; stop the C scheduler, then\n   transfer the workflow tables to the Go writer in one cutover.\n3. Move the remaining DB1 API families and session/auth control plane to Go one\n   family at a time, maintaining one writer per family.\n4. Move delegate/provider execution, vault and policy enforcement into isolated\n   Go services. Preserve durable admission-before-dispatch semantics.\n5. Rewrite the KB service and DB2 ownership in Go, retaining typed HTTP boundaries.\n6. Replace thin-client and gateway behavior where needed. Delete compatibility\n   adapters once no deployed client depends on them.\n7. Remove C build/runtime dependencies from production images. It owns DB1, runs the compute pool, routes delegates,\nserves hooks, and exposes both the internal RPC protocol and the public HTTP /v1\nAPI.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TD\n    L[\"Listen sockets<br/>aimee-http.sock (HTTP /v1) + optional localhost TCP\"]\n    EV[\"HTTP listener<br/>(accept loop hands each connection to its own worker thread)\"]\n    AUTH[\"Auth gate<br/>local UDS = filesystem-trusted (full surface)<br/>TCP = bearer-scoped + 16 capability flags\"]\n    POOL[\"Bounded compute pool<br/>(delegate exec, chat, tool calls)\"]\n    DB1[(\"DB1 SQLite\")]\n    KBC[\"KB client<br/>typed RPC to aimee-kb\"]\n    PROV[\"Delegate HTTP client<br/>libcurl\"]\n\n    L --> EV --> AUTH\n    AUTH -->|fast handlers| DB1\n    AUTH -->|blocking handlers| POOL\n    POOL --> DB1\n    POOL --> KBC\n    POOL --> PROV\n```\n\nKey properties:\n\n- **Per-connection workers, bounded compute pool.** The HTTP accept loop hands\n  each connection to its own detached worker thread, so a slow or streaming\n  request never blocks the listener and independent `/v1` requests run\n  concurrently. Heavyweight handlers (DB query, network, subprocess, delegate\n  inference) additionally run on a bounded compute pool; a compute budget gate\n  serializes heavyweight inference to bound resource use.\n- **Transport.** Clients reach the server over its `/v1` HTTP surface: the\n  always-on `~/.config/aimee/aimee-http.sock` Unix socket, plus an optional\n  localhost TCP listener. Dispatch methods use dedicated `/v1` routes; the\n  generic `POST /v1/rpc` endpoint is retired. Streaming chat uses\n  `POST /v1/chat/stream`, whose body is a sequence of newline-delimited aimee\n  events terminated by a final status object. (The legacy newline-delimited\n  JSON-RPC socket was removed.)\n- **Authentication.** The local UDS is filesystem-permission gated and fully\n  trusted: it reaches the entire dispatch surface, with no token. The optional\n  TCP listener requires a configured bearer token and is capability-scoped.","doc_id":"ee8788f3fc16ef5a146bad5e","doc_kind":""}

DB1 holds the canonical memory. The on-disk\n`memory/*.md` files are a rendered cache that aimee rebuilds — DB1 wins on any conflict.\n\n**Threat model — be honest about what is and isn't intercepted (R3 #2).** We do **not**\nclaim \"every mutation path is intercepted.\" We intercept exactly **agent-tool-mediated**\nwrites/deletes (the seam fires only on tool calls — §0). Writes that bypass the tool layer\nentirely — a human in `vim`, IDE autosave, a sync client (Dropbox/Syncthing), a container\nvolume mount, `python -c 'open(...).write()'` via `Bash`, or an agent **not** installed\nwith an `AIMEE_HOOK_CLIENT` hook — are **not** captured at write time. They are caught by a\n**session-start content-hash audit** (§5) that compares every on-disk file against its DB1\nrow and, per the deterministic reconcile policy, makes disk match DB1 (or imports\ndisk-only files). So the precise invariant is:\n\n- **Agent-tool writes** → intercepted (§3): denied, canonicalized into DB1, re-materialized.\n- **Agent-tool deletes** → intercepted (§3): tombstoned in DB1 (per-file *and* bulk/dir, §3).\n- **Non-tool / external changes** → **not prevented**, reconciled to DB1 at session-start\n  (§5) with the divergence surfaced in the audit log (§7). DB1 is authoritative; an external\n  edit does not silently become the source of truth.\n- aimee's **own** re-materialize writes use direct filesystem syscalls in the server/CLI\n  process and therefore **cannot** re-enter a PreToolUse hook (hooks fire only on *agent\n  tool calls*, not on aimee's own process I/O). This makes the no-loop property\n  **structural**, not flag-based (R1 #2, #23); a test exercises aimee's writer with the\n  hook installed to prove it.\n\nAccepted scope: **single host.** DB1 is local SQLite, so \"shared across all agents/\nsessions\" means *on this machine*. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25155:{"content":"### 6.2 Blob store\n\nPreimage bytes move out of unbounded inline SQLite blobs into a DB1-owned store beneath\n`$AIMEE_HOME/rewind/blobs`, following Aimee's existing content-addressed-store durability\npattern:\n\n- per-principal namespace; no cross-principal deduplication or equality oracle;\n- SHA-256 content identity, opaque refs at external surfaces;\n- `0700` directories, `0600` regular files, `O_NOFOLLOW`;\n- unique temp write → file `fsync` → atomic rename → directory `fsync`;\n- DB ref committed only after the blob is durable;\n- blobs with an active `rewind_blob_refs` edge are never deleted;\n- oldest eligible sealed sets expire under both count and byte ceilings;\n- manifest/audit rows survive blob expiry.\n\nExpiry is ordered: compare-and-swap the set from restore-eligible to `EXPIRED`, remove its\nactive ref edges in the same DB1 transaction, then let asynchronous GC delete now-unreferenced\nblob files after a grace period. A preimage row is never rewritten merely because its\nretained bytes expired.\n\nGarbage collection is bounded and asynchronous. If it cannot make space, protected\ncapture blocks before mutation with `store_budget_exhausted`; it does not delete a live\nref or silently degrade to partial coverage.","doc_id":"f33c1921048dcd99274cd8d4","doc_kind":""}
/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25172:{"content":"## Scope (P3a only)\n\n1. **DB2 `org_model_pricing`** — Postgres-authoritative, versioned price table:\n   `(id, provider, model, input_usd_per_mtok, output_usd_per_mtok,\n   cache_read_usd_per_mtok, version, effective_at, created_at)`, unique\n   `(model, version)`. A per-model `current_version` pointer table\n   `org_model_pricing_current(model, version)` advanced **atomically** on a price\n   change (new row + pointer update in one txn) — a price change is a NEW row, never\n   an in-place mutate, so every stateless kb instance agrees on `(model, version)`.\n   Seeded by promoting the existing static/registry/DB1 `model_pricing` prices.\n2. **DB2 `org_token_audit`** — per-request org cost ledger: `(id, request_id,\n   origin_cert_cn, actor_issuer, actor_subject, team_id, project_id, model,\n   served_model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cache_read_tokens,\n   estimated_cost_usd, pricing_version, state, created_at, settled_at)`. Idempotency\n   key **unique `(origin_cert_cn, request_id)`** (a bare request_id can replay across\n   mutually-untrusted origins). `pricing_version` is a **FK to\n   `org_model_pricing(model, version)`** (settlement references the exact immutable\n   row). Lifecycle `state ∈ {started, settled_success, settled_denied,\n   settled_failed, indeterminate}`.\n3. **`(team, project, model, day)` rollup table** — `org_spend_rollup`, maintained\n   incrementally (P3b writes it; P3a defines the table + the upsert contends only\n   per-key).\n4. **RLS (invariant #10):** all three are tenant tables — `FORCE ROW LEVEL\n   SECURITY`, membership-bound read policies keyed on `team_id ∈ principal's teams`\n   (reuse the P1 `set_tenant_context`/`aimee.principal` pattern), admin/team-lead\n   write via P3b. `org_model_pricing` is org-global read (all authenticated), admin\n   write.\n5. **Typed db2 modules:** `src/db2/org_pricing.{h,c}` (get_current_price(model) →\n   pins version; add_price_version; seed), `src/db2/org_token_audit.{h,c}`\n   (insert_started, settle, get by key), each guarded by `db2_tenant_require_pg()`.","doc_id":"f35acf7e26b35c3e1e7c4e89","doc_kind":""}

Registration and\nunregistration occur only while the HTTP listener is stopped. Dispatch borrows the handler under\nthe seam mutex, increments its in-flight count, releases the mutex for the full network call, and\ndecrements/signals on return; unregister first blocks new borrows and waits on a condition\nvariable without holding runtime/lifecycle/DB locks. The production runtime is its only owner;\ntests may inject a handler before requests begin. For exactly\n`GET /v1/servers/{id}/health`, parse the existing positive `team` parameter, require\n`kb_reqctx_actor()` to be authenticated, and invoke the registered live handler. Do not perform\nthe old direct `db2_server_registry_get()` heartbeat read and do not manufacture an owner in\nauth-off mode.\n\nMap typed B3a results without string inspection: `OK→200`, `NOT_FOUND→404`, `DENIED→403`,\n`CONFLICT→409`, `UNAVAILABLE→503`, `INTEGRITY→502`, `INVALID→400`. Build bounded exact JSON and\nescape no dependency-controlled prose. Method mismatches remain 405. The registration seam is\nconsulted only by this exact health path; `/v1/servers` list behavior and all other routes remain\non their existing direct paths, with a regression test proving the list callback cardinality is\nzero.\n\nOn aimee-server, add a pure predicate for the dedicated management transport. It returns true\nonly for the exact two method/path pairs above and a TLS peer whose already chain-verified leaf\nhas the management profile and exact management-client CN. In `handle_conn`, evaluate this after\n`server_tls_peer_identity()` plus `server_tls_peer_cert()` have extracted the verified leaf and\nimmediately before the generic DB1 `pki_cert_check`, required-mTLS ramp accounting, transport,\nbearer, bootstrap-bearer, and capability gates. The classifier is three-way: `NOT_MANAGEMENT`,","doc_id":"f4c53bdd01bdcc0570b299bd","doc_kind":""}

/tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:25527:{"content":"## The KB split\n\n`aimee-server` owns no DB2 SQL. It reaches DB2 through the **KB client**\n(`src/modules/kb_client/kb_client*.c`), typed wrappers (memory, index, docs, agent,\ndashboard, roadmap, notes, curiosity, status) that call `aimee-kb` over its\nHTTP `/v1` API (`AIMEE_KB_API_URL`, port 8741). The legacy Unix-socket transport\nwas retired in #2747; HTTP is now the only KB transport. DB1 remains local to the server;\nDB2 can be a local single-user KB or a shared KB, and server-side reflection or\npromotion flows send only scoped knowledge artifacts across that boundary.\n`aimee-kb` (`src/kb/`) owns the DB2 schema, the memory inference pipeline, the\nvector collections, the code index, document ingest, and the curator. It exposes\n43 HTTP /v1 endpoints\n(`/v1/code/*`, `/v1/docs/*`, `/v1/search`, `/v1/ingest/*`, `/v1/entities/*`,\n`/v1/reflections/*`, `/v1/maintenance/*`, `/v1/releases/*`), see\n`api/openapi-v1.yaml`. The server no longer auto-starts the KB: `AIMEE_KB_API_URL`\nmust point at an already-running `aimee-kb` (started by its service unit, container,\nor `aimee-kb --http-port`). `AIMEE_KB_NO_AUTOSTART` is now a deprecated no-op.","doc_id":"f6d89caab2ea853df7169a1d","doc_kind":""}

Revocations are rare; a flat\n * growable array consulted under the mutex is plenty and keeps the TLS verify\n * callback off the database. */\nstatic char **g_revoked = NULL;\nstatic int g_revoked_n = 0, g_revoked_cap = 0;\n\nvoid pki_reset_for_test(void)\n{\n   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_mu);\n   if (g_ca_key)\n      EVP_PKEY_free(g_ca_key);\n   if (g_ca_cert)\n      X509_free(g_ca_cert);\n   g_ca_key = NULL;\n   g_ca_cert = NULL;\n   for (int i = 0; i < g_revoked_n; i++)\n      free(g_revoked[i]);\n   free(g_revoked);\n   g_revoked = NULL;\n   g_revoked_n = g_revoked_cap = 0;\n   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_mu);\n}\n\nstatic void ca_cert_path(char *out, size_t n)\n{\n   snprintf(out, n, \"%s/tls/client-ca.crt\", config_default_dir());\n}\n\n/* --- DB1 (caller holds no lock; sqlite is serialized) --- */\nstatic void db_ensure_tables(void)\n{\n   sqlite3 *db = db1_conn();\n   if (db)\n      sqlite3_exec(db,\n                   \"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pki_certs(serial TEXT PRIMARY KEY, cn TEXT NOT NULL,\"\n                   \" issued_at INTEGER, expires_at INTEGER, revoked INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)\",\n                   NULL, NULL, NULL);\n}\n\nstatic int ramp_tables_ensure(s","doc_id":"f7548c8ca163289d7c3eaf4d","doc_kind":"code_unit_body"}

Nothing extra to install; this is what a fresh\n  `install.sh` gives you.\n- **pgvectorscale (StreamingDiskANN) is the opt-in scale-up** for large corpora.\n  It is *additive*: built on top of pgvector, it reuses the same `vector` column\n  type and distance operators and only adds the `USING diskann` index, disk-backed\n  with bounded build memory, for the large/RAM-constrained regime where HNSW's\n  in-memory graph becomes the bottleneck. Select it per corpus table:\n\n  ```yaml\n  db2:\n    vector:\n      corpus_index: auto          # auto | hnsw | diskann\n      corpus_diskann_threshold: 1000000   # rows/table before \"auto\" picks diskann\n  ```\n\n  `auto` uses HNSW until a corpus table exceeds the threshold *and* the\n  `vectorscale` extension is installed, then picks diskann; it falls back to HNSW\n  with a notice when the extension is absent (so schema apply never hard-fails).\n  Memory/hot-path vectors stay HNSW unconditionally.\n- **Switching index type is a reindex, not a migration.** Data and queries are\n  identical across HNSW and diskann; `aimee kb repair --reindex-corpus` rebuilds\n  corpus indexes to the configured/`auto` type with no re-embedding and no query\n  rewrite. /tmp/aimee-large-repo-roi-npjshscr/large-repo-b86d77d2cdd1431b/benchmarks/fixtures/gemma4-unified/ab-v1/corpus.jsonl:26134:{"content":"## Durable local replay consume\n\nAdd a DB1-owned `db1/server_management_jti.{c,h}` module and schema table dedicated to management\ntoken consumption, not a server TU reaching through `db1_internal.h` and not a generic idempotency\nstore:\n\n`server_management_jti(jti TEXT PRIMARY KEY, issuer, kid, audience, subject, team_id,\ncapability, peer_issuer, peer_serial, peer_fingerprint, request_sha256, correlation_id,\nissued_at, expires_at, consumed_at)`.\n\nSchema `CHECK`s mirror every application bound: jti 16..128, issuer 1..255, kid 1..64,\naudience 1..127, subject 1..576, positive team id, capability 1..64, peer issuer 1..511,\npeer serial 1..79 lowercase hex, both SHA-256 fields exactly 64 lowercase hex, correlation id\n1..128, and integer times with `0 <= issued_at < expires_at`. The application uses a compiled live\nrow ceiling of 4096; because the table can never exceed that ceiling, deletion of all expired rows\ninside the transaction is itself bounded. Index `(expires_at,jti)`. A single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`\ntransaction:\n\n1. deletes rows whose `expires_at` is strictly before the current time;\n2. checks a compiled live-row ceiling before insert;\n3. inserts the fully verified claim tuple with the current consume time; and\n4. commits before reporting success.\n\nThe unique insert is the authorization point. Constraint conflict means replay; saturation,\nbusy/locked DB, schema error, clock error, or commit ambiguity is unavailable/deny, never success.\nThe row is not deleted on downstream failure: C1a has no dispatch, and later packets must treat an\naccepted token as consumed before any action attempt. Persistence across process restart is\nmandatory. Expiry GC is bounded and indexed; tests use injected time and capacity rather than\nsleep. The existing DB1 transaction gate serializes in-process writers; external `SQLITE_BUSY`\ndoes not spin or sleep and fails unavailable. The promised crash boundary is process crash/restart,\nnot arbitrary power-loss durability: later dispatch occurs only after COMMIT returns success. They are not user-selectable runtime\nbackends.\n\n| Tier | Ownership | Contents |\n|------|-----------|----------|\n| DB1 | `src/db1/` | Local user and session information, credentials, checkpoints, multi-agent ensembles, local caches, local interaction/learning signals, and other same-user state. Backed by SQLite, owned by the local `aimee-server`. |\n| DB2 | `src/db2/` | Durable knowledge for the configured KB scope: memories, rules, KB metadata, task and decision records, code index metadata, coordination records, and the dense vector indexes for that knowledge (pgvector extension, in-process). Backed by Postgres, owned by `aimee-kb`, and deployable as either a local single-user KB or a shared KB. |\n\nCode outside a tier must call typed APIs instead of depending on a tier's\nstorage handles or provider vocabulary. The tier-boundary check in\n`scripts/check_tier_deps.sh` enforces the public surface that has been cleaned\nup so far.\n\nOperationally, DB1 is local to the user profile and belongs to one\n`aimee-server` process. It is where private runtime state and local evidence are\ncaptured first. DB2 is the durable knowledge source for project, workspace, and\nglobal facts plus their dense embeddings; it may be local to the same machine or\nshared by multiple servers. Shared deployments should receive only information\nappropriate for that shared scope, through the memory, learning, reflection, and\nKB APIs that promote or reflect local server evidence into durable knowledge.\n\nThe vector tier was originally a separate Qdrant sidecar; it was folded\ninto DB2 as a pgvector extension in #1575, vectors live in the same Postgres\ninstance as the rest of DB2 and need no separate connection or service.","doc_id":"fe8cf4da722fcdaac0584fe3","doc_kind":""}
